I therefore release from every exaction all who wish to bring grain, barley, beans, lentils, and chickpeas through the gates of Jerusalem [Note: supplied from B]; and both Saracens and Christians shall have free power to enter and leave [Note: supplied from B] and to sell wherever and to whomever they wish, without molestation.

Therefore I beseech and charge my successors and heirs not to presume in any way to violate or alter the terms of this ordinance. I also ask the lord patriarch and all the Jerusalemite clergy not to delay promulgating a sentence of excommunication against any person who, if perhaps instigated by greed or deceived by the devil, should attempt to violate it.

I also remit the customary payment for a measure [Note: B, “I remit”].

This was done in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1120, indiction 13, and confirmed in the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre by the testimony of suitable men whose names are subscribed:

I, Guarmund, by the grace of God patriarch of Jerusalem, have subscribed, and at the request of Lord Baldwin the king I have excommunicated those who violate this gift.

The sign of Ebremar, archbishop of Caesarea. The sign of Anschetinus, bishop of Bethlehem. The sign of Bernard, bishop of Nazareth. [The sign] of Roger, bishop of Ramla. [The sign] of Gelduin, abbot of the Valley of Jehoshaphat. [The sign] of Richard, abbot of Latrun. [The sign] of Gerard, prior of the Holy Sepulchre. [The sign] of Achard, prior of the Temple of the Lord. [The sign] of Arnald, prior of Mount Zion [Note: B, “prior of Mount Zion”]. [The sign] of Laurence, prior of Mount Olivet. [The sign] of Peter of Barcelona. [The sign] of Paganus, chancellor. [The sign] of Brandon. [The sign] of Hugh Caulis, constable. [The sign] of William of Tiberias [Note: B, Tyberiade]. [The sign] of Eustace Granarius. [The sign] of Herbert Pisellus. [The sign] of Ralph of Fontanellis. [The sign] of Guy of Milly. [The sign] of Balian. [The sign] of Romanus of Podio. [The sign] of Amalric of Flandrello. [The sign] of Baldwin of Saint Abraham. [The sign] of Manasses of Cayphas. [The sign] of Roardus. [The sign] of Anschetinus, the viscount. [The sign] of Paganus, the cupbearer. [The sign] of John, the chamberlain. [The sign] of Rainald of Pont. [The sign] of Geoffrey Acus. [The sign] of Porcellus. [The sign] of Bertinus. [The signs] of Bachelor and William Strabo.

I, Baldwin, by the grace of God second Latin king of Jerusalem, have subscribed and signed by the impression of my seal, in the third year of my reign.

## XLVI. PRIVILEGE OF KING BALDWIN II CONCERNING THE CUSTOM OF THE PORT OF ACRE

[Note: Column 1135: A, folio 42 recto; B, folio 37 verso.]  
[Note: In B this word is replaced by *Item*.]  
[Note: B reads *Achonensis*.]

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

I, Baldwin, by the grace of God second Latin king of Jerusalem [Note: B reads *Iherusalem*.], because certain evil customs had arisen in the port of Acre which greatly burdened pilgrims, at the request and admonition of the lord Stephen, venerable patriarch of Jerusalem, decreed, for the sake of the soul of my predecessor, Baldwin, king of blessed memory [Note: B reads “Baldwin, of blessed memory, king.”], and of my queen and wife, that pilgrims coming from wherever they might come should pay no census-duty in the port on any of the goods they had brought, whether cut and sewn cloth for clothing [Note: B reads *consutis*, “sewn.”].

Nor shall they pay anything on any other goods they may have brought with them, up to the value of forty bezants. Whatever in the pilgrims’ goods exceeds this value of forty bezants, if the pilgrims can bind themselves by oath to the port officials that they will reserve whatever it may be for their own use, they shall remain exempt. But if necessity compels them to sell that surplus, they shall pay from the sale whatever the custom and justice of the port require [Note: B reads *quicquid*, “whatever.”].

## XLVII. PRIVILEGE OF POPE INNOCENT

(See under Innocent II, for the year 1143.)

## XLVIII. CONCERNING THE REMISSION OF THE CLAIM WHICH QUEEN MELISENDE HAD MADE AGAINST THE VILLEINS OF BETHSURIE, THE SYRIANS OF CALANDRIA AND RAMETHES, AND THE VINEYARD OF LADY GELTIDIS

[Note: Column 1135: A, folio 43 recto; B, folio 44 verso.]  
[Note: In B the heading begins with these words: “Also, of Queen Melisende, concerning …”]  
[Note: B reads *Rametis*.]  
[Note: B reads *vineam*, “the vineyard.”]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

The rule of the ancient institution, which was once established in former times, was not negligently maintained; and the venerable tradition of the holy fathers likewise suitably observed it and beneficially transmitted it to us for observance through their succeeding examples: whenever the sequence of any deed is set down, lest it should likewise slip from human memory through the passage of time and the lapsing courses of years, it should be entrusted to memorial writings, preserved in letters and pages, for more certain knowledge and firmer efficacy [Column 1136].

[Note: B reads *Horum*, “of these,” instead of *Eorum*, “of those.”] Desiring in every respect to follow the footsteps of all these predecessors, I, Melisende [Note: B reads *Melissendis*.], by divine clemency queen of Jerusalem, wish it to be made known to all people, both present and their descendants, that I freely and peacefully relinquish the claim which, at the suggestion of certain persons, I had made against the church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: B reads *Dominici*, “of the Lord,” for *Sancti*.] and the canons of that place concerning the villeins of Bethsurie, namely: Selmen son of Maadi, Habderahmen [Note: B reads *Habderahmen*.], Selim, Hasem, Nasen, Melpedem [Note: B reads *Mekedem*.], Seleemen Sade, Brahin, Kannet, Naser [Note: B reads *Nasser*.], Ariz, Mahmut, Zafer, Demsis, Resselem, Tameh, Rosec, Sahe, Salem son of Sade, and all the others, together with the land of that casale; this I do with the consent and concession of my sons, namely King Baldwin and Amalric, count of Jaffa, and also with the counsel and approval of good men.

[Note: In diploma 52 these two names appear to form a single name.]

Thus the canons shall freely and peacefully have, hold, and possess forever, without any contradiction or claim on my part or that of any of my heirs, the aforesaid villeins against whom the claim had been raised, together with all their descendants, and the aforesaid land by our donation and concession, just as they are known to have had, held, and possessed it more freely and peacefully from the time of the most illustrious Duke Godfrey [Note: B reads *Godefridi*.].

To this donation and concession we add and join the Syrians of Calandria—Cosmas, Seimahian [Note: B reads *Semhan*.], Samuel, Ihanna, Meferreg, and Gerges—for whom the station formerly belonging to William the Bastard and the shares they held in two money-changers’ tables were granted to us from their own property for the completion of our new street in Jerusalem—and the Syrians of Ramethes, namely Bolferag, Jacob, Brahim, and Isaac, against whom we at one time brought a claim before those same canons; and also that vineyard which Lady Geltidis, wife of Lord Rohard, when she was about to depart from this world, gave to those same canons for the salvation of her soul. We confirm that the canons shall forever have, hold, and possess all the aforesaid Syrians together with all their descendants, and the aforesaid vineyard, according to the form stated above.

[Note: B reads *Kalandria*.]

Therefore, so that all these matters which we have recorded may remain fixed, firm, and unshaken for the church of the Holy Sepulchre, in the order in which we have set them forth, free from the disturbance, intervention, and quibbling of all persons, both secular and ecclesiastical [Column 1137], it pleased us to have this chirograph of the present page written for the canons of the same church; and, so that every opportunity for a future claim might be removed, to strengthen this chirograph by the impression of our seals.

The witnesses to this matter are the following, whose names appear written below:

Rohard, namely, and his nephew Radulphus; John of Valenciennes [Note: B reads *Valencienes*.]; Babinus; Fulk; Salem; Bencelinus; and Thosetus [Note: B reads *Tosetus*.], all of whom assembled concerning the land in question, about which the claim had been made.

And the others who follow, namely:

Roches of Nazareth [Note: B reads *Rorches*.]; Ermenaudus; Elias, his brother; Nicolaus, chamberlain; Odo of Turcarme [Note: B reads *Turcame*.]; Radulphus Li Fanchenirs [Note: B reads *Le Fanchenirs*.]; and Herbert of Regiteste, who were present at this concession of ours.

In the year 1152 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 15.

## XLIX. PRIVILEGE OF QUEEN MELISENDE CONCERNING THE EXCHANGE OF JOHN PATRICIUS

[Note: Column 1137: A, folio 44 recto; B, folio 43 verso.]  
[Note: This first heading is absent from A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, both future and present, that I, Melisende [Note: B reads *Milesendis*.], by the grace of God queen of Jerusalem, grant, approve, and confirm the exchange which was made in the time of my lord and husband, the illustrious King Fulk of Jerusalem, between John Patricius [Note: B reads *Iohannum*.] and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre: namely, his two casalia, Megina and Mezera, with all their appurtenances, in exchange for two other casalia of the Holy Sepulchre, Cafermelich and Anquina, likewise with all their appurtenances.

Babinus, from whom that John held his fief [Note: B places *tenebat* before *suum*.], granted the exchange and approved it in our presence. Petrosus, his kinsman, likewise granted the exchange that had been made. Bruna, John’s wife, and his sons Thomas and Eustachius, together with his heirs, assented before us and our men to the exchange, on this condition: if in the future any claim should arise concerning the aforesaid exchange of the casalia, John himself, the author of the exchange, and his heirs, and those to whom his inheritance should pass after him, would remain perpetually bound to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, so that whatever loss the church and its community might suffer because of the claim brought would be restored in full by John and his heirs, according to the assessment of good men.

But because in the time of King Fulk, on account of certain disputes arising on John’s side, the aforesaid exchange could not, as was pleasing to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, reach its proper and peaceful conclusion, I, who now see the matter and business entirely settled in peace, who was also present at the exchange that was made, and who subsequently heard from those mentioned above that the exchange had been granted and approved, hold it firm and valid and vigorously affirm it.

For the salvation of the soul of my aforesaid husband, of my own soul, and of the souls of my sons, who witnessed and granted the exchange, so that this exchange and concession might never be invalidated by anyone’s rashness, I have strengthened the present page containing the terms of the exchange and concession by the impression of my seal, so that through our care the aforesaid church of the Holy Sepulchre may have means to pray justly before the holy places [Note: B reads “before the holy places.”] to almighty God for us, who granted the gift.

The following were present at this concession of ours as truthful witnesses, whose names are written below:

Giraud [Note: B reads *Giraldus*.], bishop of Bethlehem [Note: B reads *Bethleemita*]; Arnulf, canon of the same church; Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple; Roger, his canon; Amalric, count of Jaffa [Note: B reads *Ioppe*.]; Manasses, constable; Philip the Neapolitan; Rohard; Radulphus Strabo; Orricus, viscount of Naples; Baldwin, his son; Baldwin Bubalus; Gautier Malduit; and John Vacher.

[Note: The copyist probably wrote *Balduinus* by mistake instead of *Henricus*.]

Burgesses:

Thosetus; Umbertus of Bar; Peter of Perregort [Note: B reads *Peregort*.]; Simon Rufus; Albert the Lombard.

In the year 1151 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 14 [Column 1139].

## L. ALSO, THE PRIVILEGE OF QUEEN MELISENDE CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF VUETMOAMEL

[Note: Column 1139: A, folio 45 recto; B, folio 46 recto.]  
[Note: This first heading is absent from A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, both future and present, that I, Melisende [Note: B reads *Milessendis*.], by the grace of God queen of Jerusalem, approve and grant the sale and purchase of land belonging to Hugh of Ibelin [Note: B reads *Hybelino*.], lawfully made between him and our brothers, the canons of the Holy Sepulchre: namely [Note: *Videlicet*, “namely,” is supplied from B.], Vuetmoamel with its villeins and all its appurtenances; Dersabeth [Note: B reads *Dersabeb*.] with its villeins and all its appurtenances; Corteis with its villeins and all its appurtenances; and everything else, as is contained in the privilege of King Baldwin, my beloved son.

At the request and admonition of that king [Note: B reads *amonicione*.], and likewise of Amalric [Note: B reads *Amalrici*.], count of Ascalon, as well as at the voluntary petition [Note: B reads *peticione*.] and request of the aforesaid Hugh, who made this sale, and of his brother Baldwin, and likewise at the petition [Note: B reads *peticione*.] of Lord Amalric [Note: B reads *Aimerici*.], patriarch of Antioch, whom the aforesaid canons had asked for this purpose, I approve and grant it; and, so that it may be held more firmly, I confirm this present page by the authority of my seal.

Hugh of Ibelin [Note: B reads *Hybelino*.] therefore sold the aforesaid property to the canons [Note: The text has *cannonicis*; the corrected form is *canonicis*, “canons.”] of the Holy Sepulchre for seven thousand bezants, to be possessed by hereditary right, free and exempt from every service, lordship, and exaction [Note: B reads *exactione*.].

The witnesses to this matter are:

Rainerius, bishop of Sebaste [Note: B reads *Sebastensis*.]; Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple; Philip the Neapolitan and Henry, his brother; and Roard of Naples [Note: B reads *Rohardus*.], together with many others.

This was done in the year 1155 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 4.

Given through the hand of Guido, the queen’s clerk.

## LI. ANOTHER PRIVILEGE OF KING BALDWIN IV CONCERNING THE EXCHANGE OF JOHN PATRICIUS

[Note: Column 1139: A, folio 45 verso; B, folio 48 verso.]  
[Note: This first heading is absent from A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, both present and future [Note: B reverses the order: “both future and present.”], that I, Baldwin, by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, with the consent of Melisende [Note: B reads *Milesendis*.], my mother and queen, and also with the approval of Amalric, my brother, count of Ascalon, grant, approve, and confirm the exchange made in the time of my father, the lord Fulk, illustrious king of Jerusalem, between John Patricius [Note: *Iohannem* is supplied from B.] and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre: two casalia, namely Megina and Mezera, with all their appurtenances, in exchange for two other casalia of the Holy Sepulchre, Cafermelich [Note: B reads *Caphermelich*.] and Anquina, likewise with their appurtenances.

Babinus, from whom that John held his fief, granted the exchange and approved it in the presence of our lady the queen [Note: B reads *domineque* for *dominice* in the phrase concerning the queen’s presence.] Petrosus, his kinsman, likewise granted the exchange that had been made. Bruna, John’s wife, and his sons Thomas and Eustachius assented to the exchange that had been made, on this condition: if in the future any claim should arise concerning the aforesaid exchange of the casalia, John himself, the author of the exchange, and his heirs, and those to whom his inheritance should pass after him, would remain perpetually bound to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, so that whatever loss the canons of the aforesaid church might suffer because of the claim brought would be restored in full to the church and its community according to the assessment of good men.

But because in the time of King Fulk, namely my father, on account of certain disputes arising on John’s side, the aforesaid exchange could not, as was pleasing to the aforesaid church of the Holy Sepulchre, reach its proper and peaceful conclusion, I [Note: *Ego* is supplied from B.], who now see the matter and business entirely settled in peace, who was also present at the exchange that was made, and who later heard from those whom I mentioned above that the exchange had been granted and approved, hold it firm and valid and vigorously affirm it.

For the salvation of my soul and of the souls of my parents, both living and dead, so that this exchange and confirmation might never be invalidated by anyone’s rashness, I confirm and strengthen by the impression of my seal the present page containing the terms of the exchange and confirmation, so that through my care the aforesaid church of the Holy Sepulchre may have means to pray justly before the holy places to almighty God for me, who confirm this oft-mentioned exchange.

This was done in the year 1155 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 3. The witnesses to this matter are:

Andrew of Monte Barro, master of the Temple; Humphrey, constable; Philip the Neapolitan; Guido, his brother, the Frenchman; Hugh of Ibelin [Note: B reads *Hybelino*.]; Odo of Saint-Amand; Isaac, castellan of the Tower of David; William of Barra; Galvannus of Rocha; Robert Asinus; and Thomas of Satorono.

Given at Jerusalem, through the hand of Radulphus the chancellor, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July.

## LII. ALSO, OF KING BALDWIN IV: CONCERNING THE REMISSION OF THE CLAIM WHICH QUEEN MELISENDE HAD MADE AGAINST THE VILLEINS OF BETHSURIE

[Note: Column 1139: A, folio 46 verso; B, folio 49 verso.]  
[Note: This first heading is absent from A.]  
[Note: B reads *Milesendis*.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

I, Baldwin, by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, wish it to be made known to all, both present and future, that I entirely remit to the aforesaid church and its canons the claim which Melisende [Note: B reads *Milesendis*.], my mother and queen, at the suggestion of certain persons, had made against the villeins of Bethsurie, namely: Selmen son of Maadi, Habderahmen, Selim, Hassem [Note: B reads *Asem*.], Nasen, Mekeden, Seleemen, Sade, Brahin, Kannet, Nasser, Hariz [Note: B reads *Ariz*.], Mahmut, Zaferdemsis [Note: In diploma 48 this word appears to form two distinct names.], Resselem, Tameth [Note: B reads *Tameh*.], Rosech, Sahe, Salem son of Sade, and all the others, together with the land of that casale.

I do this with the consent and concession of my aforesaid mother, the queen, and also of my brother Amalric, count of Ascalon, with the counsel and approval of good men. Thus the canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, now serving God there and destined to serve him in the future, shall freely and without any disturbance or impediment have and possess by perpetual right the aforesaid villeins against whom the claim had been raised, together with all their descendants, and the aforesaid land by my concession and confirmation, just as they are known to have had, held, and possessed it more freely and peacefully from the time of the most illustrious Duke Godfrey [Note: B reads *quiecius*, “more peacefully.”].

To this concession and confirmation of mine I also add the Syrians of Calandria—Cosmas, Semhan, Samuel, Ihanna, Meferreg, and Gerges—for whom the canons concerned granted to my mother, the lady queen, from their own property, the station formerly belonging to William the Bastard and the shares they held in two money-changers’ tables, for the completion of the new street in Jerusalem; and the Syrians of Ramethes, namely Bolferag [Note: B reads *Bolferag*.], Jacob, Brahim, and Isaac, against whom she had at one time brought a claim before those same canons; and also that vineyard which Lady Gislia, wife of Rohard [Note: B reads *Rohardi*.], when she was about to depart from this world, gave to the aforesaid canons for the salvation of her soul. I add and join these to the concession, and I confirm again that the canons shall forever have, hold, and possess all the aforesaid Syrians together with all their descendants, and the aforesaid vineyard, according to the form stated above.

[Note: B reads *sequacibus* (“followers” or “dependants”) instead of *sequatibus*; the latter is probably a corrupt spelling.]

And so that all these things which I have recorded, in the order in which I have set them forth, may remain forever fixed, firm, and unshaken for the church of the Holy Sepulchre, free from the disturbance, intervention, and quibbling of all persons, both secular and ecclesiastical, it pleased us to have this chirograph of the present page written for the canons of the same church; and, so that every opportunity for a future claim might be removed, to strengthen this chirograph by the protection of my seal [Note: B reads *cyrographum*.].

This was done in the year 1155 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 3. The witnesses to this matter are:

Geoffrey, abbot of the Lord’s Temple [Note: B reads *Templi Domini*]; Enguerrand, prior of Mount Zion; Andrew of Monte Barro, master of the Temple militia [Note: B reads *militie*, “of the militia”]; Humphrey, constable; Philip the Neapolitan; Hugh, lord of Caesarea; Hugh of Ibelin; Guido the Frenchman; Odo of Saint-Amand; William of Barra; John of Valenciennes [Note: B reads *Valantines*.]; Isaac, castellan of the Tower of David; and Babinus.

Given at Jerusalem, through the hand of Radulphus the chancellor, on the fifth day before the Kalends of July.

## LIII. ANOTHER PRIVILEGE OF KING BALDWIN IV CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF ALL POSSESSIONS

[Note: Column 1141: A, folio 47 verso; B, folio 52 verso.]  
[Note: This first heading is absent from A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, both present and future, that I, Baldwin, by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, following the footsteps of my predecessors of blessed memory—namely Duke Godfrey and his brother Baldwin, first king of Jerusalem, and also King Baldwin II, as well as Fulk, my father, third king of that city—for my salvation and that of my own, both living and dead, confirm and strengthen for the church of the Holy Sepulchre and its canons, now serving God there and destined to serve him in the future, everything which it has lawfully and reasonably obtained from the time of Duke Godfrey, by gift, concession, exchange, or purchase, within the boundaries of my kingdom up to the present day.

[Note: B reads *felicis*, “of blessed,” instead of *filicis*.]  
[Note: The words “first king of Jerusalem, and also Baldwin” are supplied from B.]  
[Note: The word *et*, “and,” is supplied from B.]  
[Note: B reads *Godefridi*.]

Therefore, in sequence, I have decided to set down, as the following statements make clear, what the aforesaid church has hitherto obtained by gift, concession, exchange, or purchase, and from whom.

First, Duke Godfrey gave and granted to the church, to be possessed in perpetuity, twenty-one casalia called by the names written below: Ainquine, Armotie, Kefreachab, Kefredil, Buhil, Hubin, Aram, Kalendie, Betdigge, Birra, Subahiet, Ataraberet, Urniet, Zenu, Helmule, Beittelamus, Baritmeta [Note: B reads *Barithmeta*.], Beituimen, Beitfuteier [Note: B reads *Beitfoteire*.], Betsurie, and Aineseins.

He also gave the same church all the ovens of Jerusalem, except two belonging to the Hospital and one belonging to the Latins. And the first King Baldwin gave and handed over to the aforesaid church the villeins at Saint Lazarus with their households, and four casalia above Saint Lazarus, whose names are these: Benehatie, Benehabeth, Ragabam, and Roma. He also gave the same church one thousand modii of wheat in the territory of Naples, to be received each year.

All these things, as they have been recalled above, I concede on my behalf to the church of the Holy Sepulchre and decree that it shall possess them forever.

Furthermore, I confirm half of that possession which the first King Baldwin gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem.

[Note: This phrase is absent from B.]

I also confirm the casale called Derina, situated in the territory of Tyre [Note: B reads *Tyrensi*.], above the great spring from which the watercourse flows, with all its appurtenances, except for another casale if it was ever subject to it; and, in the boundaries of the aforesaid casale, around the mountain lands, as much land as four pairs of oxen can cultivate from year to year; and the garden which lies between the wall and the outer wall of Tyre on the seaward side. All these things the second King Baldwin gave to the Holy Sepulchre.

Moreover, in the territory of Naples I confirm the casale called Cafermelech [Note: B reads *Cafarmelech*.], from the gift of the second King Baldwin, as it is recorded in his privilege.

Furthermore, I confirm for the canons of the Holy Sepulchre the half of the casale Fieisse [Note: B reads *Fiesse*.], now called the casale of the Holy Sepulchre, which Eustachius Ganerius [Note: B reads *Granerius*.], with the concession of King Baldwin II, gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre to be held freely and perpetually with all its appurtenances; and I confirm all that land which Gautier, son of the aforesaid Eustachius, gave to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre beyond the river around that same casale, to be held up to the boundary that was marked out and is still visible to this day [Note: B reads “the designated boundaries.”].

I also confirm to the same church the casale of Thecue with all its appurtenances [Note: B reads *appen[di]tiis*.], just as my father Fulk, third king of Jerusalem, gave it to the church of the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for Saint Lazarus in Bethany, with the consent of Melisende [Note: B reads *Milesendis*.], my mother and queen, and of Amalric, my brother, with that same freedom with which my aforesaid father is known to have held it together with Queen Melisende; and he confirmed it by his privilege [Note: B reads *firmavit*, “strengthened.”]. I likewise promise to defend the aforesaid gift and concession now and henceforth against every burden or impediment of a claim.

Moreover, I confirm the two full ploughlands which my aforesaid father confirmed to the church from the gift of Lambert Als, situated in the territory of the casale of Mimas.

Furthermore, I confirm to them the two casalia Gebul and Helcar with all their adjoining lands, the fisheries for eight days, the corvée for one day, and a ship permanently, according to the arrangement by which William de Buris granted these things to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre and by which they were strengthened by his privilege and that of my father.

I also confirm to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre the houses situated within the boundaries of Jerusalem, namely: the house of Peter Bernard, canon; the house of Evrard, canon; likewise the house of another Evrard, canon; the house of Minard [Note: C reads *Mainardi*.]; the house of Garsion; the house of Gautier Lentronior [Note: B reads *Lo Tornaor*.]; the house of Bernard Bursarius; the house of Herluin; the house of Mabilie, with the garden situated near the aforesaid house; the house of Roger of Saint Lazarus, brother of the Holy Sepulchre; and the station which belonged to William the Bastard [Note: B reads *Guillelmi*], together with the share which that William [Note: B reads *Guillelmus*.] held in the money-changers’ tables.

My father, so often mentioned, granted all these properties to the canons free and exempt from every exaction, while retaining the royal right which he ought to have in the alms that the king gives to the church [Note: B reads “which the king gives to the church.”]; and he fortified them with his privilege. I confirm them to the canons.

Moreover, I confirm the gift of the house situated at Acre, which Lambert Als, with the advice of Agnes his wife and also with the consent of Fulk my father, gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre according to the condition contained in their privilege.

Among other possessions, I ratify the three casalia, one called Capharuth, another Gith, and the third Porphyria, which Roger, bishop of Lydda, granted to the church of the Holy Sepulchre from the possession of Saint George, together with all their appurtenances, half the tithe of the harvests of those casalia, and the entire and undivided tithe of all other things, to be held by perpetual right.

I also decree valid the fourth casale, called Kefrescilta, which the aforesaid bishop of Lydda [Note: B reads *Liddensis*.] established for the aforesaid church to be possessed perpetually in its entirety and with a similar tithe to that of the three aforementioned casalia, in exchange, however, for the tithe of the castle of Arnold and the tithe of a certain casale belonging to the Hospital, called Bulbul.

I further confirm the exchange laudably made on both sides between the canons of the Holy Sepulchre and John Patricius: two casalia, Capharnelich [Note: B reads *Caphermelic*.] and Anquina [Note: B reads *Ainquina*.], in exchange for the two casalia of the aforesaid John, namely Megina and Mezera.

Finally, I confirm half of all offerings which shall come to the Sepulchre of the Lord, in every respect as the venerable Patriarch Arnulf assigned them to the aforesaid canons with the counsel of the first King Baldwin.

I also confirm to them all offerings which shall come to the life-giving Cross, except those offered solely on Good Friday [Note: B reads *parescheve*, “Good Friday.”] or those which the patriarch may carry away with him for some necessity [Note: B reads *veniunt*, “which come.”].

As for the wax that shall come to the church, I confirm two parts of it to them for the lights.

Furthermore, I confirm to them the tithes of the whole holy city of Jerusalem and of the places adjoining it, which the aforesaid patriarch granted to them, except for the tithes of the landholding (*fundi*), which belong to the patriarch.

I likewise confirm, in the manner stated above, the church of Saint Peter in Jaffa, which the patriarch so often mentioned [Note: B reads *tociens*] granted to the aforesaid canons with its entire honor and with everything belonging to the holy mother church, in full dignity.

I also confirm half of that benefice which the first King Baldwin granted to the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem.

[Note: The word *Bethleemitici*, “of Bethlehem,” is supplied from B.]

All these things, as they have been recalled above, I concede to the aforesaid church and its community, now and for those who shall serve God there in succession, to be held freely, peacefully, and without any claim or impediment in the future, and to be possessed by perpetual right; and I confirm and strengthen them by this present document.

And so that this page of my confirmation may remain valid and unaltered, I command that it be secured by the witnesses written below and by the impression of my seal [Note: Correct *precepi*, “I commanded,” for *precipi*.].

This was done in the year 1155 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 3. The witnesses to this matter are:

Amalric, the king’s brother and count of Ascalon; Humphrey of Toron, constable; Guido of Beirut [Note: B reads *Berytensis*.]; Girard of Sidon [Note: B reads *Sidoniensis*.]; Philip the Neapolitan; Guido the Frenchman; Henry Bufalus; Hugh of Caesarea; Baldwin of the Island; Odo of Tholent, castellan of the Tower of David; Odo of Saint-Amand; and William of Barra.

Given at Acre, through the hand of Radulphus the chancellor, on the third day before the Ides of July.

### Additional apparatus notes

- XLVI: B reads *ammonitu* for *amonitu* (“admonition”).
- XLVIII: B reads *quotiens* for *quociens* (“whenever”), *spaciis* for *spatiis* (“periods/spaces”), and *certiorem* for *cerciorem* (“more certain”). It reads *consilio etiam* for *etiam concilio* (“also with the counsel”), *novam* at the reference to the new street, *sequacibus* (“descendants/followers”) for *sequatibus*, *inquietatione* for *inquietacione* (“disturbance”), *eiusdem* for *eidem* (“of the same [church]”), and *cyrographum* for *cirographum* (“chirograph”).
- XLIX: B has the word order *suum tenebat* for *tenebat suum* (“held his fief”), *quicquid* for *quidquid* (“whatever”), and *locis sanctis* for *sanctis locis* (“the holy places”).
- LII: B reads *contradictione* for *contradicione* (“contradiction”).
- LIII: B reads *medietate* for *medietatem* (“half”) and *perhenni* for *perenni* (“perpetual”).

## LIV. ANOTHER PRIVILEGE OF KING BALDWIN IV CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF ALL POSSESSIONS

[Note: Column 1145: A, folio 50 recto; B, folio 58 recto.]  
[Note: This heading is absent from A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father and Holy Spirit, amen.

[The supplied source ends here.]

It should be known to all, present and future, that I, Baldwin, by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, desiring to follow in the footsteps of my predecessors of blessed memory—namely Duke Godfrey [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Godefridi*.] and his brother Baldwin, the first king of Jerusalem, as well as the second King Baldwin and my father Fulk, third king of that same city—for my salvation and that of my own, both living and dead, confirm to the Church of the Lord’s [Col. 1145C] Sepulchre and to its canons now serving God there and those who will serve Him in the future whatever, from the time of the aforesaid Duke Godfrey until this day, it has justly and reasonably obtained within the borders of my kingdom by gift, grant, exchange, or purchase.

I have therefore wished to set down, one by one, what the aforesaid church has obtained by gift, grant, exchange, or purchase, and from whom, as the following statements make clear.

First, Duke Godfrey gave the church in question twenty-one casalia, known by the names written below: Ainquine, Armotie, Kefreachab, Kefredil, Bubil, Hubin, Aram, Kalendie, Betdigge, Birra, Subahiet, Ataraberet, Uniet [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Urniet*.], Zenu, Helmule, Beittelamus, Aineseins, Barimeta, Beituimen [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Beitumen*.], and Beitfuteire; and he granted them to it for perpetual possession. [Col. 1145D] He also gave that church all the ovens of Jerusalem, except two belonging to the Hospital and one belonging to the Latins.

The first King Baldwin gave and transferred to the aforesaid church, at Saint Lazarus, the villeins together with their households, and four casalia above Saint Lazarus, whose names are these: Benehatie, Benehabeth, Ragabam, and Roma. In the territory of Naples he likewise gave the same church one thousand modii of wheat, to be received each year. All these things, as they have been mentioned above, I grant on my behalf to the church of the Holy Sepulchre and decree that it shall hold them perpetually.

[Col. 1146A] I further confirm half of that possession which the first King Baldwin gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem.

I also confirm the casale called Derina, situated in the territory of Tyre above the great spring from which the water conduit flows, with all its appurtenances, except another casale if it was at any time subject to it; and, along the boundaries of the aforesaid casale, in the mountainous region, as much land as four pairs of oxen can cultivate from year to year; and the garden situated between the wall and the outer wall of Tyre on the sea side. All these things, namely, the second King Baldwin gave to the Lord’s Sepulchre, and I confirm them.

Moreover, in the territory of Naples I confirm the casale called Cafarmelie [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Cafarmelec*.], given by the gift of the second King Baldwin, as it is recorded in his privilege.

[Col. 1146B] Furthermore, I confirm to the aforesaid church the half of the casale of Fieisse, now called the casale of the Holy Sepulchre, which Eustace Garnerius [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Granerius*.], with the grant also of King Baldwin II, gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre to be held freely and perpetually with all its appurtenances; and I confirm to that often-mentioned church all the land which Walter, the son of the aforesaid Eustace, gave to the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre beyond the river around the same casale, to be held up to the designated boundaries, which are still visible to this day.

I further confirm to it the casale of Thecue in its entirety, as my father Fulk, third king of Jerusalem, gave it to the church of the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for Saint Lazarus in Bethany, with the assent of Queen Melisende, my mother, and of my brother Amalric—namely, with the same freedom with which my aforesaid father is known to have held it together with Queen Melisende—and confirmed it by his privilege. I promise to defend the grant of this donation for the aforesaid church, now and henceforth, against every burden or hindrance of dispute.

I also confirm to it the full ploughlands which my same father, from the gift of Lambert Als, confirmed to the aforesaid church as situated in the territory of the casale of Mimas.

I likewise confirm to the same church two casalia, Gebul and Helchar, with all their dependencies, together with fisheries for eight days, a corvée for one day, and a ship permanently, in accordance with the arrangement by which William de Buris granted these things to the canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre and they were strengthened by his privilege and that of my father.

[Col. 1146D] As for the houses situated within the enclosures of Jerusalem—namely, the house of Bernard the canon, the house of Eurard the canon, likewise the house of another Eurard the canon, the house of Mainard, the house of Garsion, the house of Walter Lentronior [Note: [Col. 1145] B reads *Lo Tornaor*.], the house of Bernard Bursarius, the house of Herluin, the house of Mabilie, the house of Roger, brother of the Holy Sepulchre, and the shop that belonged to William the Bastard, together with that portion which the same William held in the money-changers’ stalls—all these my often-mentioned father granted to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre free and undisturbed from every exaction, excepting the royal right which he ought to have in the alms that the king gives to the church—and fortified them by his privilege. I confirm them to the same canons.

Furthermore, I confirm to the often-mentioned canons the house founded at Acre, which Lambert Als and his wife Agnes, with the consent of King Fulk, my father, granted to the church of the Holy Sepulchre to be possessed freely and peacefully, on this condition: that it might not be removed from them by sale, exchange, or any other means; and, if they should do so, that the royal majesty should receive service from it.

Among other things, I decree as valid the three casalia, one called Capharuth, another Gith, and the third Porphiria, which Roger, bishop of Lydda, granted from the possession of Saint George, with all their appurtenances, together with half the tithe of their harvests and the entire tithe of all other things, to be held by the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre by perpetual right; and also the fourth casale, called Kefrescilta, which the aforesaid bishop of Lydda established for the aforesaid church to possess perpetually, with all its entirety and a similar tithe to that of the three aforementioned casalia, in exchange, however, for the tithe of the castle of Arnaldo and the tithe of a certain casale belonging to the Hospital, called Bulbul.

I also confirm the exchange commendably made between the aforesaid canons and John the Patrician: two casalia, Capharmelich [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Caphermelich*.] and Ainquina, in exchange for two casalia belonging to the said John, namely Megina and Mezera.

I likewise confirm that complaint concerning the Suriani which arose between me and the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre. As it is more fully contained in their privilege, where the names of the aforesaid Suriani are also written, I remitted it to the aforesaid canons, whether it was just or unjust, free, undisturbed, and entirely released.

Nevertheless, I again wholly remit and confirm as entirely released the dispute which for some time existed concerning the boundary limits of the territory of the casale of the Lord’s Sepulchre called Bethsuri, between Queen Melisende, my mother, and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, free, undisturbed, and without any hindrance or molestation either from me, my successors, or anyone else. [Note: [Col. 1147] In A one reads “or molestation of the church.”] [Note: [Col. 1147] Correct *remitto*.]

However, I confirm to the church of the Holy Sepulchre those casalia—namely Bethel, Odemamel, Dehirsabeth [Note: [Col. 1147] *Dehyrsabeth*.], Corteis, Deirmusin [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Deirmusun*.], and Huetdebes—which the often-mentioned canons purchased from Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Hybelino*.] for a price, together with all their villeins, their entire substance, and their appurtenances.

Finally, I confirm the half of all the offerings that come and will come to the Lord’s Sepulchre, in every respect as the venerable Patriarch Arnulf assigned it to the aforesaid canons on the advice of the first King Baldwin. Of the wax that comes to the church, I likewise confirm two parts to that church for its lights.

I further confirm to the same canons all the offerings that come to the Life-giving Cross, except those offered solely on Good Friday or those which the patriarch may have carried with him for some necessity.

I also confirm to the same canons the tithes of the entire holy city of Jerusalem and of the places adjoining it, which the patriarch named above granted to them, except only the tithes of the estates.

I likewise confirm half of that benefice which the first King Baldwin granted to the Holy Sepulchre in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem.

Finally, I confirm in the aforesaid manner the church of Blessed Peter in Joppa, which the often-mentioned patriarch granted to the aforesaid canons with all its honor intact and with the full dignity belonging to the holy mother church.

[Col. 1148B] All these things, therefore, as they have been mentioned above, I grant to the aforesaid church and to its community, now serving God there and in succession thereafter, to be held freely and peacefully and without any dispute or hindrance in the future, and to be possessed by perpetual right; and I confirm them by this present document, marked by the witnesses written below and by the impression of my seal. [Note: [Col. 1147] Omitted in B.]

This was done in the year from the incarnation of the Lord 1160, indiction VIII. The witnesses of all these matters are:

Peter, archbishop of Tyre; Ernesius [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Arnesius*.], archbishop of Caesarea; Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth; Constantine, bishop of Saint George; Rainerius, bishop of Sebaste [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Sebastensis*.]; Osbert, bishop of Tiberias; Frederick, bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads “bishop of Acre”]; Adam, bishop of Paneas; Amalric, bishop of Sidon [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Sydoniensis*.]; Mainard, bishop of Beirut [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Berythensis*.]; Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple of the Lord; Rainald, abbot of the Latins; Gunterius, prior of Mount Zion; Aimericus, prior of the Mount of Olives; William, seneschal of the Templars; Brother Geoffrey Fulcher.

Of the barons and men of the king:

Amalric, count of Ascalon; Henfred of Torono [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Torone*.], constable, and his son Henfred; Walter, lord of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Tyberiadensis*.]; Guormund of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Tyberiadensis*.]; Girard of Sidon [Note: [Col. 1147] *Sydoniensis*.]; Hugh of Caesarea; Philip of Naples; Walter of Beirut; Guido Francigena; Henry Bubalus; Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1147] B reads *Hybelino*.] and his brother Baldwin; William, marshal; Odo of Saint-Amand, castellan of Jerusalem.

Given at Acre, by the hand of Radulf, bishop of Bethlehem and chancellor of the king, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August.

## LV. Another Privilege of King Baldwin IV concerning the remission of the dispute which he had raised concerning the Suriani and that which the queen had raised concerning the land of the casale of Bethsuri

[Note: [Col. 1149] A, folio 53 recto; B, folio 55 verso.] [Note: [Col. 1149] “Another” is absent in A.]

[Col. 1149A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

It should be known to all, present and future, that I, [Baldwin], by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, not tolerating that the rights of the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre be diminished in any respect contrary to what is fitting, wholly remit to the church of the aforesaid Lord’s Sepulchre that dispute concerning these Suriani, whose names are written below, which arose between me and the venerable canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre, my brothers, whether it was just or unjust; and I confirm it as entirely free, undisturbed, and released.

This is provided, however, that the Suriani in question, or their heirs, wherever they may be or wherever they may be found, shall in no way be permitted henceforth to withdraw from the lordship of the aforesaid church or, at anyone’s instigation or through any evasion, to transfer themselves to any other lord; but, just as they are known to have belonged to the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre in ancient times and from the earliest days, so they and their heirs shall remain subject to it perpetually.

The names of the Suriani are these:

From the casale of Ramatha: Cosmas and his son Baraqueth [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Barachet*]; Hubeit, the brother of Cosmas, and Teodros [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Theodros*], his brother; and Ysaac, the brother of Cosmas; Yuset and his son Petros; Ubeit and his brother Elias; Meneia the hunter; and Salem the elder and his son Ubeit; Ianna and his son Saac and his other son Elias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Helias*]; Samuel [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Samuhel*], son of George, and his brother Faet; Ianna, son of Munsor; and Petros, son of Phara, and his brother Samuel [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Samuhel*].

From the casale of Bethelegel: Salem, son of Azar [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Aazar*], and his brother Ianna; Saba, son of Sarsor, and his brothers Aaron and Jacob; Elias, son of Coer, and his son Brahin [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Brahyn*]; Oies; George, son of Zorech, and his brothers Feeth and Hetnon; Aias and his brother Pharas; George, son of Sayth; Tedros [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Thodros*], son of Brain [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Brayn*], and his brothers Ubeit and Basil; Elias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Helias*], the little one; Elias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Helias*], son of Iumel; Ianna, son of Rofehe, and his brother Salem; Petros, son of George, and his brother; George, son of Iaphar, and his son Brahin and his brother Saac; George and his son Saba; Elias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Helias*], the mason; and Elias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Helias*], son of Iaphar.

From Aithara: Salem, son of Messalem; Saac [and] [Note: [Col. 1149] Supplied from B.] his brother Elias; Braim [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Braym*], son of George; Martin, son of Ayza [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Aiza*]; Solomon and his son Cosmas; Thodros and his son Ianna; and Ysaac [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Saac*].

From Canlandria [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Calandria*]: Cosmas; Semaan and his son George; Braym, son of Cosmas; Samuel, son of Baraqueth [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Baraquet*], and his brothers Fimi and Nicholas; Meferut, son of Chame; Saac [Col. 1150A], son of George, and his brother Geuset [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Geuseth*]; Ianna and his son Geuseth, and his other son George, and his other son Elias; Camis, son of Bolpharage, and his brother Elias; Serget, son of Antoni; Belcaira, son of Monsor [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Munsor*]; Brahim [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Braym*], son of George; and George, the brother of Solomon.

From Bolferage: his son, his sister, and his brothers Brahim [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Braym*], Jacob, and Elias; Brahim [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Braym*], son of George, and his brother Botros; and Munferreth and his brother.

Nevertheless, I wholly remit and strengthen that dispute which for some time existed concerning the boundary limits of the territory of the casale of the Lord’s Sepulchre called Bethsuri, between the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre and Queen Melisende [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Milessendem*], my mother, free, undisturbed, and entirely without any hindrance or molestation either from my successors or from anyone else.

Therefore, so that the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre may have and possess all the matters mentioned above, in the order stated, in complete peace now and forever, I confirm them by this present document, marked by the witnesses written below and by the impression of my seal.

This was done in the year from the incarnation of the Lord 1160 [Note: [Col. 1149] A gives the evidently erroneous date 1155], indiction VIII. The witnesses of this matter are:

Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth; Richard [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Ricardus*], bishop of Andria; Arnulfus [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Arnulfus*], canon of Nazareth; Philip, chaplain of the lord king; Stephen, secretary of the royal chancery; Radulf, cleric of the archbishop of Nazareth.

[Col. 1150C] And of the barons and men of the lord king:

Amalric, count of Ascalon; Henfred of Torono, constable; Guido [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Guido*.] Francigena; William, marshal; Abraham, viscount of Nazareth; Oitho of Risberge; Guido [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Guido*.] de Maneriis; Albert of Retesth; Godescalcus; Peter, forester.

Given at Acre, by the hand of Radulf, bishop of Bethlehem and chancellor of the king, on the eighth day before the Kalends of August.

## LVI. Privilege of the same King Baldwin IV concerning the confirmation of Vuetmoamel

[Note: [Col. 1149] A, folio 54 verso; B, folio 51 recto.] [Note: [Col. 1149] “Of the same” is absent in A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

It should be known to all, present and future, that I, Baldwin, by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, at the urgent request of Hugh of Ibelin and with the consent of his brother Baldwin, his sister Hermengard, lady of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1149] B reads *Tyberiadis*], his mother Helois, and his uncles—namely Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, Henry Bubalus—and all the others to whom the grant of the present sale appears to belong, or to whom hereditary possession of the property sold may belong in the future, approve [Note: [Col. 1151] B adds “and”], confirm, and strengthen by the affixing of my seal the sale and purchase lawfully made between Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1151] *Hybelino*.] and our brothers, the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, whose agreement is set out on the following page.

The aforesaid Hugh therefore sold to the aforesaid brothers, the canons of the most holy church of the Resurrection, Vuetmoamel with its villeins and all its appurtenances, except two casalia belonging to the Arab knight, namely Odabeb and Damersor. He also sold Desabeb [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Dersabeb*.] with all its villeins and appurtenances; Corteis with its villeins and all its appurtenances; whatever his father possessed in Zibi on the day on which he lived and died, and which by hereditary right belongs to the lordship of Hugh himself or his successors; and likewise in the city of Bethel whatever his father possessed on the day on which he lived and died and which came to the often-mentioned Hugh as heir or to his successors.

All these things, I say, the often-mentioned Hugh sold to the community of the Lord’s Sepulchre for seven thousand bezants, to be possessed in perpetuity, free, released, and undisturbed from every service, lordship, and exaction.

So that this sale might remain more secure [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads “might remain secure”], and no one’s opposition cause it to waver, as I have said, his brother Baldwin consented to it, as did his mother Elois [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Helois*] and his sister Hermengard, namely the lady of Tiberias; likewise his uncles Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, and Henry Bubalus.

The relatives of Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Hybelino*.] also consented: Philip of Cafran, his brother, and Peter of Tellei.

On behalf of those who are under age—such as Barisan, the brother of Hugh of Ibelin, and a certain young sister of his named Stephanie, and any others of the same lineage who are found or may in the future be found to be under age—Hugh of Ibelin, his brother Baldwin, Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, and Henry Bubalus are sureties that, when those persons reach the lawful age, they will cause them, within that year, to grant the aforesaid sale. [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads “will cause them”.]

The same aforesaid barons are also lawful pledges to clear all the aforesaid matters from every dispute, now and forever. [Note: [Col. 1151] In A one reads *pelagii* instead of *plegii*.] This is on the condition that whichever of these pledges survives, when the others have died according to human custom, shall answer on their behalf and clear the dispute. If, in the meantime, any dispute should at any time arise concerning these persons for whatever reason, whichever of the aforesaid pledges first appears shall settle the dispute. But if anyone in the future brings a dispute concerning the aforesaid sale, those to whom Hugh’s inheritance passes after him shall remain perpetually bound to the community of the Lord’s Sepulchre, so that whatever loss the same community suffers because of the dispute brought against it shall be restored to that often-mentioned community in full by those persons, according to the assessment of good men.

This was done in the year from the incarnation of the Lord 1155, indiction IV. The witnesses of this matter are:

Lethardus [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Letardus*.], archbishop of Nazareth; Constantine, bishop of Lydda; Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple; Amilius, abbot of the Latins; Engerannus, prior of Mount Zion; Roger, prior of Saint Abraham; Baldwin, archdeacon of Lydda.

Of the brothers of the Temple:

Brother Odo, commander; Brother Walter of Beirut; Brother Philip; Brother Lodovicus [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Lodoicus*.]

Of the king’s barons:

Humfred of Toro [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Torono*.], constable of the king; John Gothman; Hugh of Caesarea.

And of the king’s men:

Odo of Saint-Amand; William de Barra; Odo of Tholent; Hugh of Bezan; Vivian of Cayphas [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Cayphas*.]; Gocelin [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Gozelinus*.] Pesellus; Arnald of Crest, constable of Tripoli; Arnulf of Hisinguin; William of Mount Gisard; Gocelin of Samosac; Bartholomew of Soissons; Arnulf, viscount of Jerusalem.

[Col. 1152C] Of the burgesses:

Hugh *saliens in bonum* [Latin: “leaping toward good”]; Peter of Périgueux; Bricius; Geoffrey of Tours; William the Norman; Rainald the Sicarius; Peter of Saint James; Peter Hugonis; Peter of Saint Lazarus.

Given at Acre [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Achon*.], by the hand of Radulf the chancellor, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February.

## LVII. Privilege of the same concerning the confirmation of Huetdebes

[Note: [Col. 1151] A, folio 56 recto; B, folio 57 recto.] [Note: [Col. 1151] This first heading is absent in A.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

[Col. 1152D] It should be known to all, present and future, that I, Bal[duin], by the grace of God fourth Latin king in holy Jerusalem, approve the land in question, which Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1151] B reads *Hybelino*.] cleared entirely for himself from Musse Arabit and his son George, as well as from all their relatives to whom it appeared to belong by hereditary right, and made entirely free of claim; and which he afterward, of his own free will, with the consent of the count of Ascalon, from whose fief it derives, and with the common consent of all his relatives to whom it was believed to belong by hereditary right, sold to the venerable canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre, my brothers, for three thousand bezants.

At the urgent request of the aforesaid Hugh, I approve the land in question—namely, two casalia in their entirety, with all their villeins and appurtenances, one of which is called Deirmusim and the other Huetdebes [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Uetdebes*]—for the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre and for the canons now serving God there and those who will serve Him in the future. I grant those two casalia free, undisturbed, and released from every service, lordship, and exaction, to be possessed by perpetual right forever, without any hindrance or dispute from anyone; and I confirm them by this document, marked by the witnesses written below and by the impression of my seal.

[Col. 1153B] This was done in the year from the incarnation of the Lord 1160, indiction VIII. The witnesses of this matter are:

Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth; Richard, bishop of Andria; Arnulfus, canon of Nazareth; Philip, chaplain of the lord king; Stephen, secretary of the royal chancery; Radulf the Englishman, cleric of the archbishop of Nazareth.

Of the barons and men of the king:

Amalric, count of Ascalon; Henfred of Torono, constable; Guido Francigena; William, marshal; Abraham, viscount of Nazareth; Otto of Risberge; Guido de Maneriis; Albert of Rethest; Godescalcus; Peter, forester.

Given at Acre [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Achon*.], by the hand of Radulf, bishop of Bethlehem and chancellor of the king, on the eighth day before the Kalends of August.

## LVIII. Privilege of Count Amalric concerning the gift of Geladia and the confirmation of all the possessions which the church of the Holy Sepulchre has in his land

[Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “Also”.] [Note: [Col. 1153] A, folio 56 verso; B, folio 65 verso.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

It should be known to all, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God count of Ascalon, with the assent and will of my lord and brother Baldwin, king of Jerusalem, and likewise with the approval of my lady and mother, Queen Melisende, for my salvation and for the souls of all my relatives, living and dead, and also in consideration of the expense and expenditure which they incurred in capturing Ascalon, give, grant [Note: [Col. 1153] Omitted in B.] and confirm [and] [Note: [Col. 1153] Supplied from B.] in perpetuity to the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “my fellow canons”] and to my fellow brothers now serving God there and to the canons who will serve Him canonically [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “canonically”] in the future, a certain casale called Geliadia [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Geladia*.], together with sixteen ploughlands, as it was delivered, divided, marked out with boundaries and landmarks, and delimited for them by my men. [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “marked out”.]

I also give and confirm to the same canons [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “fellow canons”] and my fellow brothers one house in Ascalon and two ploughlands in the casale called Baineolbederan, in exchange for a certain mosque, which was given to them in Ascalon from the time of its capture. The aforesaid canons [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “fellow canons”], in their chapter, by equal vote and assent of Lord Patriarch Amalric, unanimously granted, remitted, and transferred that mosque to me and my successors in exchange for these two ploughlands and the aforesaid house. The Saracens call this mosque Cathara; in Latin it is called *Viridis*, “Green.”

I likewise confirm to my often-mentioned fellow brothers four ploughlands [Col. 1154B] situated beyond the river before Joppa, as they have been divided and marked with boundaries; one garden before Joppa and the adjoining vineyard; and that vineyard [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “another vineyard”] which was given to them as alms [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “as alms”].

I confirm to them whatever they justly and lawfully possess and hold peacefully and without dispute in Ascalon and its territory, and likewise in Joppa and its territory.

Therefore, so that my aforesaid fellow canons and brothers may possess all these things freely, peacefully, and released from every exaction and burden, [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “released and peaceful”.] I have strengthened this present charter with my seal and the witnesses written below. [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads “fellow canons”.] [Note: [Col. 1153] Correct *confratris* to *confratres*.] [Note: [Col. 1153] “Without every” supplied from B.]

This was done in the year of the incarnation of the Lord 1160, indiction IV. The witnesses of this matter are:

Gunterius, prior of Mount Zion; Aimericus, prior of the Mount of Olives; Rainerus, chancellor; Radulf, archdeacon of Jerusalem; Simon [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Symon*.] of Hosdenc [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Osdenc*.]; Jocelin of Samosac; Bertram [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Bertrandus*.], marshal [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *marescalcus*.]; Rohard of Joppa and his brother Barisan; Raynald [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Rainaldus*.] of Joppa; Gerbert; Albert; Lambert; Pilatus [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Pylatus*.]; William Rufus; Gilbert, castellan.

Given at Joppa, by the hand of Radulf the chancellor, on the second day before the Kalends of December.

## LIX. Privilege of Count Amalric concerning the confirmation of Vuetmoamel

[Note: [Col. 1153] A, folio 57 verso; B, folio 61 verso.]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

It should be known to all, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God count of Ascalon, at the urgent request of Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Hybelino*.] and with the consent of his brother Baldwin, his sister Hermengard, lady of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Tyberiadis*.], his mother Alois, and his uncles—namely Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, Henry Bubalus—and all the others to whom the grant of the present sale [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *vendicionis*.] appears to belong, or to whom hereditary possession of the property sold may belong in the future, approve and confirm, and strengthen by the affixing of my seal, the sale and purchase lawfully made between Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1153] B reads *Hybelino*.] and our brothers, the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, whose agreement is set out on the following page.

The aforesaid Hugh therefore sold to the aforesaid brothers, the canons of the church of the Lord’s Resurrection, Vuetmoamel with its villeins and all its appurtenances, except two casalia belonging to the Arab knight, namely Odabeb and Darmersor. He also sold Dersabeb with its villeins and all its appurtenances; Corteis with its villeins and all its appurtenances; whatever his father possessed in Zimi on the day on which he lived and died, and which by hereditary right belongs to the lordship of Hugh himself or his successors; and likewise in the city of Bethel whatever his father possessed on the day on which he lived and died and which belongs to the often-mentioned Hugh as heir or to his successors.

All these things, I say, the often-mentioned Hugh sold to the community of the Lord’s Sepulchre for seven thousand bezants, to be possessed in perpetuity, released, free, and undisturbed from every service, lordship, and exaction.

So that this sale of his might remain more secure and no one’s opposition cause it to waver, as I have said, his brother Baldwin consented to it, as did his mother Helois [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Alois*.] and his sister Ermengard [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Hermengardis*.], lady of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Tyberiadis*.], as well as his uncles Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, and Henry Bubalus.

The relatives of Hugh of Ibelin also consented: Philip of Cafram [Col. 1155C] [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Cafran*.], his brother, and Peter of Teillei.

On behalf of those who are under age—such as Barisan, Hugh’s brother, and a certain sister of his named Theophanne [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Theophannia*.]—and if any others of the same lineage are found or may in the future be found to be under age, Hugh of Ibelin, his brother Baldwin, Philip of Naples, Guido Francigena, and Henry Bubalus are sureties that, when they reach the lawful age, they will cause them, within that year, to grant the aforesaid sale. [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads “will cause them”.]

The same aforesaid barons are also lawful pledges to clear all these matters from every dispute, now and forever. This is on the condition that whichever of these pledges survives, when the others have died according to human custom, shall answer on their behalf and clear the dispute. If, in the meantime, any dispute should at any time arise concerning these persons for whatever reason, whichever of the aforesaid pledges first appears shall remove and settle the dispute.

But if anyone in the future brings a dispute concerning the aforesaid sale, those to whom Hugh’s inheritance passes after him shall remain perpetually bound to the aforesaid community, so that whatever loss the same community suffers because of the dispute brought against it shall be restored in full to that community by those persons, according to the assessment [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *estimatione* instead of *extimatione*.] of good men.

This was done in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1155, indiction IV. The witnesses of this matter are:

Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth; Constantine [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Constantinus*.], bishop of Lydda; Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple; Amilius, abbot of the Latins; Engelrannus, prior of Mount Zion; Roger, prior of Saint Abraham; Baldwin, archdeacon of Lydda.

Of the brothers of the Temple:

Brother Odo, commander; Brother Gautier of Beirut; Brother Philip; Brother Ludoicus.

Of the king’s barons:

[The supplied source ends here, with this incomplete heading.]

[Col. 1156B] Henry of Toron [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Henfredus*], the king’s constable. John Gotman [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Gothman*]. Hugh of Caesarea [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Hugo*]. Odo of Saint-Amand. William of Barra. Odo of Tolent. Hugh of Bezan [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Hugo*]. Vivian of Cayphas [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Caypha*]. Jocelyn Pesellus. Arnald of Crest, constable of Tripoli. Arnulf of Hysengihm [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Hysenghin*]. William of Montgisard. Jocelyn of Samusac.

**Of the burgesses:**

Arnulf, viscount of Jerusalem. Hugh “Leaping into the Good.” Peter of Périgueux. Brice. Geoffrey of Tours. William the Norman. Rainald the Butcher. Peter of Saint James; Peter, son of Hugh. Peter of Saint Lazarus.

[Col. 1156C] Given at Acre [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *Achon*], through the hand of Ralph the chancellor, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February.

**LX [Note: [Col. 1155] A, fol. 58 verso; B, fol. 63 recto]. PRIVILEGE OF THE SAME [Note: [Col. 1155] In B this first heading reads: “Another privilege of Count Amalric.”] CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF HUETDEBES.**

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God count of Ascalon, at the urgent request of Hugh of Ibelin and with the consent of his brothers Baldwin and Barisan, of his sister Ermengard and his mother Alois, and of his maternal uncles Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, Henry Bubalus, and all the others to whom consent for the present sale appears to belong, or to whom hereditary possession of the sold property may belong in the future, approve, confirm, and strengthen by the affixing of my seal the sale and purchase lawfully made between the aforesaid Hugh and my brothers, the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, whose agreement the following page sets out.

[Col. 1156D] The often-mentioned Hugh therefore sold to the aforesaid canons of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1155] B reads *canonicis*] Huetdebes, with its peasants and all its appurtenances, and also Deirmuesim, with its peasants and all its appurtenances, together with the entire plenitude of rights which Muisse Arrabit and his son George had in them by gift of his father Barisan of pious memory, and which belonged by hereditary right to their successors, to be possessed in perpetuity for three thousand bezants, free and exempt from every service, lordship, and exaction.

[Col. 1157A] For Hugh of Ibelin, compelled by the impending necessity of his captivity and ransom, gave to his aforesaid men, Muisse Arrabit and his son George, the power to make an exchange according to their wishes [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *ad eorum voluntatem*] for the aforesaid estates and their appurtenances. They confirmed the aforementioned sale by oath in the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre and promised to uphold it against all.

[Col. 1157B] But so that this sale might remain more secure and no one’s opposition [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *contradictio*] weaken it, his brothers Baldwin and Barisan, his mother Alois, his sister Ermengard [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Hermengardis*], and also his maternal uncles Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus, as I have said, consented to it [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *etiam*]; so too did his kinsmen Philip of Caphran [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Cafran*], his brother, and Peter of Teillei.

On behalf of those who are under age—namely, a certain sister of the often-mentioned Hugh, Stephania, and some of the heirs of the aforesaid Arrabit and his son George, if any others of minor age are found or may in future be found among their lineage—Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Hybelino*], his brother Baldwin, the aforesaid Muisse Arrabit and his son George, Simon of Aia [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Symon de Haia*], Ordelet and his son Stephen, Adam of Orgeol, Nicholas of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Hybelino*], Hosmund, his brother Ralph, Lebert, Pagan of Rohais, and Philip of Caphran [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Cafran*] swore upon the holy relics and are also sureties that, when those persons reach the lawful age, they will cause [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *facient*] them, within that year, to come to the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre and consent to the often-mentioned sale.

[Col. 1157C] These same persons are likewise lawful pledges to clear all the aforesaid matters from every claim, now and always. Finally, if anything [Note: [Col. 1157] A reads *si quidem*] should be diminished from all that has been written above, all those who have sworn an oath concerning the aforementioned purchase, when summoned by the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre or by its messenger [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *internuntium*], shall remain as hostages within the walls of Jerusalem for fifteen days from the time of the summons, until the matter has been restored completely and in full.

[Col. 1157D] This was done in the year 1158 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the seventh indiction. The witnesses to this matter are:

[Ricard], bishop of Andria. Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple. Gunter, prior of Mount Zion.

**Of the king’s men:**

Adam the Black and his brother, Fulco [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Fulco*]. Robert of Retest.

[Col. 1158A] **Of my men:**

Simon [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Symon*] of Hosdenc. Jocelyn of Samusach [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Samusac*] and his brother Baldwin. Gerbert. Guibert. Albert. William of Tyre [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Tyro*]. William of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Tyberiade*]. Leverald. Gerald of Rumminhi [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Girardus de Ruminhi*].

**Of my stipendiaries:**

Walter of Hainaut. William of Rumhe. Albert of Guarch. Robert of Saint-Kavileffo. Fulco.

**Of the king’s burgesses:**

Hugh “Leaping into the Good.” Geoffrey of Tours.

**LXI [Note: [Col. 1157] A, fol. 60 recto; B, fol. 64 verso]. PRIVILEGE OF THE SAME CONCERNING THE CONFIRMATION OF THE VINEYARD THAT BELONGED TO NAIM THE SYRIAN.**

[Col. 1158B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God count of Ascalon, for the remedy of my present, past, and future sins and of those of my parents, both living and dead, give, grant, and confirm to my venerable brothers, the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and especially to you, Hugh, dean of Joppa, who are called “of Tarsus,” one piece of vineyard that belonged to a certain Syrian named Naim [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Naym*], which you, the aforesaid dean, purchased from the said Naim [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Naym*] for fifty-two bezants.

I mean the two parts that belonged to Naim, which you purchased from him; but the third part, which is my right, I give and confirm, as stated above, to you, the aforesaid dean, and to the aforementioned canons. I also give to you, dean, and to the aforesaid brothers the whole part and right that pertains to me in the vineyard of Menferret the Syrian.

These two pieces of vineyard lie east of the vineyard of the Lord’s Sepulchre. In return for this gift and confirmation, your fatherly affection, dean, gave me one hundred bezants. Therefore, so that these two pieces of vineyard may serve you, dean, and the aforesaid canons and their successors, the canonical brothers, in perpetuity, freely, peacefully, and without any exaction, I ordered this charter to be confirmed by the witnesses written below and by the affixing of my seal.

[Col. 1158D] This was done in the year 1158 from the incarnation of the Lord. The witnesses to this matter are:

Jocelyn of Samusac and his brother Baldwin. Garcio. Jordan Bestia. Raphael. Pontius [Note: [Col. 1157] B reads *Poncius*]. Thomas of Turchia and his brother-in-law Herbert. Lambert Galiota.

Given at Ascalon, through the hand of Ralph the chancellor, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of December.

**LXII [Note: [Col. 1159] A, fol. 60 verso; B, fol. 66 verso]. PRIVILEGE OF HUGH OF IBELIN [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Hybelino*] CONCERNING THE SALE OF VUETMOAMEL [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Hvuetmoaval*].**

[Col. 1159A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Hugh of Ibelin, with the consent of my brother Baldwin, my sister Ermengard, lady of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Tyberiadis*], my mother Alois, and my maternal uncles—namely Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus—and of all the others to whom consent for the present sale appears to belong, or to whom hereditary possession of the sold property may belong in the future, sold to the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre Vuetmoamel [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Huetmoamel*], with all its peasants and appurtenances, except for the two estates of the Arab knight, namely Odabeb and Darmersor.

I also sold Dersabeb, with its peasants and all its appurtenances; Corteis, with its peasants and all its appurtenances; everything at Zimi that my father possessed on the day on which he lived and died and that belongs by hereditary right to my lordship or to that of my successors; and likewise in the city of Bethel everything that my father possessed on the day on which he lived and died and that belongs to me [Note: [Col. 1159] reads *michi*] as heir or to my successors.

All these things, I say, I sold to the aforesaid brothers of the Lord’s Sepulchre to be possessed in perpetuity for seven thousand bezants, free and exempt from every service, lordship, and exaction, free and peaceful.

But so that this sale of mine might remain more secure and no one’s opposition make it unstable, my brother Baldwin, and likewise my mother Helois [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Alois*], my sister Ermengard, lady of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Tyberiadis*], and also my maternal uncles Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus, as I have said, consented to it; my kinsmen Philip of Cafran and his brother, and Peter of Tellei, also consented.

On behalf of those who are under age—namely, my brother Barisan and my sister Stephania, and any others of minor age who are found or may in future be found in my lineage—I, my brother Baldwin, Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus are sureties that, when they reach the lawful age, we shall cause [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *faciemus*] them, within that year, to consent to the aforementioned sale.

We ourselves, the same aforesaid barons, are likewise lawful pledges to clear all these matters from every claim, now and always, on this condition: whichever of us pledges survives, when the others die in the human manner, he shall answer on behalf of all and clear the claim. If at any time, in the meantime, any claim should arise for any reason concerning the persons named above, whichever of our pledges encounters it first shall remove and settle that claim.

But if anyone in the future should bring a claim concerning the aforesaid sale, those to whom my inheritance passes after me shall be bound to the convent of the Holy Sepulchre so that whatever damage the convent suffers because of the claim brought shall be restored to it in full by them, according to the assessment of good men, and the aforesaid sale shall remain valid forever.

Therefore, so that nothing might be lacking to the authority of this privilege of mine—both because all these things were done with the assent and consent of my lord Amalric, count of Ascalon, whose fief held the property involved in the present sale [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *vendicionis*], and because I myself have no seal—I obtained, by urgent request, that this charter be strengthened by the seal of my aforesaid lord, the count of Ascalon.

Letard, archbishop of Nazareth. Constantine, bishop of Lydda. Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple. [Col. 1160B] Amilius, abbot of Saint Mary Latin. Engelran, prior of Mount Zion. Roger, prior of Saint Abraham. Baldwin, archdeacon of Lydda.

**Of the brothers of the Temple:**

Odo, commander. Walter of Beirut. Philip. Lodoic.

**Of the barons:**

Henfred of Toron [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Turono*], the king’s constable. John Gotman. Hugh of Caesarea. Odo of Saint-Amand. William of Barra. Odo of Tolent. Hugh of Bezan. Vivian of Caypha. Jocelyn Pesellus. Arnald of Crest, constable of Tripoli. Arnulf of Ysengihm [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Ysengihn*]. William of Montgisard. Jocelyn of Samusac. [Col. 1160C] Bartholomew of Soissons.

**Of the burgesses:**
