Arnulf, viscount of Jerusalem. Hugh “Leaping into the Good.” Peter of Périgueux. Brice. Geoffrey of Tours. William the Norman. Rainald the Butcher. Peter of Saint James. Peter, son of Hugh. Peter of Saint Lazarus. Andrew, son of Toset.

Given at Acre [Note: [Col. 1159] *Achon*], through the hand of Ralph the chancellor, on the nineteenth day before the Kalends of February.

**LXIII [Note: [Col. 1159] A, fol. 61 verso; B, fol. 68 recto]. PRIVILEGE OF THE SAME CONCERNING THE SALE OF HUETDEBES.**

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

[Col. 1160D] Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1159] B reads *Hybelino*], with the consent of my brothers Baldwin and Barisan, of my sister Ermengard and my mother Alois, and of my maternal uncles Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus, and of all the others to whom consent for the present sale appears to belong, or to whom hereditary possession of the sold property may belong in the future, sold to my brothers, the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, Huetdebes, with its peasants and all its appurtenances, and also Deirmugsin, with its peasants and all its appurtenances, together with the entire plenitude of rights which Muisse Arrabit and his son George had in them by gift of my father Barisan, and which belonged by hereditary right to their successors.

[Col. 1161A] I sold them, I say, to be possessed in perpetuity for three thousand bezants, free and exempt from every claim, service, lordship, and exaction, free and peaceful.

For I, compelled by the impending necessity of my captivity and ransom, gave to my men mentioned above, Muisse Arrabit and his son George, the power to make an exchange according to their wishes for the aforesaid estates and their appurtenances. They confirmed this sale by oath in the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre and promised to uphold it against all.

[Col. 1161B] But so that this sale of mine might remain more secure and no one’s opposition make it unstable, my brothers Baldwin and Barisan, my mother Alois, my sister Ermengard, and also my maternal uncles Philip of Naples, Guido the Frank, and Henry Bubalus, as I have said, consented to it; my kinsmen Philip of Cafran and his brother, and Peter of Teilli, also consented.

On behalf of those who are under age—namely, a certain sister of mine, Stephania, and some of the heirs of the aforesaid Arrabit and his son George, if any others of minor age are found or may in future be found in my lineage or theirs—I, my brother Baldwin, and my men Muisse Arrabit and his son George, Simon of Haia, Ordelet and his son Stephen, Adam of Orgeol, Nicholas of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Hybelino*], Hosmund and his brother Ralph, Lebert, Pagan of Rohais, and Philip of Cafran, swore upon the holy relics and are sureties that, when those persons reach the lawful age, we shall cause [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *faciemus*] them, within that year, to come to the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre and consent to the often-mentioned sale.

[Col. 1161C] We, the same aforesaid persons, are likewise under the aforesaid oath lawful pledges to clear all these matters from every claim, now and always. Finally, if anything [Note: [Col. 1161] A reads *si quidem*] should be diminished from the matters stated above, we who have sworn an oath concerning the aforementioned sale, when summoned by the chapter of the Holy Sepulchre or by its messenger [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *internuntium*], shall remain as hostages within the walls of Jerusalem from the day of the summons until the fifteenth day, until the matter has been restored whole and secure.

[Col. 1161D] Therefore, so that nothing might be lacking to the authority of this privilege of mine—both because all these things were done with the assent and consent of my lord Amalric, count of Ascalon, whose fief held the property involved in the present sale, and because I myself have no seal—I obtained by diligent request that this charter be strengthened by the seal of my aforesaid lord, the count.

This was done in the year 1158 from the incarnation of the Lord [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *dominice*], in the seventh indiction. The witnesses to this matter are:

Constantine, bishop of Lydda. Absalon, bishop. Geoffrey, abbot of the Temple. Rainald, prior of Saint Mary Latin. Peter of Calvary.

[Col. 1162A] **Of the brothers of the Hospital:**

Peter Bertrandi and William of Acer. Azo, chaplain of the estate of the Baths. Ralph, chaplain of Ramla. Paletel, viscount of Ibelin.

**Of the king’s burgesses:**

Humbert of Bar. Simon the Red. Brice. Geoffrey of Tours. William [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Willelmus*] the Norman. John Raimundi. Guibert Papais. Peter Burdinus. Peter of Saint James. Hugh “Leaping into the Good.” Ralph the Burgess. Peter of Saint Lazarus. John the Glazier. Everunimus [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Everinunus*]. Anschetinus. John, son of Rainald, the Poitevin.

**LXIV [Note: [Col. 1161] A, fol. 62 verso; B, fol. 69 verso]. PRIVILEGE OF HERBERT, ABBOT OF SAINTS JOSEPH AND ABACUC [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Abacuch*], CONCERNING THE EXCHANGE OF BETHEL [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *commutatione*].**

[Col. 1162B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Herbert [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Arbertus*], by the grace of God abbot of Saints Joseph and Abacuc, with the approval and consent of the entire community of clergy and laymen serving God there, in the presence of the good men whose names are written below, exchanged and returned to Hugh of Ibelin, lord of Ramla, whatever his father Barisan had given us at Bethel—namely Bethel itself and Beze, which is called Bazirim, with two ploughlands of land and five days’ work of land that we were claiming there, as well as the tower and whatever we had built there—so that the aforesaid Hugh might have power thereafter to do whatever he wished, without any opposition from us or our successors.

We also gave the chapel that we had built there, both at the command of the lord patriarch Amalric and at the request of lord Hugh, to lord prior Nicholas and the convent of the Holy Sepulchre. But the confirmations that we possess in our privileges concerning all these matters we entirely cancel and utterly declare void.

[Col. 1162C] All these things, in the presence of our brothers and of Baldwin, archdeacon of Saint George, and Gilbert, cantor of that same church, and Master Anschetinus, Brother Robert of Git, and also the knights Marsirius and Andrew of Anjou and Albert the Lombard, the lord Hugh himself gave, granted, and delivered freely and peacefully, to be possessed in perpetuity, to the convent of the Holy Sepulchre through the hands of the canons of that church—namely lord Bernard the cantor and Master Achilles—in the church of Saint Joseph itself [Note: [Col. 1161] B reads *Iosep*]. All of us, by common assent and good will, approved, consented to, and confirmed the same donation.

The aforementioned Hugh, satisfying our will and consulting the advantage of our church, gave us in exchange part of the *turonium* that lies below Mirabel at the Deaf Fountains, and two ploughlands in the same territory.

[Col. 1162D] Therefore, so that this may remain ratified and unshaken, we confirm it by the impression of our seal and by the testimony of the brothers whose names are written below.

I, Herbert, abbot, have subscribed, making the sign of the cross [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *faciendo*].

**The brothers:**

Bonetus. Nicholas. Martinus. Harduinus. Martinus. Robert. Lambert. Laurence [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Lauriencius*]. Peter. William. Raymond [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Raimundus*]. Albert. Ebroin. Humbert. John. Garin [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Guarinus*]. Anselm. Bernard. Christian. Gerard. John. Saberandus [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Siberandus*]. Galand.

[Col. 1163A] For the confirmation of this privilege we affix the seal of lord Constantine, bishop of Ramla, together with our wax seal.

This was done in the year 1160 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the eighth indiction, while Baldwin, fourth king of the Latins, was reigning.

**LXV [Note: [Col. 1163] A, fol. 63 verso; B, fol. 70 verso]. PRIVILEGE OF HUGH OF IBELIN, CONCERNING THE GIFT OF BETHEL [Note: [Col. 1163] These two headings are absent from B].**

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Hybelino*], lord of Ramla by the grace of God [Note: [Col. 1163] Supplied from B], for the remedy of the souls both of myself and of my parents, and in return for the great benefit conferred upon me by my brothers, the canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, in freeing me from captivity, give, grant [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *concedo, dono*], and deliver to lord Nicholas [Note: [Col. 1163] Supplied from B], prior, and to the convent of that church, in the presence of lord Amalric the patriarch and lord Constantine, bishop of Ramla, whatever my father Barisan had given as alms to the church of Saint Joseph at Bethel—namely Bethel itself and Beze, which is called Bazarim [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Bazerim*], with two ploughlands of land and five days’ work of land [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *iornatis*] that the brothers of Saint Joseph were claiming there, as well as the tower and whatever they had built there.

The abbot Herbert of that church and all his brothers willingly consenting and granting these things, I gave them, in exchange for the aforesaid alms of my father, according to their will and judgment, in the territory of Mirabel a portion of the *turonium* that lies above the Deaf Fountains, and in the same territory two ploughlands of land, which are known to be much better and more convenient for them. For Bethel, because their boundaries there could not be extended, as I have often heard from them, could benefit them either not at all or only little [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads “either little or not at all”].

The church that they had built there, both because of the lord patriarch’s command and because of my request [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *peticione*] and entreaties, the abbot and his brothers, by common assent, granted and gave to the aforesaid prior and convent of the Holy Sepulchre.

[Col. 1164A] Therefore, let my brothers, the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre, freely and peacefully possess all the aforesaid things in perpetuity, my brothers Baldwin and Barisan, and my sisters Ermengard [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Ermengarda*] and Stephania, consenting to and confirming them; and let them have free power to do with them whatever they wish [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *faciendi*], without opposition from me, my heirs, or my parents [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads “my heirs or my parents”].

Therefore, so that this may remain ratified and unshaken, I strengthen it by the impression of the seal of my grandfather Baldwin, the first lord of Ramla of the Latins.

This was done on the advice of lord Philip of Naples, who himself is also a witness [Note: [Col. 1163] Supplied from B].

[Col. 1164B] **The witnesses are also:**

Ralph, archdeacon of Jerusalem. Bernard, monk. John, dean of Saint George. Baldwin, archdeacon. Gilbert [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Gillebertus*], cantor. Franco. Master Anschetinus. Azo, Ralph, and Erchenbert [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Erchembaldus*], chaplains. Rainald of Saint Gallericus [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Valericus*]. Marsirius of Ramla. Andrew of Anjou. Albert the Lombard. Humbert of Bar. Simon the Red. Herbert the Crooked. John Raimundi.

Barisan also testifies to this and confirms it. He also confirms the sales of the estates—namely Odomamel, Dersabe, Corteiz, Hodabet, and Dermasun—which I, the aforesaid Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Hybelino*], his brother [Note: [Col. 1163] These two words are absent from B], sold to the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre.

[Col. 1164C] **The witnesses to my aforesaid donation and to my brother’s confirmation are [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads: “The witnesses to my aforesaid donation and to the confirmation of my brother, etc.”; in A the words *testes sunt* are placed after the signatures]:**

Ordelez [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Ordeletz*]. Philip of Caphran [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Caphrano*]. Pagan of Rohais. George Arrabit [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Arrabiz*]. Adam Dorniel. Osmund. Pagan of Isengrin [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Hisengrino*]. Garin. Jordan of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *Hybelino*]. Ralph and Peter, chaplains.

These things were done in the year 1160 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the eighth indiction, while Baldwin, the fourth king of Jerusalem of the Latins, was reigning.

For the confirmation and strengthening of this privilege, I, Constantine, bishop of Ramla, affix my seal.

**LXVI [Note: [Col. 1163] A, fol. 64 recto; A, fol. 92 recto]. PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE REBELLION MADE BY THE PRIOR AND CANONS OF MOUNT OLIVET AGAINST THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE, AND CONCERNING THE SATISFACTION AND JUDGMENT IMPOSED UPON THEM [Note: [Col. 1163] B reads *iudicio*].**

[Col. 1164D]

It is written: “Corruptible flesh weighs down the soul, and the earthly dwelling presses down the mind that thinks upon many things.” Therefore, considering [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Intuentes*] the condition [Note: [Col. 1165] Correct *conditionum* to *conditionem*] of human minds [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *mencium*], that the deeds of past or present affairs are easily removed from all memory unless they are recorded by certain signs, we brothers in Christ, the canons established in the church of the Most Holy Resurrection of Jesus Christ in Jerusalem under the rule of the venerable [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *venerabili*] father Patriarch Fulcher, deemed it useful to commit eternally to memory, for both the present and succeeding generations, the rebellion and indignation that our fellow canons in the church of Mount Olivet, together with their prior Aimeric, attempted to undertake against their mother, namely the aforesaid [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *prefatam*] church, whose sons and servants we are, though unworthy; and the satisfaction for their presumption, which they were justly compelled to provide before the Most Holy Sepulchre by the judgment of the archbishops—namely Peter of Tyre, Baldwin of Caesarea, and Letard of Nazareth; of the bishops Ralph of Bethlehem, Constantine of Lydda, Reiner of Sebaste, Frederick of Acre [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Achonensis*], Albert of Tiberias, Adam of Paneas, Amalric of Sidon, and Mainard of Beirut [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Berithensis*]; and of the abbots Geoffrey of the Temple of the Lord, Peter of Saint Mary of Jehoshaphat, Amilius of Saint Mary Latin, R. . . of Saint Samuel [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Sancti*], Herbert of Saint Abacuc, Engelran, prior of Mount Zion, Hugh, prior of the Temple of the Lord, and Ralph, prior of Sebaste.

In the year 1156 from the incarnation of the Lord, when lord Patriarch Fulcher was traveling to Rome because of the conflicts of certain of our parishioners who were wickedly and unjustly rebelling against the Holy Sepulchre of the Lord, on the arrival of the day of the holy Ascension, following as far as we were able the custom of my predecessors [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *nostrorum*] who had been before us and also the ordinances of the patriarchs, we came with the solemn arrangement of our procession, according to custom, to the church of Mount Olivet, intending to perform there the station due on that day with the full service.

When the canons of that place, with their prior, the aforementioned Aimeric, saw this, they took our arrival badly and opposed us face-to-face [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *faciem*], saying that they absolutely did not wish to allow us to have any dignity or station [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *stacionem*] in their church, whether by right or by custom, in the patriarch’s absence. They compared themselves in every respect with the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre and protested that they owed it no subjection.

At that time and place we remained silent, and out of reverence for so great a solemnity patiently endured our rejection. Thus we returned to our church and awaited the arrival of the patriarch.

When he had returned from Rome in due course, and was seated in a full assembly of bishops and other dignitaries, as well as clergy and people, we laid before him, by way of complaint, the course of events concerning the presumption and indignation of the canons mentioned above. After hearing our complaint against them and their response, it was decided by the counsel of the dignitaries that they should come barefoot [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *discalciati*] from Mount Olivet to the Lord’s Sepulchre.

But lord Peter of Tyre [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Tyrensis*], Adam of Paneas, and Mainard of Beirut [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Berithensis*], moved by humility and piety, came with the aforesaid [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *prefato*] prior of Mount Olivet and with his canons—namely Guido, Bonitius [Note: [Col. 1165] *Bonicio*], John, Berruier, Durand, Odo, and Zachariah—barefoot [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *nudis pedibus*] into our full chapter to make satisfaction on their behalf.

It was also established and, from the time when the worship of God [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *servitium Dei*] was renewed in holy Jerusalem after the expulsion of the Saracens, it was recalled by all the persons—archbishops, bishops, and others—who had attended the aforesaid assembly before the patriarch, that this is the dignity, custom, and right of the Most Holy Sepulchre: whenever it makes a procession to any church within or outside the city of Jerusalem—as on the day of the Purification to the Temple, on the day of the Ascension to Mount Olivet, on Pentecost to Mount Zion, and on the day of the Assumption of Saint Mary to the Valley of Jehoshaphat—the convent of the Holy Sepulchre is to have precedence in arranging the entire service, with the full dignity of its station. Thus, if the patriarch is absent, the prior of the Holy Sepulchre shall sing Mass in each church on these solemnities and preach [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *faciat*] to the people, unless he wishes to entrust this to someone else.

**LXVII [Note: [Col. 1165] A, fol. 65 verso; B, fol. 75 verso]. PRIVILEGE OF WILLIAM, ARCHBISHOP OF TYRE [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Tyrensis*], CONCERNING THE GIFT OF THE CHURCH OF SAINT MARY, WHICH IS AT TYRE.**

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

I, William, by the grace of God archbishop of the church of Tyre [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Tyrie*], the second of the Latins, give and firmly and irrevocably grant to the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre and to my brother canons serving God there the church of Saint Mary at Tyre [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Tyri*], to be possessed in perpetuity through the hand of lord Patriarch Stephen and William, prior of that same Lord’s Most Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1165] Absent from B].

And because I wished this donation to remain ratified and secure—having made it with sound counsel and with the assent and consent of the canons, my sons in our church—I deemed it appropriate to record it on the page of this present document, seal it with my seal, and strengthen it by the testimony of the worthy men who were present at this donation: namely the lord patriarch, the clergy, the king, and his barons.

This was done publicly in the city of Acre [Note: [Col. 1165] B reads *Achon*] in the year 1129 from the incarnation of the Lord, with lord Stephen presiding as patriarch of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, and Baldwin II reigning as king of Jerusalem.

The witnesses to this donation, who had assembled in the aforesaid [Note: [Col. 1167] B reads *prefata*] city, are therefore:

First, lord Patriarch Stephen. William, archbishop of Nazareth. Anselm, bishop of Bethlehem. Acard, prior of the Temple of the Lord; Arnald, prior of Mount Zion; and Adelelm [Note: [Col. 1167] B reads *Adalelmus*], prior of the church of Nazareth. Hugh, canon of Bethlehem. Peter, Walter, John, and Hugh, canons of the church of Tyre. John, provost of the church of Acre [Note: [Col. 1167] B reads *Achon*].

[Col. 1167B] **Of the laymen:**

King Baldwin II. Fulk, count of Anjou. William of Bury. Hugh of Joppa [Note: [Col. 1167] *Iopensis*]. Barisan. Garin [Note: [Col. 1167] B reads *Guarinus*], viscount of Tyre, and many others.

**LXVIII [Note: [Col. 1167] A, fol. 66 recto; C, fol. 74 recto]. PRIVILEGE OF PETER, ARCHBISHOP OF TYRE, CONCERNING THE TITHE OF THE ESTATE OF DERINE.**
In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit [Note: [Col. 1167] The words “of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” are missing in B.], amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Peter, by divine favor and not by merit archbishop of the church of Tyre, and the chapter of that same church, grant to God and to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, and to its venerable prior, Lord Nicholas, and to his entire convent, the whole tithe of a certain estate called Derina, from everything that they now possess either personally or through their men, to hold freely; and if thereafter they should acquire anything which they say belongs to the aforesaid estate, let it remain included in the same grant. Likewise, we permit them to hold in perpetuity another tithe from a certain garden, which is separately enclosed by a *berquilium* between the wall of Tyre and its outer wall, in the same manner. We also grant them the church of Saint Mary, which was formerly the first see of Tyre, without prejudice to the dignity of our mother church. The witnesses of this matter are:

A[malric], patriarch, in whose presence this was granted. Lord Amicus, provost of the Holy Sepulchre. Lord Gotofred [Note: [Col. 1167] B, Gottifridus.], treasurer [Note: [Col. 1167] B, thesaurarius.]. Lord Reynald, Master Girard, and Lord William, canons of Tyre.

In the year 1161 of Our Lord, with the ninth indiction.

### LXIX [Note: [Col. 1167] A, fol. 66r; B, fol. 74v.] Another privilege of Peter, archbishop of Tyre [Note: [Col. 1167] Missing in B.], concerning the testimony of the division made at the castle of Feniculus with G[ilduin], abbot of the Valley of Jehoshaphat.

[Col. 1168A]

I, Peter, by the grace of God humble archbishop of the church of Tyre, make known and testify to present and future generations the agreement made and confirmed in good peace between me, at that time prior of the most glorious Sepulchre, and G[ilduin], abbot of Saint Mary of the Valley of Jehoshaphat, concerning the dispute over their land and ours at the castle called Feniculus, which was settled in this manner:

The aforesaid abbot G[ilduin], with some of his monks, and we, with some of the canons, came to the land on the appointed day. Through the mediation of Lord B[aldwin], archbishop of Caesarea, and on his advice, we summoned good and faithful men of Caesarea who knew the boundaries of both lands with certainty. After they had been summoned, we entrusted to their good faith, on both sides, the task of showing the division of the two lands. They traversed the land in a straight line and in agreement, from the palm-tree to the *carrobletum*, [from the *carrobletum* to the reed-bed] [Note: [Col. 1167] Supplied from B.], from the [Note: [Col. 1167] A reads *ad*] reed-bed [Note: [Col. 1167] B, *conneto*.] to the river plain.

Afterward, however, out of generosity and good will, and so that perpetual peace might henceforth remain between our churches, we granted them the land beyond the reed-bed, which is almost tongue-shaped, so that the division from the reed-bed transversely to the river plain might become fixed and firm. This division was made in the following manner, and, so that it might remain firm and stable forever, it was granted on both sides in the presence of Lord B[aldwin], archbishop of Caesarea [Note: [Col. 1167] Everything that follows is missing in B.], and of the other good men whose names are written below:

Manasses. Gervasius. Aeris of the Area. Emelinus, knight. Arnald Shortcloak. Georgius Herminius. Rainald of Belgrant, and many others.

This privilege was made in the year 1162 from the incarnation of the Lord, and in the thirteenth year of my archbishopric.

### LXX [Note: [Col. 1167] A, fol. 66v; B, fol. 75v.] Privilege of Evremar, archbishop of Caesarea, concerning the tithes of the estate of Deffeisse.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

In the year 1129 from the incarnation of Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the seventh indiction, I, Evremar, by the grace of God archbishop of Caesarea in Palestine, desiring to order ecclesiastical rights to the praise and glory of almighty God [Col. 1168D] and to the honor of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, insofar as my reason permits, and wishing, by ordering them, to advance them from good to better, seeing that, because of the many circumstances arising and opposing them, they needed assistance and counsel according to time and place from both the lords and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, deemed it fitting to provide for and advise them [Col. 1169A] as a companion [*contubermo*; the reading is uncertain].

Therefore, for the benefit and honor of our aforesaid church and of our sons, the canons serving God therein, both present and future, with their agreement and counsel I give and grant to the aforesaid brothers of the Lordly Sepulchre, and for their alms—that is, for the food of the poor and their refreshment—the tithes belonging to our church from the estate called Deffeisse [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Deffiesse.], both in grain and in animals and in all other things subject to tithe.

But so that the document of this grant and donation may remain firm, approved, and stable for those now living and for posterity, we order it to be written under the attestation of our name and marked with our leaden seal. If anyone should presume to annul or invalidate this gift, let him be struck by the sword of blessed Peter [Col. 1169B] and remain subject to perpetual anathema. The witnesses of this matter are [Note: [Col. 1169] B, “the witnesses of this matter are”]:

Rainerius, archdeacon. Boniface [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Bonifacius.], Aymo [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Aimo.], Gosbertus, Alexander, canons [Note: [Col. 1169] B, canonici.] and sons of our church. Aymericus [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Aimericus.], canon and almoner of the Holy Sepulchre. Albertus. Baldwin. Richard, seneschal of Caesarea.

This charter was made at Caesarea, while Baldwin II was reigning as king of Jerusalem, venerable Stephen was presiding there as patriarch, and William was prior for the second time.

### LXXI [Note: [Col. 1169] A, fol. 67r; B, fol. 76v.] Privilege of Walter, lord of Caesarea, concerning the gift and grant of the estate of Fraisse [Note: [Col. 1169] B, of Fiaisse.].

[Col. 1169C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Since disagreement frequently arises in donations of property, therefore I, Walter, lord of Caesarea, have decided to hand down to the memory of all, present and future, and have likewise determined that the donation should remain forever approved [and] [Note: [Col. 1169] Supplied from B.] firm, inviolable, and fixed: namely, one half of the estate called Fiaisse, together with the adjoining lands, which my father Eustace Granerius gave to the Lordly Sepulchre and to Prior Girard, and which I afterward augmented for the regular canons serving God there [Note: [Col. 1169] B, “serving.”], for the salvation of my soul and of my father and our parents, both living and dead.

This was done according to the way my father divided the territory from the estate of Saint Mary of the Valley of Jehoshaphat, the estate of Saint Peter of Caesarea, the estate of the Forest, the estate of Sabarinus, the estate of Saint John of Sebaste, and from my estate called Bufles; and according to the way I myself marked it and caused it to be indicated in certain places by crosses made on rocks, and in others by stones fixed in the ground. And [Note: [Col. 1169] A adds *in*, which would make the construction of the sentence entirely different.] the written charter of remembrance and donation, both of my father and of myself, no one objecting, [Col. 1170A] has been issued and confirmed with my seal and with the witnesses written below.

In the year 1145 from the incarnation of Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the eighth indiction, the witnesses being:

Lord Bernard, bishop of Sidon [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Sydonensis.]; Rorgon, bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achonensis.]; Oston of Saint-Omer [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Audomaro.], and Ralph of Patinges, brothers of the Knights Templar; Robert of Franco Loco; Eustace Escoffel; Arnald Costa; Rainerius of Cossia; George the Armenian; Geoffrey of Port; Simon of Castelliono; Peter Basso.

### LXXII [Note: [Col. 1169] A, fol. 67v; B, fol. 77r.] Privilege of John, bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achonensis.], concerning permission to build a church in the city of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achon.] and concerning the gift of the church situated in the territory of the estate called Amimas [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Minas.].

[Col. 1170B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

John, by the grace of God bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achon.], sends greetings to his dearest brothers and fellow canons [Note: [Col. 1169] B, fellow canons.], Peter, prior of the church of the Lord’s Resurrection, and the other brothers professing canonical life in that church, present and future.

Just as, laboring in the Lord’s vineyard through the administration of pastoral care, we command you to devote yourselves to the advancement of souls, so, for the sake of ecclesiastical usefulness, it is fitting that we commend fraternal grace and charity by words and deeds, as an example to posterity. Therefore, assenting to your just and reasonable petitions, Prior Peter, and those of your brothers, [Col. 1170C] [Note: [Col. 1169] B, *peticionibus*.] we grant you permission to build a church in honor of the Lord’s Sepulchre in the city of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achon.], specifically on the land which you possess by the gift of Lambert Aals.

To this gift, for the lasting remembrance of us, we add by episcopal authority another church in the territory of an estate called Amimas, three miles distant from the city of Acre [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Achon.], together with everything belonging to it. We give and decree that you may possess both churches freely and peacefully in perpetuity, without prejudice to episcopal rights.

And so that this gift of our free benevolence, to which the assent and counsel of our chapter have contributed, may remain approved and undisturbed, we order this present document concerning the matters stated above to be strengthened both by the placing of our seal [Col. 1170D] and by the testimony of those who were present [Note: [Col. 1169] B, “who attended.”]. Their names are as follows:

Adam, archdeacon of our church. Marinus, Nicholas, John of Poitiers [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Pictaviensis.], priests. Gocelinus [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Gozelinus.] and Jonathan, canons. Dodo, Iterius, priests. Peter, deacon. Stephen. Leo. John of Bru[II]dusio. William Capperons [Note: [Col. 1169] B, Capperuns.]. Baldwin, chancellor of the patriarch of Jerusalem, and many others [Note: [Col. 1171] B, “other many men.”].

This document was inscribed in the year 1138 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the first indiction.

### LXXIII [Note: [Col. 1171] A, fol. 68v; B, fol. 77v.] Privilege of Roger, bishop of Ramla, concerning the gift and grant of the estates of Capharuth, Gith, Kefrescilta, and Porphilia.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

It is clear that what many legitimate witnesses attest by hearing and sight ought to be granted and held approved and firm. Since this matter proceeds in that manner, and since the bishop’s inviolable judgment remains confirmed by the presence of his clergy and canons [Note: [Col. 1171] B, canons.], I, Roger, by God’s providence bishop of Ramla, with the counsel and assent of the entire chapter of Saint George—namely, Ralph, then archdeacon, and the other canons—grant and confirm to that same church of the Most Holy Sepulchre what I gave and confirmed to the church of the Lordly Sepulchre, namely to Lord William, its prior, and the other canons of the Holy Sepulchre and their successors.

Specifically, I grant and confirm to the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre, namely to Lord Peter, its prior, and the other canons of the most glorious Sepulchre and their successors, two estates from the property of Saint George, with all their appurtenances, to possess in perpetuity by hereditary right. One of these estates is called Capharuth, and the other Gith [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Gith.]. I granted these estates to the aforesaid church of the Lordly Sepulchre in the presence of Lord Guarmund, patriarch, who expressly approved the act.

Furthermore, since it is permissible for one venerable church to make an exchange of even immovable property with another venerable church, with the patriarch’s permission if both parties approve, likewise, with the counsel and assent of the entire chapter of Saint George, I give and confirm to the aforesaid church of the Most Holy Sepulchre, namely to Lord Peter, its prior, and the other canons of the Holy Sepulchre and their successors, two other estates, Kefrescilta and Porphilia, from the property of Saint George, with all their appurtenances, and one half of the tithes of the crops of those estates and the entire tithe of all other things [Col. 1171D].

In exchange, I confirm to the aforesaid church the estates Capharuth [Note: [Col. 1171] Capharuth.] and Gith, with all their appurtenances, and one half of the tithes of the crops of those estates and the entire tithe of all other things, on this condition: that the aforesaid Lord Peter, prior, and the other canons of the Holy Sepulchre give, grant, and confirm to the church of Saint George—to me, that is, and to my successors and our canons—the tithes of Arnold’s Castle and the tithes of the estate of the Hospital, called Bulbul, to possess in perpetuity.

These estates were then deserted and somewhat wasteland, and, since they did not burden the church’s interests but rather, given under the aforesaid condition, were beneficial, I gave and granted them in the presence of Lord William, patriarch, who expressly approved the act, in such a way that none of my successors who might later be installed in that church of Saint George could thereafter bring any claim concerning them; yet the Christian faith and the half of the tithes of the crops belonging to them are preserved.

This gift was made in the year 1136 of the Lord’s incarnation, in the fourteenth indiction, on the Kalends of November, while Fulk, third king of the Franks, was reigning in Jerusalem. The legitimate witnesses of this gift are:

Anselm, bishop of Bethlehem. John, bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Achon.]. Achard, prior of the Temple of the Lord. [Col. 1172B] Arnald, prior of Mount Zion. Henry, prior of Mount Olivet. Guy, prior of Saint Abraham [Note: [Col. 1171] B, “prior of Saint Abraham.”].

And from the chapter of Saint George:

William son of Thurold. Jordan. Baldwin. Hugh, and many others.

Therefore, if anyone should attempt to violate this grant of our gift, or the assent and confirmation of the lord patriarch, let him be struck by the sword of anathema until he repents and makes satisfaction. So be it, so be it, amen, amen.

### LXXIV [Note: [Col. 1171] A, fol. 69r; B, fol. 79r.] Privilege of William of Buris concerning the gift of two estates, Gebub [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Gebul.] and Helkar [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Helcar.], and concerning the gift of a fishery.

[Col. 1172C]

In the year 1132 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the tenth indiction, while William was presiding as patriarch of the church of Jerusalem and Fulk, third king of the Franks, was reigning, I, William of Buris, for the salvation of my soul and of my parents, with the assent and grant of the aforesaid king and of my nephews Ralph of Ysis and Simon [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Symon.], give and grant to the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre and to the canons regularly serving God there two estates, namely Gebul and Helkar, and all the land belonging to them, to be possessed freely and in perpetuity.

The length of this land extends from the mountains across the plain as far as the Jordan [Note: [Col. 1171] B, “is extended.”]; its width extends from the boundary of Bethsan and Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1171] B, Tyberiadis.] as far as the hollow nearest the estate called Huxenia, and it indicates and directs [Col. 1172D] the straight boundary line toward the aforesaid mountains and river.

Moreover, I grant to my aforesaid canon brothers all my fisheries, free and exempt, for eight days each year, namely from Septuagesima until Easter, to be taken in whichever week they wish. This condition applies: if, during the days on which they begin to fish, the sea is disturbed and they are unable to fish as they wish, the benefit shall be paid and compensated to them on other days which they choose.

I also grant them annually the entire labor-service and aid of all my fishermen for one day. In addition, I likewise give them a boat to have continually fishing on the Sea of Galilee. The witnesses of this donation are:

Lord William, patriarch, and the aforesaid Fulk, king. William, archbishop of Nazareth. Anselm, bishop of Bethlehem. Peter, prior of the Holy Sepulchre. Achard, prior of the Temple. Arnald, prior of Mount Zion.

From Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1173] B, Tyriade.] and its territory the witnesses are:

Goffred, chaplain of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1173] B, Tyberiadis.]. Guala, viscount. Guarmund. Pagan of Mont Royal. Mangoth. Ricolf. Hugh of Badalone. Thomas of Bethsan.

[Col. 1173B] And so that the aforesaid gift may be firm, I confirm this present charter with my seal.

I, Fulk, by the grace of God king of Jerusalem, confirm the aforesaid gifts with my seal.

### LXXV [Note: [Col. 1173] A, fol. 70r; B, fol. 80r.] Privilege of Bertrand, master of the Knights Templar, concerning the remission of 150 bezants [Note: [Col. 1173] B, bizanciorum.] which we used to pay annually to the aforesaid order.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, future and present, that I, Bertrand, by the grace of God master of the Knights Templar, with the common assent and will of our entire chapter, remit and grant to Nicholas, by that same grace prior of the Lordly Sepulchre, and to the entire chapter of the canons of that Sepulchre, to hold freely and peacefully in perpetuity, 150 bezants which they used to pay annually for our support.

We make this remission and grant to them for three estates with all their appurtenances, both lands and peasants. If we are able to acquire elsewhere any peasants belonging to these estates, they grant them to us, except for those peasants [Note: [Col. 1173] B, “those peasants.”] whom they have in their own estates.

The names of these estates are as follows: the first is called Bubin, the second Caphardin, and the third Betelcanzir [Note: [Col. 1173] B, Bethelcanzir.].

An agreement and settlement was thus made between us and them: for this donation—namely, of the three estates which they grant to us—the aforesaid 150 bezants shall no longer be demanded either by us or by our successors, [Col. 1173D] because the church of the glorious Sepulchre shall remain forever peacefully and freely exempt from this exaction.

Therefore our aforesaid canon brothers of the Lordly Sepulchre grant to us and to our successors, to hold forever, freely and peacefully, the aforesaid three estates—namely Bubin, Caphardin, and Betelcanzir—subject to their half of the tithe, as they possess it in the case of the other tithes, without any opposition from them or their successors.

If anyone should wish to bring a claim against us concerning any of the three aforesaid estates, they must secure peace for us from all men. And so that this may remain approved and undisturbed at all times, we strengthen and confirm it by the document of this present charter and by the impression of our seal; we also corroborate it by the attestations of those whose names are written below:

William, namely, seneschal; Brother Geoffrey Fulcher; Brother Thomas Hermoin; Brother Berengar of Castello Perso; Brother Walter of Beirut; Brother Odo of Avalon; Brother Bonet; Brother Mainard; Brother Amalric of Berno; Brother Geoffrey, chaplain; Brother John, chaplain; Brother Ralph of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1173] Tyberiadensis.]; Brother Hugh of Corbel; Brother Leo; Brother Stephen of Jerusalem; Brother Hugh of Vaudemon; Brother William of Philisteda; [Col. 1174B] Brother Brice; Brother Ysmion.

This was done in the presence of Lord Amalric, patriarch, who himself is also a witness.

### LXXVI [Note: [Col. 1173] A, fol. 70v; B, fol. 80v.] Another privilege of the same concerning the grant of tithes.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

We wish it to be known to all, future and present, that I, Bertrand, by God’s grace called master of the Knights Templar [Note: [Col. 1173] B, “called master.”], and the entire convent of the aforesaid order, grant to Lord Nicholas, prior of the Lordly Sepulchre, and to the entire chapter of the canons of that Sepulchre, one half of all the tithes which we possess or shall possess in places belonging to them or to their church—namely, of wine and oil, wheat and rye, barley, oats, beans, chickpeas, lentils, sesame, rice, and millet—to be faithfully rendered annually to them and to their successors, without any claim or opposition from us or our successors and without any deceitful device.

Of all other things, they have granted us permission to have and possess the tithes in full, as is contained in the privilege which they made for us. If we should grant any estate on lease for grain or for bezants [Note: [Col. 1173] B, bizanciis.], we shall give them the tithes in the manner stated above.

And so that this may always remain approved and stable, we strengthen and confirm it by the writing of this present document and by the impression of our seal, [Col. 1174D] and we also corroborate it by the attestations of those whose names are written below [Note: [Col. 1173] B, “attestations.”]:

William, namely, seneschal; Brother Geoffrey Fulcher; Brother Thomas Hermoin; Brother Berengar of Castello Perso; Brother Walter of Beirut; Brother Odo of Avalon; Brother Bonet; Brother Mainard; Brother Amalric of Berno; Brother Geoffrey, chaplain; Brother John, chaplain; Brother Ralph of Tiberias; Brother Hugh of Corbel; Brother Leo; Brother Stephen of Jerusalem; [Col. 1175A] Brother Hugh of Vaudemon; Brother William of Philisteda; Brother Brice; Brother Ysmion.

### LXXVII [Note: [Col. 1175] A, fol. 71r; B, fol. 81v.] Privilege of William, third prior, concerning the fief of Saint Lazarus.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity.

I, William, by the grace of God third prior of the Lordly Sepulchre, have taken care that this writing and many other matters be preserved for our successors.

A certain Peter, a brother of Saint Lazarus and of the Lordly Sepulchre, when he was dying, left his daughter, who was under age, in the care and counsel of the canons of the aforesaid Sepulchre, together with her mother, his wife. He mercifully asked that they take pity on his daughter, who was not yet of age, at the time of her marriage, specifically so that the fief of Saint Lazarus, which he had held from them while alive, might be given in marriage to the girl, provided only that the girl’s husband, through the canons’ gracious concession, should fulfill the service which her father had rendered, and that the girl’s mother, meanwhile, should be supported from the same fief, if this accorded with their counsel.

Therefore, after a long time, yielding to the petition [Note: [Col. 1175] B, “petition.”] of the deceased brother, we sought to lawfully join the marriageable girl to one of our household servants, named Peter. When her utterly wicked mother heard this, after long scoldings and insults directed against us, she refused to agree to our will and counsel concerning her daughter, grieving that she would lose the fief during her lifetime.

Accordingly, after taking counsel with Lord Patriarch S[tephen] in the chapter, the brothers caused the daughter and her mother to come before him. I addressed the girl in the presence of the patriarch, the convent, her mother, her stepfather, her godparents, and many other laymen, asking whether she wished to consent to this for her honor and salvation. She replied that under no circumstances would she marry that man Peter against her mother’s will, and that she would rather seek bread by begging from door to door than, after abandoning her mother, accept him as her husband.

During this proceeding, in the presence of those standing by, she returned the fief into our hands, never again to seek it, and only on this condition: that her mother, while alive, should possess the fief with her stepfather.

Since the girl had thus relinquished the fief, we showed this mercy at the supplication of the stepfather and the mother: we would receive their only son, whom they had, into the church of the Holy Sepulchre after the death of his father and mother, to have food [Col. 1175D] and clothing.

But if anyone should presume, setting aside the valid decision of the chapter, to restore the aforesaid fief to the girl and to deprive our church of its possession, let him be subject to divine vengeance. The witnesses of this settlement are those who were present:

Anselm, cantor. Azo. Gislebert. Peter Bernard. Gaudentius [Note: [Col. 1175] B, Gaudencius.]. Peter, almoner. Aimericus. Geoffrey Acus. Peter of Vendôme. Berengar Parvus.

This settlement and charter were made in the year 1129 from the incarnation [Col. 1176A] of the Lord, in the seventh indiction, while S[tephen], venerable patriarch, was presiding in the pontifical see of Jerusalem, and he marked it with his own seal, while Baldwin II was reigning there.

### LXXVIII [Note: [Col. 1175] A, fol. 71v; B, fol. 82v.] Privilege of the same concerning the purchase of a vineyard which belonged to Peter of Saint-Gautier.

Since, because of the burden of human flesh which we observe daily with mortal eyes, we easily consign things to oblivion [Note: [Col. 1175] B, “with the eyes.”], I, William, by the grace of God [prior] [Note: [Col. 1175] Supplied from B.] of the Lordly Sepulchre, have taken care that the matters which are evident and will be beneficial to our brothers be preserved in writing for our successors.

I make known to all the faithful that I purchased from Peter of Saint-Gautier, his wife, and his son a certain vineyard, enclosed together with the adjoining land, which appears on the left-hand side to those coming to Jerusalem as they leave Mahumeria, in the valley. I purchased it with the money [Note: [Col. 1175] B, *pecunia*.] of our alms, to be possessed in perpetuity for the needs of the poor, for the price of 140 bezants, free from every claim and customary due except the tithe, which belonged to our right and which we afterward remitted in the chapter by the common counsel of the brothers, who ordered the present charter to be marked with their leaden seal.

The witnesses of this purchase are:

Goisbert, provost. Aimericus, almoner. Peter Clement. Anselm, chaplain of Mahumeria. Geoffrey Acus. Peter of Joppa. Peter Guitart. Bernard, who had Peter of Saint-Gautier’s daughter. [Col. 1176C] Roger Lombard, and many others.

This charter was made in the year 1129 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the eighth indiction, in the second year of the patriarchate of the venerable Stephen, patriarch of Jerusalem, while King Baldwin II was reigning in that city.

I, Peter of Saint-Gautier, seller in this matter, confirm this charter. I, Audearz [Note: [Col. 1175] B, Audeartz.], Peter’s wife, ratify it [Note: [Col. 1175] B, “confirm it.”]. I, Andrew, their son, grant and confirm it. I, Petronilla, their daughter, grant and confirm it.

### LXXIX [Note: [Col. 1175] A, fol. 72r; B, fol. 83r.] Privilege of Prior Peter concerning the vineyard which belonged to Sister Odiarda.

[Col. 1176D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, [amen] [Note: [Col. 1175] Supplied from B.].

I, Peter, by the grace of God prior of the Lordly Sepulchre, together with all the brothers, make known to present and future generations that a certain woman named Odiarda [Note: [Col. 1175] B, Odiardam.], resident of Mahumeria, when she became a free sister of the convent of the Holy Sepulchre, handed over to that convent for possession one vineyard which she had.

After her death, her son Andrew had held it by force and against our will for a long time. By the judgment of the archbishops Robert of Nazareth and Fulcher of Tyre, and of the bishops Bernard of Sidon [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Sydoniensis.], Rorgon of Ptolemais, Helias of Tiberias [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Helie.], and Roger of Ramla, and of the others who were present [Note: [Col. 1177] B, “who had been present.”], it was adjudicated to us, together with the fruits he had received from it.

But since we ought to devote ourselves to works of mercy and ought not to repay evil with evil, out of consideration for piety we remitted to Andrew the fruits he had received and granted him the aforesaid vineyard for as long as he lived, on this condition: that he cultivate it well and retain for himself two parts of whatever God might grant him from it, while returning the third part to us, with the share of our tithe wholly reserved [Note: [Col. 1177] B, *porcionem* for *portione*, “share”]. At his death, however, the aforesaid vineyard shall be possessed freely and in perpetuity by our church.

The witnesses of this matter are:

Lambert, subprior. Godefrid, treasurer [Note: [Col. 1177] B, thesaurarius.]. Nicholas, cellarer. Obert of Joppa. Robert of Acre [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Achon.]. Alexander. Bertrand. Ademarus [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Ademarius.]. William, provost. Lambert the Fleming. Aimericus. Fulk. Bertold. John the Englishman.

Of the deacons:

Evrard. Girald. Hugh.

Of the subdeacons:

William of Beirut [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Berytensis.]. John of Poitiers [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Pictavensis.]. William of Spain.

### LXXX [Note: [Col. 1177] A, fol. 72v; B, fol. 84r.] Another privilege of Prior Peter concerning the houses situated above the vaults of the Hospital exchange.

[Col. 1177C]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Peter, by the disposing mercy of God prior of the Lordly Sepulchre, together with the consent and will of all our brothers, the canons, give and grant to Arnulf, son of Beruald [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Bernard.], a Syrian, and to his heirs, to possess by perpetual right, the houses situated above the vaults of the Hospital exchange, which stand above our oven located on the road leading to Mount Zion, and one shop situated beside the aforesaid oven, under an annual rent of nine bezants, payable to the Lordly Sepulchre on the octave of the Lord’s Resurrection.

This is on the condition that if damage should come from below to the upper houses situated above the vaults through our negligence, it shall be repaired by us; but if damage should come from above to the lower houses through his negligence, it shall be repaired by him.

Whatever building he constructs above what has already been built, if at some future time he wishes to sell it to anyone, shall be sold to us for one mark of silver less than he could sell it to others [Col. 1178A]. But if we do not wish to buy it, he shall have the power to sell it to whichever of the burgesses or Syrians [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Syrianorum.] he wishes, provided only that the purchaser pay the established rent, as specified, to the Lordly Sepulchre on the octave of the Lord’s Resurrection, without any exaction from us.

But if he should pass the appointed day, we shall possess the houses and whatever he has made there without opposition. As for the shop beside the oven, which we mentioned above, if damage should come to him through it, we are in no way obliged to answer him for it; rather, it shall be repaired by him.

We entrust the key of his cistern to his authority, so that the keeper of the oven may take from it as much water as is needed for repairing the walls of the oven, if necessary, the benches, and the other uses belonging to the office of the oven.

And so that this grant of ours may retain its force in the present and future, it is strengthened by the protection of our seal together with the witnesses written below:

John Vaccarius. Fulcher, goldsmith. Jordan, cleric. Herbert, money-changer. Saibert. Rainerius of Arrat [Note: [Col. 1177] B, Arraz.]. Peter Bordinus. William, interpreter. John, his son. John of Puy. Robert the Cook.

Done in the year 1144 of the Lord’s incarnation, in the sixth indiction, in the month of April.

Written by the hand of Donatus, deacon and scribe [Col. 1178C] of the Lord’s Sepulchre.

### LXXXI [Note: [Col. 1177] A, fol. 73v and fol. 98r; B, fol. 84v.] Privilege of Prior Amalric concerning the vineyards which Nemes the Syrian and his sons and the sons of his brother [Note: [Col. 1177] The words “and the sons of his brother” are missing in B.] possess at Calandria.

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Whatever [Note: Col. 1177, B reads “Quicquid.”] a prelate of a holy church grants to someone with the consent of his chapter ought prudently to be entrusted to memory through the enduring bond of writing, lest, as time passes, what had previously been settled by his decree later rise in opposition, and disputes and renewed claims perhaps arise from it. Therefore I, Amalric, prior of the Glorious Sepulchre, and the entire community of its canons, grant to Nemes Surianus [Note: Col. 1177, B reads “Syriano.”] and his sons and the sons of his brother Antonius the lands and vineyards that they possess at Calandria, and whatever he, his sons, and the sons of his brother Antonius may subsequently acquire there, to be held by perpetual right, on the following condition [Note: Col. 1177, B reads “condicione.”]: every year they shall faithfully render to the canons of the aforesaid community half the produce of the land, namely of all the crops [Note: restored from B], vineyards, and trees that they have already established or shall establish in the future. And so that this grant of ours may retain the firmness of its validity both in the present and in future times [Col. 1179A], we strengthen this present document with the protection of our seal [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “is strengthened.”]. Here are the witnesses:

Lord Aimeric, subprior; Giraldus, precentor; Raul; William the Norman; Baldwin; Godfrey [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Godefridus”]; Nicholas; Ademarus; Peter of the Sepulchre; William of Beirut; Hugh; John; Ulric; William the Spaniard [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Yyspanus”]; Peter of Latina; Peter of Bologna.

In the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1151, indiction 13.

## LXXXII [Note: A, fol. 74r; B, fol. 85v.]

### PRIVILEGE OF PRIOR PETER CONCERNING THE HOUSE THAT BELONGED TO A CERTAIN MAN NAMED BERNARD AND HIS WIFE AOISE

[Note: In B the heading reads: “Concerning the house of Bernard and his wife Haose, which they sold to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre.”]

In the year from the Lord’s incarnation 1135, indiction 12, on the ides of March [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “of the month”; B also reads “marcii”], while Fulk, third king of the Franks, reigned in Jerusalem and William was serving as patriarch and holding the highest pontifical office, I, Bernard, together with my wife Haoise, without dispute or anyone’s accusation, with the aforesaid patriarch’s approval, sold and conveyed for perpetual possession to Peter, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, and to the canons of the same church and their successors, my house for 200 bezants. It is situated within the walls of Jerusalem, so that they may have free power to sell it, give it away, and do with it whatever they wish [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “to do”].

The aforesaid house has on one side the house of those same canons, which belonged to William the dragoman; on another, the church of Saint Chariton; on another, a public road; and on another, the house of Theodore. Whoever, hateful to God and man and rebellious, should attempt to violate this sale, and in this matter should dare, with evil intent, to bring a lawsuit or accusation against the church of the Holy Sepulchre and its canons, let him, struck by the arrow of anathema [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “struck”], be subjected to perpetual punishment under divine vengeance, and let him pay a pound of gold into the royal treasury. The witnesses to this sale are:

Seibertus [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Seibertus”], judge; Peter, smith; Tustanus; Sinardus [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Sivardus”]; Peter of Petragora; Bernard and Fulk, all of them goldsmiths, were present at this sale; and Ruhelandus Britto [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Britto”].

John, subdeacon [Note: Col. 1179, B adds “who”], wrote this charter [Col. 1179D] with erased letters in the fifth line, in the month and year stated above [Note: Col. 1179, these last five words are absent from B].

## LXXXIII [Note: A, fol. 74v; B, fol. 86r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF BERTOLD CONCERNING THE GIFT OF ALL HIS POSSESSIONS AND THE CONFIRMATION OF THE CHURCH THAT IS IN DEN KENDORF

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all the faithful, clerics and laymen alike, present and future, that I, Bertold, free and of free birth by nature, give and grant to the Lord’s Sepulchre, without any contradiction, for the salvation of my soul and of all my parents, everything that I possess by right on this day, whether fields, vineyards, villages, people, or any other possessions, according to the law of the Swabians, freely and in its entirety, just as I possess it.

The condition is that, for as long as I live, I shall hold the aforesaid possessions as a benefice from Lord William, patriarch, and Peter, prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre; and every year, to confirm the aforesaid gift, I shall publicly pay ten solidi of current coin as rent. If it should come into my mind to leave everything behind and submit myself to religious life in the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem, or in the church that is in Den Kendorf, the patriarch and the prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre who then preside over the church of the Holy Sepulchre shall receive me without any contradiction, and shall freely possess all the aforesaid property.

I also confirm by this present privilege the gift that I formerly gave to the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre, namely the church that is in Den Kendorf, with all its appurtenances. And if, after this first and legal gift, I should wish to sell or give the aforesaid property to anyone, I shall have no power to do so in any way. Confirming all the aforesaid, I subscribe with my own hand:

William.

The witnesses to this gift are noblemen, in whose presence this gift was made. Their names are:

Sifrit, Drutwin, and Dederich, priests; Conrad of Conronbach [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Coronbach”]; Volframus of Bernhusin [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Berenhusim”]; Hugh of Bliningin [Note: Col. 1179, this signature and the following one are absent from B]; Reinbold Hecel of Benrenhusim; Wolthodo [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “Woltodo”] and Rainaldus of Custordingen; Rudolf of Rinuelden; Rudiger of Bodoboro; Arnold of Speyer.

And since I did not have a seal of my own, I obtained the confirmation of all that is written above [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “prescribed”] by the seal of the Lord’s Sepulchre and its canons.

All this was enacted [Note: Col. 1179, B reads “done”] in the chapter of the Lord’s Sepulchre, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1142, indiction 5, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May.

## LXXXIV [Note: A, fol. 75r; B, fol. 87r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF RODERIC CONCERNING THE GIFT OF A CERTAIN VILLAGE CALLED PASSEREL, WITH THIRTY-ONE FARMSTEADS

[Col. 1180D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Instructed by evangelical teaching, our fathers have related to us that the church of the holy Resurrection of the Lord is to be venerated above all others by every faithful person, since our Lord Jesus Christ consecrated it neither with the blood of prophets nor with that of martyrs, but by his presence and by the sprinkling of his own blood, and by the glory of his resurrection [and] ascension [Note: “and” is supplied from B], as though by firm and coherent privileges and an added prerogative, dedicated it to himself as special and proper. Nor is there doubt that whenever honor is shown to that church for the praise and glory of the same Jesus Christ, the Father and the Holy Spirit are likewise honored in it, with whom he is proclaimed to be essentially one God and Lord.

Therefore I, Roderic son of Peter, although unworthy, count of the land that lies near the church of Saint James, for the salvation or remedy of my soul, of my parents, and of my wife, grant to the church of the holy and glorious Sepulchre of the Lord, to be possessed perpetually and without accusation [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “without accusation”], a village called Passerel, situated within the boundaries of a certain castle called Trana, together with its thirty-one farmsteads and their appurtenances.

The condition is that, for as long as I live, I may peacefully possess the aforesaid dwellings with their inhabitants, which, as stated, are called farmsteads among us, and that every year I shall send two marks of silver to the canons, to preserve the stability and memory of this gift of mine to the Lord’s Sepulchre. When, however, I am called to enter upon the way of all flesh, the aforesaid village shall pass freely into the right of the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre and of the brothers dwelling there.

And I, Roderic, when I had visited the Lord’s Sepulchre for the second time, desiring that this gift of my devotion be strengthened by the presence and privilege of Lord William, patriarch, who at that time presided over the church of Jerusalem, summoned witnesses before me and, for the confirmation of this matter, marked with my own hand the sign that this present charter displays at its lower edge. Having affixed the seal of Lord the patriarch, which I obtained with many tears and prayers, I caused the names of the witnesses to be written below. Present at this gift of mine were my friends and countrymen:

Arissa Varich of Ripa Migno; John Aris of the land of Saint Martin of Latron; Roderic, abbot of the land of Pena Regine; John Tirant, brother of the bishop of Toy; Nimuranna of Lunia; Helvitu Sanizh [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “Saniz”] of the land of Saint James; Peter the Spaniard [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “Hyspaniensis”], a brother of the Knights of the Temple; and many others.

[Col. 1181D] This document was made in the year of the Lord 1138, indiction 1.

## LXXXV [Note: A, fol. 76r; B, fol. 88r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF FULK, THIRD KING OF JERUSALEM [Absent from B], WHILE HE WAS GOVERNOR AND BAILIFF OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ANTIOCH, CONCERNING A CERTAIN HOUSE THAT IS BESIDE THE BATH, ONCE CALLED TANCRED’S

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

I, Fulk, by the grace of God third king of the Latins in Jerusalem, and also governor and bailiff of the principality of Antioch and of the daughter of Bohemond the Younger, grant and confirm the gift that Osmund of Mont Garou, canon of Saint Peter, gave to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre for the redemption of his soul: namely, one house with an adjoining bordellum (small house) beside the bath once called Tancred’s.

If anyone should at any time, for any reason, wish to take it away from them or diminish it, let him know that this charter, fortified with our seal, stands as an eternal memorial.

In the year from the Lord’s incarnation 1133 [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “1134”], indiction 12, epact 24 [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “23”].

Given in the palace of Antioch [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “palacio”], by the hand of F[rancon], chancellor, in the presence of the barons listed below:

Rainald Mansuerius [Note: Col. 1181, B reads “Mansuerius”], constable; Leo, duke of Meopoli; Guido of Merlon; Thomas, viscount; Godfrey, son of Renbauth.

## LXXXVI [Note: A, fol. 76r; B, fol. 88r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF THE SAME [FULK] CONFIRMING CERTAIN POSSESSIONS THAT THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE HAS IN ANTIOCH

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

I, Fulk, by the grace of God third Latin king of Jerusalem, and also bailiff and guardian of the principality of Antioch, wish it to be known to all, present and future, that the canons of the Holy Sepulchre of our Lord Jesus Christ brought before the court of Antioch a complaint concerning certain possessions of their church, which they had long since lost in the territory of Antioch. When we carefully investigated this, we discovered through the secretaries and faithful witnesses of the lord of Antioch and of the patriarch that the matter was as they had shown.

Therefore, out of honor and reverence for the holy Cross, which at that time we had brought with us to Antioch for the liberation of Christendom, and for the redemption of the souls of the lords of Antioch—namely, Bohemond the First and the Second—and of the other orthodox faithful, after consultation with the lord patriarch, the bishops, the barons, and likewise the burghers, by the common judgment of all and as justice required, we restore to them in full, as it was found by our secretaries, what had belonged to them. Thus, just as the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre possessed the aforesaid properties in the time of the Greeks, so henceforth it shall possess them in perpetuity, with every accusation removed and all disturbance caused by exaction excluded, in complete tranquility.

The witnesses to this grant of ours are:

B[ernard], patriarch of Antioch; R[alph], archbishop of Mamistra; S[tephen], archbishop of Tarsus; S[lacuna], bishop of Artash; A[nselm], bishop of Bethlehem; A[lacuna], archdeacon; John, canon of Bethlehem.

Among the barons:

R[ainald] Masuerius; G[uy] of Merlo; E[lacuna] of Moszon; G[odfrey] of Guircha; W[lacuna] of Verno; Leo, duke; Thomas, viscount.

Among the burghers:

G[odfrey], son of Raimbald; W[lacuna] of Aversa; B[lacuna] of Berriensis.

Given at Antioch, on the fourth day before the Nones of August, by the hand of Franco, chancellor, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1135, indiction 13, epact 4, concurrent 1.

## LXXXVII [Note: A, fol. 77r; B, fol. 89r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF RISO, CHAPLAIN OF BOHEMOND, PRINCE OF ANTIOCH, CONCERNING THE GIFT OF THE HOUSES THAT HE HAD IN ANTIOCH, WITH THE ORCHARD BELONGING TO THEM

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

[Col. 1183B] Let it be known to all [Note: Col. 1183, absent from B], present and future, sons of holy mother Church, that I, Riso, formerly chaplain of Bohemond, prince of Antioch and son of the great Bohemond, grant to the brothers of the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre and to those who profess or shall profess canonical life therein my houses, together with the orchard belonging to them, which I remember purchasing from William the physician for sixty-four bezants [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “bisantiis”], to be held in perpetuity.

I decree, by this written document and in the presence of Lord William, patriarch of Jerusalem, that they shall enjoy possession of them with the same freedom by which they were given and granted to me by the aforesaid Bohemond, and that this gift of mine shall remain inviolable and valid.

So that the site of these houses may be distinguished with complete certainty from the others [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “recognized”], they are contiguous with the houses of Pontius, treasurer of Antioch, with only a public road lying between them. And so that every scruple of controversy may be removed from this voluntary grant of mine, let it be known to all that I retain in those same houses, for as long as I live, a dwelling in which to reside. I also grant to a certain servant of mine, whom I called away from unbelief to the grace of baptism, the chamber that, by my grant, he possesses for habitation in the aforesaid houses, to hold for as long as he lives and serves me faithfully.

When, however, divine providence and the term that cannot be passed have removed him and me from this light, then, as stated above [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “written”], the houses and their possession shall forever belong to the church of the Lord’s Sepulchre and its canons.

And so that what is written above may remain valid and unharmed, and so that its confirmation and certainty may be demonstrated, I left with the brothers of the church of the Lord’s Resurrection the privilege of Lord Bohemond, written concerning the gift, sale, or liberty of the aforesaid houses that had been granted to me. I also humbly asked that the present document, written concerning the truth of this gift of mine, be strengthened by the seal of Lord William, patriarch.

This gift and its document were made in the year of the Lord 1138, in the presence of that same Lord William [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “the patriarch William”], patriarch, the entire community of the brothers, and the patriarch’s clerics:

Humbert, chaplain; Amelius, deacon; Baldwin, chancellor; John; and many others.

But if thereafter anyone, corrupted by diabolical instigation or by the decay of worldly greed, should attempt to weaken [Note: Col. 1183, supplied from B] or invalidate this gift [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “to debase”], then, if warned once, twice, or three times, he does not repent, let him be struck by the sword of perpetual anathema.

This document was made in the year 1138, indiction 1.

## LXXXVIII [Note: A, fol. 77v; B, fol. 90r.]

### PRIVILEGE OF PRINCE RAIMUND CONCERNING THE GIFT AND GRANT OF THE MILLS AND OTHER POSSESSIONS THAT THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE HAS IN ANTIOCH

[Col. 1184B]

In the name of the supreme and true God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

The diligence of naturally prudent intelligence established from the beginning that the truth of a laboriously accomplished deed ought by right to flow into the celebrated knowledge of posterity; through this, both the firmness worthy of the deed itself is strengthened, and the pious emulation of posterity, by a kind of neighboring example, is always inflamed toward better things.

Therefore we consider it necessary to make known to all present and future that I, Raimund, by the favor of God’s mercy prince of Antioch, and the most illustrious lady Constance [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “Constancia”], my wife, being in every respect debtors to him who died for us—indeed, who also rose again—freely and peacefully restore, give, and grant for perpetual possession to the most reverend Sepulchre of that same Lord of ours Jesus Christ certain rights situated near Antioch. Although these rights had long ago been assigned to the uses of the aforesaid place, in recent times they were regarded as almost unknown, both because of their long deprivation and because of the distance of the lands.

We have taken care to identify all these properties partly by their proper names and partly by the situation of the places. First, there are two mill buildings situated outside the Bridge Gate to the west, the upper of which is called Funeidec in the Arabic language; the other, lower one, has lain ruined for a long time. There is also a certain vineyard formerly possessed by Bruno the street-vendor (*platearius*). These properties mentioned above lie outside the city walls [Note: Col. 1183, correct *urbis*].

The properties that follow are contained within the circuit of the same city [Note: Col. 1183, B reads “within”]. First, a certain shop situated before the baths called Omar in Arabic; also one deserted house before the church of Saint Menas, called by its old name Beruti; and another house beside the church of Saint Peter, which is called Serice. Likewise, another house situated before the house called Serice, formerly possessed by a certain Greek named Solomon, a canon of the Holy Sepulchre; and all the houses situated before the hospital called Hebeneboleit, from the uncovered oven of Saint George, as far as the road that leads toward the church of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

Again, we do not omit that, by the same authority of our gift, we give and grant to the Holy Lord’s Sepulchre, to be held in perpetual peace and by perpetual right, certain other properties recently transferred through the benefactions of the faithful: namely, a certain house given as alms by Osmund, a canon of Antioch, situated before the baths of Lord Tancred; also the house of Gamaliel the priest, a canon of the Holy Sepulchre, near the church of Saint Leonard; and another house belonging to a certain layman named Benedict, before the church of Saint Symeon.

Thus we give all these properties, each and every one, to the glorious Sepulchre of the Lord, as stated above, forever; we protect them by this present privilege, mark them with our seal, and confirm them with suitable witnesses.

This privilege was made in the year of the incarnate Word of God 1140, indiction 3, in the month of April, in the fourth year of the principate of Lord Raimund, most invincible prince of Antioch. The witnesses are:

Lord Gaudin [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Gaufridus”], archbishop of Mamistra; Lord Hugh, bishop of Gabala; Aymericus [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Aimericus”], dean of Antioch; William Brachet, Aimericus, and William of Poitiers, chaplains of the palace; William son of Peter, cleric; Peter, canon of the Temple; Godfrey [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Godefridus”], canon of Saint Abraham; Drogo and Goisbert, knights of the Temple; Roger of Montibus, constable; Walter of Surdavelle; Garento of Saône; Fulk of Buiguin; William Fraisnelli; Leo Maiopolus, duke of Antioch; Geoffrey of Guirchia; Peter Armoini, castellan; Guiterius of Moceon; Richard of Belmont [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Belmunt”]; Robert, son of Geoffrey; Pagan of Fai; Garnerius of Burgo; Hugh of Boleira; Abo of Bolins [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Molins”]; Cheale of Mausiac; Basil, chamberlain, and Oliver, his brother; Garinus Malmuz, marshal; Godfrey [Note: Col. 1185, B reads “Godefridus”], son of Raimbald, viscount; Raimund, marshal; Theodore, notary; George, master of the secretariat.

If anyone, instigated by the devil, should presume in any way to violate this privilege, legitimately made, let the wrath of God come upon him.

Given at Antioch, by the hand of Odo, chancellor, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May.

## LXXXIX [Note: A, fol. 79r; B, fol. 91v.]

### PRIVILEGE OF RAIMUND, PRINCE OF ANTIOCH, CONCERNING THE JUDGMENT MADE IN HIS COURT REGARDING THE INJURY THAT THE COMMUNITY OF THE CHURCH OF SAINT PAUL HAD FOR A VERY LONG TIME INFLICTED UPON THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE OVER THE UNJUST POSSESSION OF A CERTAIN GARDEN

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

The authority handed down by the ancient fathers teaches that whenever a worthy and celebrated institution deserves the effectiveness of equity, it ought to be protected all the more attentively by the manifest lines of a written memorial, so that it may more carefully trample down the insolence of forgetfulness and perpetually take precautions against every attack of accusation.

Therefore, it is necessary to make known to those present and to their descendants that I, Raimund, born of the illustrious lineage of the Poitevins, having obtained by heavenly gift the throne of the kingdom of Antioch, ascended, in the third year of my principate, with the Lord’s favor, to worship at the holy places of Jerusalem.

There, among the other joys of human redemption, I was especially delighted by a singular visit to the most glorious Sepulchre. From Lord William, the most reverend patriarch of that holy city, from Lord Peter, venerable prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and from the entire holy community of that place, I received a devout and humble expression of complaint concerning certain injuries that had long been inflicted near Antioch upon the most excellent burial place of God and man, Christ Jesus. I was also frequently entreated by the common prayer of all in the Lord to restore mercifully to that celebrated place of the ineffable mystery its full rights, from which it had until then been gravely deprived unjustly, for the remedy of my soul.

Since I could neither oppose nor ought to oppose the pious request of so many intercessors—for I am bound by duty to admit mercifully the just voice of anyone oppressed, and still more the common outcry of such great reverence—I pursued their wishes with such diligence that whatever of the right of the Lord’s Sepulchre lay in my hand I most willingly restored from that time and forever to Christ the Lord and to his servants, for the perpetual memory of his resurrection. I also promised that, regarding all the other things that belonged to its right, which had passed into the possession of others, I would most devotedly administer justice to them in the hearing of my court.

For this reason, in the very year of my return from Jerusalem, the aforesaid prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre and Wlgrin, provost, accompanied by several of their brothers, came to Antioch on the first day of February. Not long afterward they vigorously demanded the fulfillment of my promise and requested that I grant them a hearing in equity concerning, specifically, an injury that the community of the church of Saint Paul had for a very long time inflicted upon them through the unjust possession of a certain garden and some land. Although they had repeatedly asserted their claim, they had never yet been able to obtain justice.

To carry this out, I took pains to notify Lord Robert, abbot of the monastery of Saint Paul, and the entire community. Their one voice and single judgment was this: that the examination of this matter did not belong in any way to the judgment of a secular court, but solely to the authority of the lord patriarch of Antioch and of that church. For the entire possession had proceeded from ecclesiastical right, especially since the lord Bernard, patriarch of blessed memory, had formerly given it in exchange for the house of Stephen, treasurer of the church of Saint Paul, and had confirmed the gift by an authentic sanction of his privilege, which they possessed, when he had also confirmed it by agreement with Lord Bohemond the Younger, of august memory.
