I make this exchange with the approval and consent of Lord Fulk the king, Lady Melisende the queen, and their sons, and likewise with the approval and consent of Babinus, my lord, and Petrosius, my kinsman, with the same exchange also approved and commended by my wife Bruna, and by Thomas and Eustachius with my other sons; so that henceforth my aforesaid two casalia, Megina and Mezera, with all their appurtenances, in exchange for the two casalia, namely Cafermelio and Anquina, shall belong to the right and jurisdiction of the church and community of the Lord’s Sepulchre. Thus they shall have the power to do with them whatever they wish, without any claim or opposition from any of my lords or relatives, or from any Christian.

If, concerning the aforesaid casalia, which I, John Patricius, exchange with the church and chapter of the Holy Sepulchre in the manner stated above, whether during my lifetime or after [Col. 1215A] my death, any dispute should arise from anyone, I and my heirs—or whoever receives the inheritance by succession—shall remain perpetually bound to restore in full to the church and chapter whatever loss may result from the dispute that has been raised, according to the assessment of good men.

## CXXI [Note: [Col. 1215] A, fol. 101 recto; lacking in B]. ON THE GIFT OF A CERTAIN VINEYARD WHICH RADULF OF FONTANELLIS GAVE TO GAUFRIDUS ACU

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Radulf of Fontanellis, with the counsel and consent of my wife, and of Gaufridus of Parenti, my son-in-law, and his wife, namely my daughter, and of my other friends, granted to Gaufridus Acu, because he had long served me well and faithfully, one vineyard adjoining the lord patriarch’s property, beside the road leading to Bethlehem, on the left-hand side of that road, not far from Jerusalem.

I granted it to him to possess in perpetuity by hereditary right, also with free power to sell or give it to whomever he wished, without any condition or obligation of service. In this manner I gave him the aforesaid vineyard freely, absolutely, and peacefully to possess. The witnesses of this gift are:

Anschetinus, viscount; Rainaldus of Pont; Bonet of Toulouse; Porcellus; Gerard Bocher; Soherius of Beirut; Peter the Provençal; Bachelerius; and many others.

## CXXII [Note: [Col. 1215] A, fol. 101 recto; lacking in B]. ON THE PROMISE WHICH BALDWIN MADE TO THE HOLY CHURCH OF JERUSALEM

[Col. 1215C]

I, Baldwin, profess and promise before God and his angels that from now on and henceforth I shall, to the best of my ability and knowledge, establish and preserve law, justice, and peace for the holy Church of God in Jerusalem and for the people subject to me, while preserving a fitting regard for mercy, as we may be able to determine better with the counsel of our faithful; and that I shall show the patriarch, and likewise the bishops of the churches of God, fitting and canonical honor; and those things which emperors, kings, and princes have bestowed and restored to the churches entrusted to them.

## CXXIII [Note: [Col. 1215] A, fol. 101 verso; lacking in B]. THE PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE DISPUTE AND SETTLEMENT OF THE CASALE OF GEBUL

[Col. 1215D] In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Since, as the years pass, all human deeds easily fall into oblivion unless they are committed to the written points of a memorial page, therefore I, Walter, by the grace of God prince of all Galilee, ordering this charter to be made, make known, present and future, that the dispute which had for some time been agitated between the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre and Guido, son of Arnulf [Col. 1216A] the monk, was settled in my presence before my barons.

For the aforesaid Guido entirely relinquished in peace to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre the casale over which the dispute had arisen, namely Gibul, situated in the mountains, with all its appurtenances. At sunset it has the casale of Hubelet nearby, and the casalia of Dersoet, Derlauha, and Kafra, while to the north it reaches Cocquet. In recognition of the truth and right of the Holy Sepulchre, he received from those same canons one hundred bezants as a token of affection. Moreover, for confirmation of the matter, he handed over to me the privilege that he possessed.

Having learned the truth through the statements and testimony of my barons and of the legitimate and ancient men of Tiberias, I invested the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, by virtue of that privilege, with the aforesaid casale of Gibul and all [Col. 1216B] its appurtenances. Now, so that these deeds may always remain firm and unshaken, I confirm and strengthen this page with the impression of my seal. The witnesses of this matter are:

Herbert, bishop of Tiberias; Gerald, treasurer; Gerald, canon; Lord Fulk; Guarmund; W[illiam], marshal; Walter, viscount; Ivo; Ludovicus; Baldwin of Culnilz; Fulk of Petrona; W[illiam] of Sueka; Vivian; John; Hugh Grassinus.

## CXXIV [Note: [Col. 1215] A, fol. 102 recto; lacking in B]. THE PRIVILEGE OF THE GIFT, CONFIRMATION, AND LIBERTY OF THE CASALIA AND FISHERY IN THE CITY OF TIBERIAS AND ITS TERRITORY

[Col. 1216C] In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Since all Catholic men, and especially the powerful who have been endowed with divine gifts, ought to honor and exalt all the churches of God, they ought more particularly to exalt the church of the most glorious Sepulchre, where the Lord suffered and died, and by rising again on the third day restored salvation to the human race, and to enrich it with their benefactions, so that, when they have completed the course of this life, they may deserve to possess the boundless joys of eternal life.

Therefore I, Walter, by the grace of God prince of all Galilee, with the consent of my wife Eschiva, grant and confirm the gift which Lord William of Bures, my predecessor of blessed memory, gave to the church of the glorious Sepulchre and to the canons serving God there according to their rule [Col. 1216D], with the concession of King Fulk and his heirs, Radulf of Ysis and Simon: namely, the two casalia of Gebul and Helkar, in their entirety, together with all the land belonging to them, to be possessed freely, peacefully, without any claim or impediment, without exaction, by perpetual right.

The land of these casalia is divided as follows: its length begins at the casale of Hubelet, which lies toward the west, and extends from the other casalia—namely Dersoet, Derlauha, and Kafra—and northward as far as the casale of Cocket [Col. 1217A], and from there stretches toward the River Jordan. Its width extends from the boundary of Bethsan and Tiberias as far as the hollow which is near the casale called Huxenia.

Moreover, I confirm that all fisheries belonging to me shall be held by the aforesaid canons of the Holy Sepulchre, free and undisturbed each year, as William of Bures had granted them—namely, from Septuagesima until Easter, in whichever week they wish to take them. If, however, during the days on which they begin to fish the sea should be stormy, and they should not be able to fish as they wish [Note: [Col. 1217] Correct to potuerint, “should not be able”], it shall be rendered and made good to them on other days of their choosing.

I also grant them annually the entire forced service and assistance of all my fishermen for one day. Furthermore, I likewise grant that they may always have one boat at sea in Galilee for fishing. The witnesses of this matter are:

Herbert, bishop of Tiberias; Gerald, treasurer; Lord Fulk; Garmund; W[illiam], marshal; Walter, viscount; Ivo; Ludovicus; Baldwin of Cunilz; Fulk of Petrona; William of Sueka; Vivian; John; Robert the Neapolitan; Hugh Grassinus.

This was done and confirmed with my seal, while Amalric was patriarch and Amalric was king, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1165.

## CXXV [Note: [Col. 1217] A, fol. 102 verso; lacking in B]. ON SIX CARRUCATES OF LAND ON THIS SIDE OF THE RIVER OF CAIPHAS

[Col. 1217C] In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Roger of Caiphas, and John, my brother, have given to the canons of the Most Holy Sepulchre six carrucates of land, bounded as follows: three on this side of the river of Caiphas, near the springs, and three situated beyond the boundary above the banks, as much as six pairs of oxen can till and cultivate through all the sowings—namely, three for sowing and the other three for fallowing.

To this we add and grant that they shall have these aforesaid carrucates of land free, peaceful, and exempt, released from every exaction and evil customary due [Col. 1217D], and shall possess them by hereditary right forever and throughout all ages, amen. The witnesses of this matter are:

Hernesius, archbishop of Caesarea; Boniface, canon of Caesarea and chaplain of Caiphas; William, the king’s marshal; William of Montgisart; John, his brother; Henry of Gilebeleth; Kogh, son of Manasseh; Humbert, Pagan’s knight; Vivian, viscount; Clement, steward of the lord of Caiphas.

## CXXVI [Note: [Col. 1217] A, fol. 103 recto; lacking in B]. ON THE GIFT AND LIBERTY OF THE CHURCH OF TYRE MADE BY THE VENERABLE ARCHBISHOP PETER TO THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

[Col. 1218A] In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Peter, by divine mercy and not through my merits archbishop of the church of Tyre, and the chapter of the same church, grant to God and to the church of the Holy Sepulchre, and to its venerable prior Lord Nicholas and the entire community, the Church of Blessed Mary, which was the first see of Tyre, while preserving the dignity of our mother church.

We also permit them freely to have the entire tithe of a certain casale called Derina, from everything which they now possess either themselves or through their men; and if hereafter they acquire anything which they say belongs to the aforesaid casale, it shall remain under the same concession.

We likewise consent to the tithe of four carrucates of land which Baldwin, second Latin king, gave to the church of the Holy Sepulchre beside the aforesaid casale. In the same way, we grant them in perpetuity another tithe from a certain garden enclosed separately by a *berquilium*, between the wall of Tyre and its outer wall. The witnesses of this matter are:

Lord Mainard, by the grace of God venerable bishop of the church of Beirut; Lord Walter, dean of the church of Tyre; Lord William, archdeacon of the same church; Lord Aimo, cantor of the same church; Lord Rainaldus, treasurer of the same church; Lord Matthew, canon; [Col. 1218C] Lord Odo, canon; Lord Philip, canon; Lord William, canon; Lord Gerard, canon.

Given at Tyre, by the hand of Albert, chancellor of the church of Tyre, in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1163.

## CXXVII [Note: [Col. 1217] A, fol. 103 verso; lacking in B]. THE PRIVILEGE OF SAYFA [Note: [Col. 1217] Correct to Caypha]

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Vivian, lord of Caypha, and my son Paganus, for the salvation of ourselves and all our relatives, give and grant in perpetuity to the glorious Sepulchre of Jesus Christ [Col. 1218D] and to its canons, in the deserted village situated between Caypha and Palmarea, from the ancient gate of the village on the Palmarea side, beside the upper road, as far as the stone fixed as a boundary beyond the middle of the village; and from that stone as far as the stone above the cross-marked carob tree (*carublerium*); and again from that cross-marked stone, across the hill, as far as the bottom of the hollow, leaving the ancient tombs within their boundaries [Note: [Col. 1217] This sentence is obviously incomplete: the copyist omitted the object of the donation itself. A word must therefore be supplied, perhaps *terram*, “land,” or *casale*, “casale”].

We also give the whole land and its entire plain from the aforesaid village, beside the public road, as far as the two carob trees (*carubleria*). [Col. 1219A] From there, leaving the plain, along a little-used and ancient double track, and by the ridge and the denser carob trees (*carubleria*), as far as the great hollow whose waters flow into Palmarea, we grant to them; from this aforesaid hollow as far as the other hollow, which belongs to the deserted village and is near their building, their boundaries are defined in a straight line to the highest mountain peaks by our donation, without any opposition.

We also add to the aforesaid gift one garden within Palmarea, containing two cisterns. We give all these things to the Holy Sepulchre and its canons free, peaceful, exempt, and liberated from every exaction and evil customary due, so that the canons may have them with their rights of access and return, and possess them by hereditary right forever.

To this we also add and grant that, if they wish to buy, sell, remove, or bring in whatever movable goods are necessary for the house, whatever those goods may be, whether in the village or outside the village, whether by sea or by land, they may do so freely and without any customary payment or fee.

We do not permit them to buy houses, lands, or any inheritances without our permission, or to retain donated properties for more than a year and a day. The witnesses of this matter are:

Amalric, patriarch; Hernesius, archbishop of Caesarea; Boniface, chaplain of Caypha; Roger of Caypha, and John, his brother; William, the king’s marshal; Giraud of Conins; Henry of Gilebelet; Baldwin, Roger’s kinsman; Clement Rufus, steward of the lord of Caypha; [Col. 1219C] Vivian, viscount.

The charter was made in the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1165.

I, Vivian, the aforesaid lord of Caypha, together with my wife Beatrice and my son Paganus, with his wife Hodierna, ordered this charter to be made and confirmed it with the impression of our seal.

## CXXVIII. THE PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE OFFERINGS AND LIBERTY BELONGING TO THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE AND ITS CANONS

(See in Celestine III under the year 1198.)

## CXXIX [Note: [Col. 1219] A, fol. 107 verso; lacking in B]. THE PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE EXCHANGES OF VINEYARDS MADE WITH CERTAIN BURGHERS OF MAHUMERIA

[Col. 1219D]

Let it be known to all, future and present, that Arnald, prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre, with the counsel and consent of the chapter, made the following exchanges with certain burghers of the aforesaid town.

He made one exchange with Guibert Papasius concerning a certain vineyard which the aforesaid Guibert freely held and possessed beside the church of Montjoie, adjoining the cemetery of that church. In exchange for this vineyard, he gave him, at the far end of the great vineyard beside the upper road, a certain part [Col. 1220A] of vineyard, marked out and divided by definite boundaries, for himself and his heirs to have and possess, subject only to the tithe. This vineyard also adjoined Guibert’s vineyard, from which he paid the tithe and the land tax. The aforesaid Guibert did this with the counsel and consent of Usanna, his wife, who was heir to the aforementioned vineyard.

In the same way he made another exchange with Walter the Carpenter concerning a vineyard adjoining the aforementioned vineyard, which had belonged to Guibert Papasius. In exchange for this vineyard he gave him, in another part of the great vineyard, beside the great road [Note: [Col. 1219] Correct to *iuxta*, “beside”], a certain part of vineyard, marked out by boundaries, for himself and his heirs to have and possess freely and peacefully, subject only to the tithe.

[Col. 1220B] In the same way he gave Ainard Cavallom a certain part of vineyard in the same great vineyard, adjoining Walter the Carpenter’s portion of vineyard, likewise bounded by markers and subject to the tithe, in exchange for the vineyard which that same Ainard held beside the vineyard that had belonged to Walter the Carpenter.

The aforesaid Ainard, compelled by extreme poverty and having no means by which he could support and raise his wife and children, sold this vineyard, for their support and sustenance, with their consent and also with the consent of the lord and by the just judgment and consideration of the court, to Martin the Carpenter of Montjoie for twenty-six bezants.

He also made another exchange with the daughters of Pontius the Smith and their husbands concerning a certain cultivated land [Col. 1220C] containing thirty *iugera*, situated in the territory of Kalandria, from which they paid the tithe and land tax. In exchange for that land he gave them two pieces of vineyard in the valley of Saint Mary, one containing four *iugera* and the other two, which had belonged to Brother Peter of Ramatha; from these they and their heirs shall pay a third part and the tithe.

He also gave Stephen Pastinace the vineyard which had belonged to Brother Arnold, on the following condition: that he should plant the uncultivated land belonging to the aforesaid vineyard, and each year render half and the tithe from both.

He also made another exchange with Helyas and Amicus, his son-in-law, concerning a certain part of their garden adjoining the *berquilium*. This portion is divided by boundaries from the other part [Col. 1220D] which they retained for themselves. In exchange for it he gave them a certain part of that uncultivated land which he and the other canons had acquired through the settlement with Robert of Retest; this land also borders Helyas’s own land.

He likewise made another exchange with the Hospital situated at Mahumeria concerning a certain part of a garden which extends from the Sepulchre’s *berquilium* as far as that Hospital’s *berquilium*. In exchange for this portion he gave the aforesaid Hospital two *iugera* of vineyard which had belonged to Brother Stephen Ortalis, subject only to the tithe.

We also wish it to be known to everyone that Brother Robert Porcarius, when Lord Arnald the prior happened to be at Mahumeria one day, in the presence of the burghers of the aforesaid town gathered before him in a full court, confirmed the gift which he had formerly made of himself [Col. 1221A] and all his possessions to the church of the Most Holy Sepulchre, and, handing over to Lord Arnald the prior the staff which he held in his hand, invested him with all his possessions and property.

Lord Arnald, taking the staff and immediately extending it back to Brother Robert before everyone, entrusted and commended these same possessions to him, for him to guard during his lifetime and to administer and increase for the honor of the Most Holy Sepulchre.

Brother Robert then began to report and enumerate there, one by one, how and in what manner he had held and acquired those possessions and properties, saying:

“Prior Giraldus gave me, with my wife, land adjoining the land of Robert the Hungarian; she had formerly been betrothed to Humbert, who, because he could not cultivate the aforesaid land according to the established custom, had abandoned both the land and the village. Prior Peter, who later became archbishop of Tyre, gave me another piece of land contiguous with the aforesaid land in exchange for a certain piece of land which I had bought from Walter Bela. Beside that same land, the same prior Peter gave me another piece of land subject to the land tax and tithe.”

We also wish it to be known to all, present and future, that one day Prior Arnald and Lord Robert [Col. 1221C] of Retest met together at Mahumeria and said to each other:

“Let us go and see the boundaries and divisions of our fields and our land.”

This pleased them both, and they went out to see and traverse the boundaries and markers of the lands. They chose an old Saracen named Pedem Tortum to go before them, for he knew the divisions and boundaries of the lands.

Lord Robert, whose peasant he was, ordered him to speak the truth and lead them by the fixed and just boundaries of the lands, threatening to have his good foot cut off if he lied or ever strayed from the straight path.

The peasant therefore went ahead, and both men approved the indication which he showed them and the route by which he proceeded. The following canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre were present at this survey [Col. 1221D]:

Lord Peter, almoner; Lord Bernard the Antiochene; Brother Pisanus; Peter the Jew; and John, interpreter; Arbertus; Stephen. The son of the aforesaid Robert was also present.

## CXXX [Note: [Col. 1221] A, fol. 109 verso; lacking in B]. ON THE CONFRATERNITY OF BALDWIN OF TORNACO

Let it be known to all that Amalric, prior, and the other canons of the Holy Sepulchre received Baldwin of Tornaco into their confraternity. Therefore they granted him, at Christmas, Easter, Pentecost, the feast of Saint Augustine, and the feast of All Saints, a prebend either in Jerusalem or at Mahumeria, as though he were one of them.

The aforesaid Baldwin released and renounced, without any claim or opposition from himself or his heirs, in favor of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, whatever he had justly or unjustly claimed, or could claim, concerning the possessions or inheritance of Brother Robert Sepulchre Porcarius.

The same Baldwin also granted to the aforesaid church, after his death, a fourth part and the tithe of a vineyard in Brother Robert Porcarius’s land, containing six *iugera*, which vineyard he freely and peacefully possessed.

Therefore the aforesaid canons granted him, during his lifetime, the land tax and tithe of the vineyard which he had beside Gabaon; after his death, however, the aforesaid canons shall have the tithe and land tax of the vineyard mentioned above. Baldwin, according to these terms, may give or sell either vineyard to whomever he pleases.

## CXXXI [Note: [Col. 1221] A, fol. 109 verso; lacking in B]. ON THE OATH OF THE BURGHERS OF MAHUMERIA

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

In the year of the Lord’s incarnation 1155, in the fourth indiction, on the third day before the Ides of February, under Fulcher, patriarch of Jerusalem, and Baldwin, fourth Latin king of Jerusalem, the burghers of Mahumeria swore an oath of loyalty to the community of the Most Holy Sepulchre in the following form:

“I, John Guitard, swear fidelity to God and to the Most Holy Sepulchre and to the community of that same Most Holy Sepulchre, to preserve and defend [Col. 1222C] their life and limbs, their honor, and everything that belongs to the Holy Sepulchre and to the aforesaid community, while preserving the fidelity owed to the king of Jerusalem. So may God and this holy Gospel help me.”

The following page gives the names of these burghers:

John Guitard; Andrew of Saint Gautier; Peter the Jew; Peter of Auvergne; Rainaldus of Barletta; Geoffrey Claire; Humbert of Jehoshaphat; Arnulf of Joppa; Aimeric Guitard; Peter Orgerius; Gerald Rufus; Robert the Smith; Martin the Carpenter; Albert the Smith; Peter the Provençal; Hugh of Saint Helyas; Helyas Lombard; John Catalan; Bartholomew; Robert Malvais; John Pissot; William of the Forge; Frumentius; [Col. 1222D] William of Tuschet; Anselm Lombard; Girbert the Burgundian; Odo the Frenchman; Pontius Bonari; William the Clerk; Giraud Lambert; Maurinus; Stephen of Linedan; Maius; Bernard the Burgundian; Bruno of Poitiers; William the Provençal; Aimeric of Poitiers; Peter Bonet; Godefrey Lombard; Radulf Senus the Mason; John Cortiliarius; Bernard; Pontius Milii; Bernard the Shoemaker; Rainaldus Gaite; Girbert; Robert Plantavigna; Arnold Tardi; Bernard of Jehoshaphat; Peter of Ramatha; Durand the Mason; Peter Catalan; Gallard, son of Arnold; Bernard the Shoemaker; Walter the Mason; Christian; [Col. 1223A] Clement Droco; Radulf of the Court of Babylon; William Rufus; Robert, brother of Guido the Patriarch; Bernard, brother of Rainaldus Gaite; Bernard, brother of Bartholomew; Peter the Carpenter; Peter of the Baths; Stephen, father of Gilbert; Stephen, son of Garsendis; Robert the Frenchman; Oliver, brother of Peter Bonus; Bonus Valet; Durand; Pontius the Provençal; Godoet; Geoffrey the One-Eyed; Laurence; William Hollow-Mouth; Aimeric the Great; Bruno; Valentinus; John the Provençal; Theobald; William the Butler; Theobald Rufus; Peter of Auvergne; Bernard, son-in-law of Bernard of Gerim; William Gascon; Stephen of Bourges; Bernard Lombard; Bernard of Saint-Albino; Walter the Little; Bernard of Montjoie; Walter [Col. 1223B] Dominic of Montjoie.

This was done in the cloister and chapter house of the Most Holy Sepulchre, with Amicus the dean administering the oath, before suitable witnesses named as follows:

Rainaldus Sicher; Simon Rufus; Peter of Périgueux; Geoffrey of Tours; Albert Lombard; Pontius Gaagne; Peter of Saint Lazarus.

Humbert the Smith [Note: [Col. 1223] All the names that follow, which in the manuscript are separated by a paragraph from the preceding names, probably designate burghers established at Mahumeria after the year 1155, from whom the same oath was required]; Robert of Naples; Master Lucas the Venetian; Segnoret; Albert the Frenchman; Raymond the Crooked; Clement the Mason; Gilbert the Mason; William of Pissot; William of Tours; Martin Gascon; Peter of Poitiers; Stephen [Col. 1223C] son of Peter the Jew; Andrew of Valle Cursus; Ainardus Cavaillum; Raymond the Weaver; Pontius of Burgundy; Peter Bodinus; Stephen, son of Andrew of Saint Walter; Ambrosius; Gerald the Baker; Otgerius of the casale of Saint Giles; Aldebert; Geoffrey Bocher; Gerald the Shoemaker; Arnold with the Beard; William of the casale of Saint Mary; Rampnulf, brother of Peter of Joppa; Constantine; Aimeric of Poitiers; Peter, son of Rainaldus of Barletta; Arduinus; William of the casale of Saint Giles; Humbert of Bourges; Jordan, son of Peter the Goldsmith; John of Cava; Vincent; Raembald; Bernard with the Head; Radulf; Gerald of Belinas; Peter of Limoges; Arnulf; Constantius Bocher; Lambert of Burgundy; Walter the Carpenter; Rainaldus of Monte Alberti; [Col. 1223D] Lambert of Bourges; Pontius; Peter of Bourges.

## CXXXII [Note: [Col. 1223] A, fol. 111 recto; lacking in B]. ON A CERTAIN LAND OF MAHUMERIA WHICH ROBERT OF RETEST POSSESSED, ADJOINING THE CASALE OF SALOME

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Because human memory quickly slips from the mind amid the many cares that arise and the instability of life, it pleased both parties [Note: Correct *patri* to *parti*.]—the canons and the same Robert—that a written record should be made of how the dispute repeatedly brought by Robert of Retesta against the canons of the Holy Sepulchre over the land of Birre, now called Mahumeria, adjoining his estate called Salome, was settled, so that it would not disappear from the memory of those now living or of those who come after. [Col. 1224A]

We therefore wish it to be known to all, present and future, that when both parties—the lord canons and the aforesaid Robert—had come to discuss that land, the lord prior and his brethren showed, from the division made by King Baldwin I and from the gift, that the land belonged to the Holy Sepulchre. They also brought forward witnesses who were ready to swear that this was true. When Robert heard this, after taking counsel with his friends, he remitted the aforesaid claim to the lord prior and his brethren, for the honor of the Holy Sepulchre and out of affection for them. [Col. 1224B]

Since Robert had shown himself kind toward the lords, the lord prior and the other brothers granted him that whichever burghers of Birre wished to do so might cultivate his land, not only with grain, oil, and legumes, but also with vines, trees, and everything that the land can produce. They were to give the tithes to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, while they were to give Robert what they had agreed to give him as rent; Robert himself, for his part, was also to give the lords the tithes. Over the aforesaid burghers, however, they granted neither to him nor to his heirs any power or lordship to exercise authority, inflict violence, demand a penalty or exaction, or require anything else on account of what has been stated above. [Col. 1224C]

The witnesses to this agreement are:

Radulfus Strabo; Adam Niger and his brother Fulco; Simon, burgher of Jerusalem; Baldwin of Torrai; Peter of Joppa; Arnulf, his son; John Guidardus; and many others.

### CXXXIII. [Note: A, fol. 111 verso; missing in B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING SAPHARORIA, WHICH GIBELINUS SOLD TO THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

Since the memory of deeds preserved in writing removes many disputes, we therefore wish it to be known to all, future and present, that Gibelinus, knight, son of Anchetinus, sold to the Latin canons of the Holy Sepulchre a certain estate called Saph[ar]oria, with all its dependent land and all its appurtenances, for 180 bezants and a fur garment; and he granted it to them and to their successors to possess freely and peacefully forever by hereditary right. He gave them legitimate guarantors, namely Hugh, his son-in-law, and William the Norman.

If, in his own time or in that of his successors, any claim should arise from any quarter concerning this matter, Gibelinus himself, Hugh his son-in-law, their sons and grandsons, and all their heirs shall completely annul and settle that claim. [Col. 1225A]

Agnes, Gibelinus’s wife, and their son Anselinus approved and granted this arrangement. The canons gave Anselinus a perpetual grant of five bezants and one sword.

The witnesses to this sale are:

John, the king’s dapifer; Geoffrey, the lord [Note: The word *dominus* has no meaning here; it should probably be corrected to *domesticus* or *dominicus*. In the first case, the Geoffrey in question would be the same as Geoffrey of Tours, called “seneschal of the lord patriarch” (*senescalcus domni patriarche*) in document 100; in the other case, there would be two persons, one named simply Geoffrey and the other Dominic the Patriarch, who appears in document 138.], the patriarch; Peter of Périgord; Simon Rufus; Britius; Albert the Lombard; Baldwin of Tournai; and Robert of Jehoshaphat.

The witnesses to the grant by Agnes, Gibelinus’s wife, and their son Anselinus are:

Brictius; William Beraldi; and Albert the Lombard.

And among the sworn men of Jerusalem:

Simon Rufus; Rainaldus Sicherius; Albert Tortus; Guibertus Papais; and Arnulf, sworn man of Mahumeria.

### CXXXIV. [Note: A, fol. 112 recto; missing in B.] PRIVILEGE OF ROBERT THE SWINEHERD OF MAHUMERIA

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Robert the Swineherd of Mahumeria, give myself and everything that I possess or may thereafter possess to God and to the community of the Most Holy Sepulchre, for my soul and the souls of my parents: vineyards, lands, houses, gold, silver, all movable goods, and, in short, all possessions, to be held forever by hereditary right.

This charter was made in the year 1155 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 3, while the venerable patriarch Fulcherius presided in Jerusalem and King Baldwin IV reigned. [Col. 1225C]

The witnesses to this surrender and gift are:

Amalricus, prior of the Holy Sepulchre; Arnaldus, subprior; Giraldus, precentor; Radulfus Parisius; William the Norman; Godefridus, treasurer; Nicholas, almoner; Stephanus, provost; Peter Sepulchrarius; Constantinus, cellarer; Bertoldus; Bernardus, chamberlain; Baldwin; Mainerius; and Peter Clemens.

Of the deacons:

William Beriti; John of Poitiers; Hugh; and Peter.

Of the subdeacons:

William of Spain; Rainaldus of Loches; Peter; and Robert of Antioch.

Of the brothers:

Robert of Mahumeria; Brother Henry; and all the others.

### CXXXV. [Note: A, fol. 112 verso; missing in B.] PRIVILEGE OF THE MEN OF MAHUMERIA CONCERNING THE VINEYARDS

Let it be known to all, future and present, that I, Arnaldus, prior of the Most Holy Sepulchre, [Col. 1226A] and the entire community grant to the men of Mahumeria our vineyards—namely, the vineyard of Lord Hugh of Horso and the vineyard called that of Lord Radulfus of Paris—for them and their heirs to have forever, on the following condition: each of them shall bring, from his own share, half of the produce, both in grapes and in the fruits of the trees, both in seed and in plantings, and the tithe belonging to him, to the court of the Holy Sepulchre at Mahumeria, or wherever the steward of Mahumeria orders it to be brought.

If anyone wishes to sell his vineyard, he shall sell it with our counsel and shall pay us half of the price. He shall not, however, be permitted to sell it to Templars, Hospitallers, any church, knights, or anyone else through whom the church might suffer harm. If any of these men poorly cultivates his share of the aforesaid vineyards, the steward of Mahumeria, accompanied by four or five suitable witnesses, shall come to him and point out the poorly cultivated vineyard. If he refuses to correct it, he shall pay half a mark of silver, and the vineyard shall be given to another. [Col. 1226B]

If any of these men wishes to receive land for planting a vineyard, he shall not be permitted to plant except on the land of the Holy Sepulchre. [Note: Correct to *non ei*.] Furthermore, if the aforesaid canons wish to enlarge their village, they may, without prohibition or compensation, give dwellings in the aforesaid vineyards to whomever they wish.

With Lord Amalricus, patriarch of Jerusalem, consenting—in whose presence this was done—the witnesses are the canons of the same church, whose names are subscribed:

The aforesaid prior Arnaldus; Nicholas, subprior; Godefridus, treasurer; Gamaliel; Ilbertus; Peter of the Sepulchre; Achilles; Bernard of Antioch; Peter Clemens; Hugh Nigelle; Peter the Latin; Peter Lombard; Rainaldus of Loches; and Robert of Antioch.

Of the men of Mahumeria:

Brother Pisanus, steward of the house; Brother Ungarus; Robert; Arnulfus; John Guitardus; Peter the Jew; Andrew of Saint-Galterius; Hugh of Saint Elias; Martin of Mount Joy; Ambrosius; and Robert Iners.

### CXXXVI. [Note: A, fol. 113 verso; missing in B.] CONCERNING AN AGREEMENT MADE WITH CERTAIN SETTLERS IN RAMATHES

[Col. 1226D]

Let it be known to all who hear this that I, Nicholas, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, and the entire community give to Guido Camelarius, Giraldus Caprellus, and Hugh of Joppa, and to their heirs and to others who come to settle within our estate of Ramathes, at the place called New Village, plots on which to build houses, to be held freely without any rent, and land for planting vineyards and trees, as was shown to them through the agency of Lord Peter of the Sepulchre.

We also give Guido one carucate of land, Hugh another, and Giraldus two, to cultivate well, on the condition that from the produce of the grain and legumes which they obtain from it, they shall give us each year a fourth and a tenth. [Note: Correct *donabit* to *donabunt*.] From the produce of the vineyards and olive groves which they plant there, we shall receive a fifth and a tenth. We also give Giraldus and Hugh a large part of the olive grove which William Beritensis had planted for himself; from its produce they shall render us a fourth and a tenth. [Col. 1227A]

They shall bring our aforesaid share—namely, the fourth, fifth, and tenth—to our storehouses at New Village. We grant to the aforesaid men and to others who come to settle there the oven, mill, and other customary dues according to the usage of Mahumeria.

We also give to Giraldus Caprellus and Hugh of Joppa, and to their heirs, our vineyard at Ramathes, to cultivate well; from its produce they shall give us one half and a tenth. If any of them or any of their heirs wishes to sell something from his possession, he shall first offer it for sale to us. If we do not wish to buy it, he may then sell it to another burgher of his own standing who is to live there and who must observe and fulfill toward us the obligations stated above.

This was done on the eighth day before the Kalends of April, in the year 1160 from the Incarnation of the Lord. The witnesses to this matter are:

Nicholas, prior; Arnulfus, subprior; Bernard, cantor; Godefridus, treasurer; Ilbertus; [Col. 1227C] Eurardus; Peter of the Sepulchre; Achilles; Peter Clemens; Rainerius; Hugh of Nigella; Peter of Latina; Rainaldus; and Peter Lombard.

### CXXXVII. [Note: A, fol. 114 recto; missing in B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING A CERTAIN HOUSE WHICH NICHOLAS, PRIOR OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE, GAVE TO STEPHANUS PASNAIE

Let it be known to all who hear this that I, Nicholas, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, with the consent of our entire chapter, grant to Stephanus Pasnaie and his heirs, to be held by perpetual hereditary right, that house which Lord Peter of the Sepulchre bought from Nicholas and his wife Pontia, on the following condition: Stephanus and his heirs shall pay us and our successors five bezants each year on the Purification of Blessed Mary. [Col. 1227D]

We further stipulate that if they wish to sell that house, they shall first offer it for sale to us. If we do not wish to buy it, they may then sell it to another burgher of their own standing who is to live there, subject to the aforesaid rent and our grant.

This was done on the fourth day before the Nones of April, in the year 1160 from the Incarnation of the Lord. The witnesses to this matter are:

Nicholas, prior; Arnulfus, subprior; Godefridus, treasurer; Ebrardus; Ilbertus; Peter of the Sepulchre; Peter Clemens; Achilles; Bernard of Antioch; Rainerius; Hugh of Nigella; [Col. 1228A] Peter of Latina; Rainaldus of Loches; Peter Lombard; and Robert of Antioch.

### CXXXVIII. [Note: A, fol. 114 verso; missing in B.] CONCERNING THE GIFT OF A CERTAIN HOUSE LOCATED IN MAHUMERIA

Let it be known to all who hear this that I, Nicholas, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, with the consent of our entire chapter, give to Dominic, who is called the Patriarch, and to his heirs, to possess by perpetual hereditary right, one house situated in Mahumeria, which Lord Peter of the Sepulchre bought from a certain woman named Armellina, on the following condition: the aforesaid Dominic and his heirs shall pay us and our successors annually, on the Purification of the Mother of God, six bezants as rent. [Col. 1228B]

Nevertheless, if it should happen by some unforeseen circumstance that they wish to sell that house, they may sell it to another burgher of their own standing, subject to the aforesaid rent and our right; but they shall first offer it for sale to us.

This was done on the third day before the Nones of April, in the year 1160 from the Incarnation of the Lord. The witnesses to this matter are:

Nicholas, prior; Arnulfus, subprior; Godefridus, treasurer; Eurardus; Ilbertus; Peter of the Sepulchre; Peter Clemens; Achilles; Bernard of Antioch; Rainerius; Hugh of Nigella; Peter of Latina; Rainaldus of Loches; Peter Lombard; and Robert of Antioch.

### CXXXIX. [Note: A, fol. 114 verso; missing in B.] CONCERNING THE GRANT OF A CERTAIN HOUSE LOCATED IN THE VILLAGE OF MAHUMERIA

[Col. 1228C]

Let it be clear to all the sons of Holy Mother Church that I, Nicholas, prior of the Holy Sepulchre, and the entire community grant to Suardus and his heirs, to be held by perpetual hereditary right, one house with all its appurtenances, situated in the village of Mahumeria, which Lord Peter of the Sepulchre acquired by purchase from Acardus and his wife, named Bella, on the following condition: Suardus and his heirs shall pay us and our successors each year, on the Purification of Blessed Mary, eight bezants as rent. [Col. 1228D]

We further stipulate that if Suardus or his heirs wish to sell that house to another burgher of their own standing, no one shall place any impediment in their way, subject to the aforesaid rent and our right.

This was done on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April, in the year 1160 from the Incarnation of the Lord. The witnesses to this matter are:

Nicholas, prior; Arnulfus, subprior; Godefridus, treasurer; Ebrardus; Ilbertus; Peter of the Sepulchre; Peter Clemens; Achilles; Reinerius; Hugh of Nigella; Peter of Latina; Rainaldus; and Peter Lombard.

### CXL. [Note: A, fol. 115 recto; missing in B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THREE WASTELANDS WHICH THE ABBOT OF SAINT SABA SOLD TO THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

Let it be known to all, future and present, that I, Miletus, by the grace of God abbot of the church of Saint Saba, and the entire community of our brother monks sell, with the common consent of our entire chapter, to Nicholas, prior, and the Latin canons of the church of the most glorious Lord’s Sepulchre, for 500 bezants less 20, that land consisting of three wastelands called Kafarrus, Old Betor, and Deirfres, which Queen Melisende, of worthy memory, is known to have given to our church and to us as an alms in exchange for 24 purchased loaves, which we and our successors must celebrate every Saturday forever for the redemption of her soul.

With those bezants we immediately bought from Amalricus, king of Jerusalem, land more useful to us, namely an estate called Thora. [Col. 1229B]

Furthermore, let it be known to all that, while we shall celebrate forever in the customary manner the established alms for the soul of the aforesaid queen, we must defend in every court against every unjust claim or assault the aforesaid alms-land, in its full extent and breadth, which we have sold free and clear to the prior and canons of the Holy Sepulchre, together with its villagers, appurtenances, and everything known to belong to its jurisdiction.

### CXLI. [Note: A, fol. 115 verso; B, fol. 32 recto.] CONCERNING THE PURCHASE MADE WITH THE PRIOR AND CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE, AND BALDWIN, LORD OF SAINT EGIDIUS, CONCERNING HOUSES AND OTHER PROPERTY [Note: In B the heading reads: “The assent of Baldwin, of the estate of Saint Egidius, concerning the purchase made by the monastery of Mount Tabor.”]

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

Let it be known to all the faithful of God, present [Col. 1229C] and future, that I, Baldwin, by the grace of God lord of the estate of Saint Egidius, together with my wife Stephania, in the presence of Lord Roardus [Note: B, Ricardus.], castellan of Jerusalem and my father-in-law, and of the other good men whose names are written below [Note: B, “recorded below.”], have given our assent to the purchase which Lord Peter, prior, and the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre made of the houses, [Note: Missing in B.] buildings, and vineyards, with all their appurtenances, which the abbot and monks of Mount Tabor held in the aforesaid estate, whether by gift of my predecessors, by purchase, or by acquisition, so that they may hold and possess all these things freely and peacefully forever, without any claim, with the same [“frantitia”; B, *francicia*] and liberty in which the abbots and monks of Mount Tabor are known to have held them in the time of my predecessors and in my own. [Col. 1229D]

Furthermore, we completely remit the claim which we had been making against the aforesaid canons concerning a certain house which they had held in the aforesaid estate before that purchase, and we grant that henceforth they may hold and possess it peacefully and without dispute.

So that our grant and assent may not later be overturned or violated in any way by anyone, we caused this present document to be made in duplicate by the alphabet and divided through the middle: one copy is held by the prior and chapter of the Holy Sepulchre, while we have retained the other as a sign and memorial of the transaction. [Col. 1230A]

The witnesses are:

Roardus, castellan of Jerusalem, my father-in-law; Anselm of Brie; Simon of Bethlehem; Andrew of Caïpha, knights; Geoffrey of Tours [Note: The signature of this witness is missing in B.]; Robert of Pincen[iacum]; John Raimundi; William Patronus; Radulfus, brother of Lord William, archbishop of Tyre; Bernard Proet; the burghers of Jerusalem; Arnulfus of Mahumeria; and Guarinus [Note: B, Garinus] the Neapolitan of the Temple, servant of Lady Queen Maria.

This was done in the year 1175 of the Lord’s Incarnation, indiction 6, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of January.

### CXLII. [Note: A, fol. 116 recto; B, fol. 33 recto.] PRIVILEGE OF LORD GUARINUS, ABBOT OF MOUNT TABOR, AND OF PETER, PRIOR OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE [Note: In B the heading reads: “Concerning the possessions of Mount Tabor which are at the estate of Saint Egidius.”]

In the name of the Lord, amen.

Let it be known to all the sons of Holy Mother Church, present and future, that I, Guarinus, abbot of Mount Tabor, with the consent of Lord Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth, and with the assent and unanimous will of Prior Lancelinus and the entire chapter of our church, have reached the following agreement with Peter, prior of the church of the Lord’s Resurrection, and the whole community of that church:

Because of the remoteness of the place and the burden of the great expenses, we have, with good will and unanimous consent, returned to Peter, the prior, and the canons of the same church—which had the right to it—our church which we had at the estate of Saint Egidius, together with its offerings, parochial right, and everything else pertaining to it, as well as half of all the tithes of that estate and of two others, namely Turbasaim [Note: B, Turbasym.] and Dere. We held these from them by lease, by grant of the late Lord W[illiam] the patriarch, in return for one wheel of wax. [Note: Missing in B.] [Col. 1230C]

We have sold to them, for 1,000 bezants [Note: B, “for 2,000 bezants.”], our vineyards, houses, [Note: Missing in B.] buildings [Note: B, *edificia*], and other movable goods, which we acquired both through our own labor and by purchase [Note: B, *precio*, “price”]. In recognition of these vineyards, houses, and buildings [Note: B, *edificiorum*], they must pay us and our church each year three wheels of incense and one wheel of wax on the feast of the Transfiguration of the Lord [Note: B, *persolvere debent*, “they must pay.”]. [Col. 1230D]

The witnesses to this transaction are:

Letardus, archbishop of Nazareth; Radulfus, bishop of Sebaste; John, prior of the same church; and Peter, cantor of the church of Tyre.

Of the canons of the Holy Sepulchre:

John of Poitiers; Hugh of Nigella [Note: B, Hugo]; Rainaldus of Loches; Constantinus; and Peter, cantor, priests. Odo [Note: B, Oddo.] and Geoffrey, deacons. Peter of Mahumeria [Note: B, Mahomaria.] and Robert of Rome, subdeacons.

Of the monks of Mount Tabor:

Lancelinus, prior; Peter of Podium, treasurer; Martinus; John the Spaniard [Note: B, *Hyspanus*.]; Stephanus, cantor; Aimericus; Dominicus; John of Nazareth; Enardus; Pandulfus; William the Provençal [Note: B, *Provincialis*.]; and Marcellinus.

Of the clergy of Nazareth:

Geraldus, archdeacon of Nazareth; Tibaldus, canon of Sidon [Note: B, *Sydoniensis*.]; John, canon of Nazareth; Galterius of Capella; John of Corinth [Note: B, *Coritensis*.]; Gibertus, chaplain of the lord archbishop of Nazareth; and Jordan the Merchant.

This transaction was made in the year 1175 of the Lord’s Incarnation, indiction 6, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of November.

### CXLIII. [Note: A, fol. 117 recto; missing in B.] CONCERNING A PEACE RESTORED BETWEEN THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE AND THE MONKS OF LATINA

I, William, by the grace of God bishop of the church of Acre, delegated by Lord Pope Alexander, was judge of a certain case being disputed between the canons of the Holy Sepulchre and the monks of Latina concerning the tithes of a certain estate called Montople. The monks said that these tithes belonged to their right, while the canons, on the contrary, asserted that they possessed them as due to themselves.

When a day had therefore been set for the two parties to present their evidence, and their arguments on both sides had been carefully heard and examined, sufficient sworn witnesses finally established for me that previously, when this same dispute was being dealt with between the aforesaid churches before Patriarch Fulcherius, Amelinus, abbot of Latina, had acknowledged in peace that the tithe was owed to the canons and had left it to them: once before the lord patriarch, in the presence of certain of his brothers, none of whom objected; and a second time in the full chapter of Latina, with none of the brothers objecting.

Having therefore learned of this solemn renunciation, I absolve the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre from the monks’ claim and judge that they may justly possess the aforesaid tithe forever.

The witnesses present at this charter were:

Hernesius, lord archbishop of Caesarea; Lord Jubaldus, elected bishop of Byblos; Daniel, cantor; Rutinus, treasurer; Master Monachus; Master Rogerius; Guido, canon; William and Peter, priests; Girardus, Robertus, Bernoldus, and Fulco, deacons; Guido of Meniers; Manesserius of Caesarea; Rorgus of Nazareth; Godecallus; Amalricus of Caesarea; Aicaldus; Raimundus; and Pandulfus Pisanus.

### CXLIV. [Note: A, fol. 121 verso; B, fol. 117 verso.] PRIVILEGE OF AMALRICUS, FIFTH KING OF THE LATINS, CONCERNING THE GIFT AND LIBERTY OF THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE [Note: In B the heading contains only these words: “Privilege of King Amalricus.”]

[Col. 1232A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, future and present [Note: [Col. 1231] A reads: “future and future.”], that I, Amalric, by the grace of God fifth Latin king in the holy city of Jerusalem, wishing to follow in the footsteps of my predecessors of blessed memory—namely Duke Godfrey; his brother Baldwin, first king of Jerusalem; Baldwin, second king; my father Fulk; and my brother Baldwin, of blessed memory, fourth king of that same city—for the salvation of myself and my own, both living and dead [Col. 1232B], confirm and ratify for the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1231] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] and for its canons, now serving God there and destined to serve Him in the future, whatever that church has lawfully and reasonably obtained, at any time and from the time of Duke Godfrey onward, within the boundaries of my kingdom, by gift, grant, exchange, or purchase, up to the present day.

I have therefore wished to set out in sequence what the aforesaid church has obtained by gift, grant, exchange, or purchase, and from whom, as the following statements make clear. First, Duke Godfrey gave the aforesaid canons twenty-one villages with their appurtenances, called by the following names: Ainquine, Armotie, Keffreca, Keffredil [Note: [Col. 1231] B reads Kefredil.], Bubin—which, together with a certain gastina called Bethchamzir, the aforementioned canons gave to the Knights Templar for 150 bezants [Note: [Col. 1231] B reads “Byzantines.”], which they paid annually for the defense of the land—Hubim, Haram, Kalendrie, Bentiligel, Birra, now called by the modern inhabitants Greater Mahomeria, Sabaiet [Note: [Col. 1231] B reads Sabahiet.], Ataraberet, Urinet, Zenum, Lemule, Bentelamus, Aineseins, now called Valdecurs, Barmita, Beituimen, Beitfoteire, and Betsurieh, in whose territory the village called Little Mahomeria was founded; he gave these to the church in question and granted them to be possessed by perpetual right.

He also gave the same church all the ovens of Jerusalem, except only two: one belonging to the Hospital and the other to the Latins.

The first King Baldwin gave and handed over to the aforesaid church, at Saint Lazarus, villeins with their families, and four villages above Saint Lazarus, whose names are these: Benehatie, Benehabeth, Ragabam, and Roma. Likewise, in the territory of Naples, the first King Baldwin gave the same church one thousand measures of wheat to be received each year. The second King Baldwin, however, gave in exchange for these thousand measures in the territory of Naples a village named Cafarmelech.

All these things, as they have been mentioned above, I, Amalric, fifth king of Jerusalem, grant on my part to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1231] B reads Sepulcri, “of the Sepulchre.”], and decree that they be held perpetually.

In exchange for Saint Lazarus in Bethany and the four aforesaid villages [Col. 1233A], I confirm to the church the village of Thecue with all its entirety, just as my father Fulk, third king of Jerusalem, with the consent of Queen Melisende—my mother—and of King Baldwin, my brother, gave it to the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulcri, “of the Sepulchre.”] with the same liberty by which my aforesaid father is known to have held it with Queen Melisende [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Milisende.], and confirmed it by his privilege. I also promise to defend this grant of exchange for the church against every calumny, trouble, or impediment, now and hereafter.

Furthermore, I confirm the commendable exchange made between the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] and John Patricius [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Patricius.] concerning the villages Capharmalic and Ainquina, in exchange for John’s two villages, namely Megina and Mezera.

I also confirm half [Note: [Col. 1233] Supplied from B.] of that possession which the first King Baldwin gave to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads “the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.”] in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Bethlehemitici, “of Bethlehem.”].

I further confirm the village named Derina, situated in the territory of Tyre above the great spring from which a watercourse proceeds, with all its appurtenances; and, in the boundaries of the aforesaid village toward the mountains, as much land as four pairs of oxen can cultivate from year to year; and the garden situated between the wall and the outer wall of Tyre on the seaward side. All these things the second King Baldwin gave to the Lord’s Sepulchre.

Moreover, I confirm half of the village of Fieisse, now called the village of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”], which Eustace Garnerius [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Granerius.]—with the grant also of Baldwin, second king—gave to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] to hold freely and perpetually with all its appurtenances. I also confirm to the said church all that land which Walter, son of the aforesaid Eustace, gave to the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] beyond the river around that same village, to be held up to the marked boundaries, which are visible to the present day.

Furthermore, I confirm the church and possessions at Acre which Lambert Als and his wife Agnes [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads sua, “his,” rather than eius, “his/her.”] gave to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] with the consent of King Fulk, my father.

Likewise, I confirm the village of Mimas with two full ploughlands of land, given by the aforesaid Lambert Als, which my father confirmed to the aforementioned church.

I confirm the garden which belonged to Mainard of Portu, and which his son Raymond, having become a brother of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] upon his conversion, gave [Col. 1233D].

I also confirm to the same church two villages, Gebul and Helcar, with all their adjacent lands; eight days of fishing; one day of forced labor; and a ship continuously, in the manner in which William of Buris granted these things to the canons of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] and in which they were strengthened by the privilege of himself and my father.

As for the houses situated in the city of Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Ierusalem.], namely, the house of Bernard the canon; the house of Evrard [Col. 1234A] the canon; likewise the house of another Evrard, the canon; the house of Mainard; the house of Garsion; the house of Walter Tronaior; the house of Bernard Bursarius; the house of Herluin; the house of Mabilie; the house of Roger, brother of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulehri, apparently an orthographic error.]; the shop which belonged to William [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Guillelmus.] the Bastard; that part which the same William [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Guillelmus.] had in the money-changers’ market [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads numulariorum, “of the money-changers,” rather than mummulariorum.]; and the house of Martin Caraoane—all these my frequently mentioned father granted to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] free and exempt from every exaction, and fortified by his privilege; I confirm them to the same church.

I also confirm to the aforesaid canons the land situated within the precincts of Jerusalem, together with its houses and shops, so that they may do in them whatever they wish, with this sole exception: that no one other than the king alone may do so in that city [Col. 1234B]. I confirm them so freely that whoever—whether money-changers, merchants, or practitioners of any work or craft—has rented them from the aforesaid canons, or wishes to rent them [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads conduxerint and voluerint, “will have rented” and “will wish to rent,” rather than conduxerunt and voluerunt.], may freely and peacefully, without any disturbance or impediment, carry on his trade there.

Among the rest, I decree valid three villages, one called Capharuth, another Gith, and the third Porphyria, which Roger, bishop of Lydda, granted from the possession of Saint George, with all their appurtenances [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads appenditiis, “appendages/appurtenances.”], together with half the tithe of the harvests of those villages and the whole and entire tithe of all the others, to the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] to be held by perpetual right.

And I decree valid a fourth village, named Kefrescilta, which the aforesaid bishop of Lydda established for the aforesaid church, to be possessed in perpetuity with all its entirety and with a similar tithe to those two villages, but in exchange for the tithe of the castle of Arnold and the tithe of a certain village belonging to the Hospital, named Bulbul.

I confirm as freely, peacefully, and completely remitted to the aforesaid canons the complaint concerning the Syrians that arose between King Baldwin, my brother, and the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”], as King Baldwin remitted it to those canons freely, peacefully, and wholly released, more fully as is contained in their privilege, in which the names of the aforesaid Syrians are also written.

Likewise, I entirely remit and confirm as fully released the dispute that had for some time existed concerning the boundaries of the territory of the village of the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] called Bethsuri, between Queen Melisende [Col. 1234D], my mother, and the canons of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1233] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”], free and peaceful and without any impediment or trouble from me, my successors, or anyone else.

Nevertheless, I confirm to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] those villages—namely Bethel, Odemamel, Dehyrsabeth, Corteis, Deirmusim, and Huetdebes—which the frequently mentioned canons purchased from Hugh of Ibelin for a price [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads pretio, “for a price,” rather than precio.], with all their villeins and with all their entirety and appurtenances [Col. 1235A].

I likewise confirm to the same church the village named Geladia, which I myself gave in payment for the expense and outlay incurred by the canons of the Holy Sepulchre in capturing Ascalon.

I also confirm the village named Beitatap, which the aforesaid canons purchased from John Gomannus and Ancherius, his son, with all its gastinae and appurtenances, as is fully contained in the privilege of King Baldwin, my brother.

Furthermore, I confirm to the aforesaid church these two villages, namely Cafaruth and Old Bethor, and the gastina Derfres, which my mother, Queen Melisende, gave to the abbot and monks of Saint Sabas for the salvation of her soul, and which the aforesaid canons of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] purchased from those monks of Saint Sabas [Col. 1235B] for a price [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads pretio, “for a price,” rather than precio.].

I confirm the gift of the land which Vivian, lord of Haifa, with the consent of his son Pagan, gave to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”] within and outside the city of Old Haifa [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads intus, “inside,” rather than interius, “within.”]. I also confirm the land which the two knightly brothers, Roger and John, gave to the same church beside the river of Haifa.

Finally, I confirm to the same Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads “the Church of the Holy Sepulchre.”] one half of all offerings that come and will come to the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Sepulchri, “of the Sepulchre.”], in every respect and entirely, just as the venerable Patriarch Arnulf, with the counsel of the first King Baldwin, assigned them to the aforesaid canons.

As for the wax that comes to the church, I confirm two parts of it to the same church for the lights.

I also confirm to the same canons all offerings that come to the Life-Giving Cross, except those made solely on Good Friday, or if the patriarch should carry it with him for some necessity.

I likewise confirm to the same canons the tithes of the entire holy city of Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Ierusalem.] and of the places adjacent to it, which the aforementioned patriarch granted them, except only the tithes of the estates.

Finally, I confirm, in the manner stated above, the Church of Blessed Peter in Joppa, which the frequently mentioned patriarch granted to the aforesaid canons with its full dignity, with all its honor intact and with everything belonging to the holy mother church [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads “belonging to the mother church.”]. I also strengthen for the same canons the Church of Quarentena [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Quadrantena.] with its appurtenances.

I therefore grant all these things, as they have been mentioned above, to the aforementioned church and to the aforesaid community serving God there, now and in succession, to be held freely, peacefully, and without any calumny or impediment in the future, and to be possessed by perpetual right. I confirm them by this present document, marked by the witnesses written below and by the impression of my seal [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads suppressione, “by the application/impression of my seal,” rather than subpressione.].

This document was made in the year 1164 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 12. The witnesses to this matter are:

[Col. 1236A] John, bishop of Paneas; Richard, bishop of Andria; Ralph [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Radulphus.], prior of Sebaste [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Sebastenus.]; Walter, prince of Galilee; Humphrey of Toron, constable; and his son Humphrey; Gerard of Sidon; Philip of Naples; Hugh, lord of Caesarea; Guy Francigena, seneschal [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads senescalcus.]; Fulk of Tiberias; Gormund of Tiberias; Henry Bubalus; Odo of Saint-Amand, cupbearer; William [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Guillelmus.], marshal; Roard [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Rohardus.] of Naples; Baldwin, viscount of Naples; Anselm of Brie; Roard [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Rohardus.] of Joppa; Pagan of Voh; Jocelin Pessellus [Note: [Col. 1235] B reads Pesellas.]; Otto of Risberge.

[Col. 1236B] Given at Ascalon, through the hand of Lord Ralph, bishop of Bethlehem and chancellor of the king, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of August.

## CXLV [Note: [Col. 1235] A, folio 125 recto; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE OF THE EXCELLENT KING JOHN AND THE MOST NOBLE QUEEN MARIA OF FRANCIA CONCERNING THE GREAT GARDEN

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, John, by the grace of God tenth king of the Latins of Jerusalem and count of Brienne, and Lady Maria, my wife, illustrious queen, grant and confirm to you, Sancio, prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and to the entire chapter of that church, present and future, the garden which is near Acre, which you purchased [Col. 1236C] from William Pomaranus, together with the houses and land within the circuit of that same garden, and everything belonging to the garden, just as you purchased it from the aforesaid William Pomaranus.

Moreover, for the salvation of our souls and those of our predecessors, we give and remit to you all rights that we ought to have in that garden.

We also grant and give you permission to sell freely, without any exaction or contradiction, the fruit and vegetables of the aforesaid garden upon our mounts [Note: The text has nostras, “our”; it probably should be corrected to vestras, “your.”] throughout the city of Acre, and to possess that garden with its appurtenances peacefully and freely forever.

But so that this grant, gift, and confirmation of ours may remain valid and unshaken forever, we have ordered this present charter to be secured with our seal and the witnesses written below [Col. 1236D].

The witnesses to this matter are:

Walter of Montbéliard, constable of the kingdom of Jerusalem; Ralph of Tiberias, the king’s seneschal; James of Durnay, the king’s marshal; Aymar, lord of Caesarea; Philip of Ibelin; Guy of Montfort; Garnerius the German; Roard, lord of Haifa; Amion d’Ays; Thomas of Maugastel; Daniel of Molembec; Adam Coste.

[Col. 1237A] This was done at Acre, in the year 1211 from the Incarnation of the Lord, on the Kalends of July, [through the hand] of the nota[ry] Baldwin.

## CLII [Note: [Col. 1237] A, folio 128 recto; absent from B.] THE PATRIARCH’S OATH

I, patriarch of Jerusalem, from this hour onward shall be faithful and obedient to blessed Peter, to the holy apostolic Roman Church, and to my lord Pope Innocent and his canonically succeeding successors.

I shall not participate in counsel or action whereby they might lose life or limb, or be captured in an evil captivity. The counsel which they entrust to me, whether in person, through their messengers, or by letter, I shall not knowingly reveal to anyone to their harm.

I shall be their helper in retaining and defending the Roman papacy and the regalia of Saint Peter, subject to my order, against every person.

I shall treat honorably the legate of the Apostolic See whom I know for certain to be its legate, both on his departure and on his return, and I shall assist him in his necessities.

When summoned to a synod, I shall come unless prevented by a canonical impediment.

Every four years I shall visit the thresholds of the Apostles, either in person or through my messenger, unless I remain away by apostolic permission.

I shall neither sell, give away, pledge, newly enfeoff, nor alienate in any other way the possessions belonging to the table of my patriarchate without consulting the Roman pontiff.

So may God help me and these holy Gospels.

## CLIII [Note: [Col. 1237] A, folio 128 recto; absent from B.] UPON RECEIVING THE PALLIUM

For the honor of almighty God, blessed Mary the Virgin, the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, Lord Pope Innocent, and the Roman Church, as well as the church entrusted to you, we give you the pallium taken from the body of blessed Peter—that is, the fullness of pontifical office—so that you may use it within your church on the specific days expressed in the privileges granted to your church by the Apostolic See.

## CLIV [Note: [Col. 1237] A, folio 128 verso; B, folio 129 verso.] THE OATH OF THE KINGS OF JERUSALEM [Note: [Col. 1237] B reads “The oath of the kings.”]

I, Aimeric, by divine permission king of Jerusalem who am to be crowned [Note: [Col. 1237] B reads Ierusalem, “of Jerusalem.”], promise to you, Lord Patriarch Monachus, and to your successors, under the witness of almighty God and of the whole Church [Note: [Col. 1237] B reads tocius, “of the entire Church.”], that from this day forward I shall be your faithful helper and defender, and the faithful helper and defender of all persons in the kingdom of Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 1237] B reads Iherosolimitani, “of Jerusalem.”].

I shall maintain and defend the possessions of the Church of Jerusalem and of all the churches that have a primary relationship to it, which they formerly used to possess and which they are justly to acquire in the future during our times.

I shall preserve the canonical privileges, due laws and justice [Note: [Col. 1237] B reads iusticias, “justices.”] of those churches, as well as their former customs and practices of liberty, both theirs and those of all the people of the land, just as King Amalric and King Baldwin, his son [Note: [Col. 1237] Supplied from B.], maintained them. With the Lord’s help, I shall provide as much defense as I am able, and I shall abolish the new impositions introduced especially after the destruction of the land, just as a Christian and faithful king ought rightly to provide in his kingdom for every bishop, church entrusted to him, and the people.

So may God help me and these most holy Gospels.

[Col. 1238C] Then, after the crown has been placed upon the king’s head, the patriarch shall take his right hand and promise in this manner:

“And I shall help you to maintain and defend justly the crown placed by us upon your head [Note: [Col. 1237] Supplied from B.], subject to my order,” giving him a kiss.

Let the other persons likewise promise him in the same manner and give him a kiss.

## CLV [Note: [Col. 1237] A, folio 129 recto; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE VILLAGE OF FENICULUS, ITS LIBERTY AND THE BOUNDARIES OF ITS LAND

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, amen.

Since all Catholic men, and especially the powerful who have been endowed with divine gifts, ought to honor and exalt all the churches of God, they ought especially to raise up and enrich with their benefits the church of the most glorious Sepulchre, where the Lord suffered and died and, rising on the third day, restored the salvation of the human race, so that, when they have completed the course of this life, they may deserve to possess the boundless joys of eternal life.

Therefore I, Hugh, by the grace of God lord of Caesarea in Palestine, with the consent of my wife Isabel and the counsel of my good men, give and grant to Peter, prior, and the Latin canons of the Holy Sepulchre the mountains adjoining the garden of Feissa, where the spring of the watercourse rises.

The boundary begins on the other side of the land at the road that comes from Braicaet toward the village of the Holy Sepulchre [Col. 1239A]. It proceeds eastward through the ravine between two mountains, namely along the torrent that flows in winter, until it reaches the small mountain situated between the aforesaid mountains and the mountains of Broiquet. From the bed of the torrent it goes toward the aforesaid small mountain and along the crest of that small mountain, as the crosses indicate, until the aforesaid boundary reaches the small hill called the Lime Kiln. From there it extends southward to another small hill not far away, where the ancient lime kiln stood. It then runs down the slope of the mountain in a straight line toward the ridge situated on the plain, which divides the land of the village of the Lord’s Sepulchre, Faisse, from that of Sabarim belonging to the Hospital [Col. 1239B], and there it ends.

I also grant and confirm the boundary which the aforesaid canons of the Holy Sepulchre established with George and his son Baldwin.

Furthermore, I confirm the gift made to the aforementioned canons by my grandfather Eustace and my father Walter, as well as the boundaries which they marked out, and I promise to defend them.

In addition, we grant the canons of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre this liberty: throughout all my land, both in the city of Caesarea and outside it, they may freely and peacefully, exempt from every toll and exaction, sell or buy, weigh or measure, and transport by sea or land.

For the gift of the aforesaid land, the confirmation of the boundaries, and the aforementioned liberty, the canons generously pay me four hundred bezants [Col. 1239C].

I have also retained this right: if at any time I wish to repair the ancient watercourse of the aforesaid spring and lead the spring to the village of Bubalorum in order to make channels, I may do so without contradiction from the aforesaid canons. This is on the condition, however, that for one maceria I pay the aforesaid church one-half quintal each year, and, if there is more, a full quintal.

So that all these things which we have recorded may remain firm and unshaken in the order in which we have stated them, I confirm them by the affixing of my seal.

This charter was made in the year 1166 from the Incarnation of the Lord, indiction 15.

The witnesses to this matter are recorded, whose names appear below:

[Col. 1239D] Rainerius, bishop of Sebaste; Ralph, provost; John, cantor of Caesarea; Simon, canon; Arnulf, subprior; Peter Lombard; Brother Adam; Brother Vitalis; Peter of Mahomeria; Peter Costa, viscount; Engelbert of Aria; Charles Hamelinus; Robert of Cossia; George; Baldwin, his son.

If, however, I should wish to make another watercourse and lead the spring to the aforesaid village by another route, no one shall contradict me.
