## CLX [Note: [Col. 1239] A, folio 136 recto; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING THE CHURCH AT NAPLES

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father [Col. 1240B], Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

A[malricus], by the grace of God patriarch of the Holy Resurrection of Christ, to P[eter], prior of the same church, and to all the canons, present and future, forever.

Since the most holy Church of the Lord’s Resurrection, by a certain special prerogative of holiness, is deservedly venerated with the greatest devotion by all Christian people, and since, with pious regard to the restoration of humanity, it is rightly proclaimed by all worshipers of God to be the fountain and origin of the universal Church, we who, by God’s assent, preside over the aforesaid church have wished to honor it especially and to labor diligently for the enlargement of its possessions.

Moved, therefore, by the requests of our beloved son Amalric, illustrious king of Jerusalem [Col. 1240C], and likewise assenting to your just petitions, pleasing to God, with the consent and counsel of our venerable brother Hugh, abbot of the Temple of the Lord, we grant to you, Peter, prior, and to your successors, as well as to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, present and to be canonically appointed in the future, the church which you founded at Naples, on the land which the aforesaid king had given you for this purpose.

With the full extent of parochial rights, and by the patriarchal authority granted to us by God, we confirm this church, decreeing that, since it is known to have been founded under the title of the Lord’s Passion and of His Resurrection, it shall have full power to baptize, to reconcile women after childbirth to God and the Church, to absolve the sick throughout the city and give them Communion, to bury the dead, and to retain forever for your use, without any calumny, the tithes of all labor arising from your own expenses, in their entirety.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person should presume to violate this privilege by rashly acting against it, let that person be separated from the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ and, unless he repents and comes to make satisfaction, let him remain perpetually subject to the penalty with which the Lord threatens all the accursed. But let peace and mercy from the Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe it, in this age and in the age to come.

[Col. 1241A] So that this privilege of ours may remain firm, fixed, stable, and unshaken, it pleased us to secure it with the impression of our leaden seal and to confirm it by the truthful testimony of the witnesses written below. The witnesses to this matter are:

The illustrious Lord King Amalric; Ralph of Bethlehem, Rainerius of Lydda, and Rainerius of Sebaste, bishops; Rudolph, prior of Sebaste; Hameric, prior of Mount Olivet; Guilricus, dean of Naples; Rudolph, archdeacon; Amalric, chancellor; Master Heraclius; Robert of Pinchinec; Geoffrey of Tours; Baldwin, viscount of Naples; Master Stephen.

Given at Jerusalem, in the year 1168 from the Incarnation of the Lord, sixty-nine years from the capture of Jerusalem.

## CLXI [Note: [Col. 1241] A, folio 137 recto; absent from B.] CONCERNING THE CHURCH OF SAINT NICHOLAS, WHICH IS OUTSIDE THE WALLS OF JOPPA

[Col. 1241B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Amalric, by the grace of God patriarch of the Church of the Holy Resurrection of Christ, to his beloved sons P[eter], prior of the same church, and to all the canons, present and future, forever.

Since the most holy Church of the Lord’s Resurrection, by a certain special prerogative of holiness, is deservedly worshiped with the greatest devotion by all Christian people, and since, with pious regard to the restoration of humanity, it is rightly proclaimed by all worshipers of God to be the fountain and origin of the universal Church, we who, by God’s assent, preside over the aforesaid church [Col. 1241C] wish to honor it especially and to labor diligently for the enlargement of its possessions.

Assenting, therefore, to your just petitions, pleasing to God, we grant to you, Peter, prior, and to your successors, as well as to the canons of the Holy Sepulchre, present and to be canonically appointed in the future, the Church of Saint Nicholas, which is constructed outside the walls of the city of Joppa, on the northern side, on the mound of Saint Nicholas above the sea.

With the full extent of parochial rights, and by the patriarchal authority granted to us by God, we confirm it, decreeing that, since the aforesaid Church of Saint Nicholas is known, through the house and grant of our most beloved son Amalric, illustrious king of Jerusalem, to pertain to the title of the Lord’s Passion and of His Resurrection [Col. 1241D], it shall have full power to baptize, to reconcile women after childbirth to God and the Church, to absolve the sick throughout the city and give them Communion, to bury the dead, and to retain forever for your use, without any calumny, the tithes of all its possessions, lands, and vineyards, which it now has or may be able to have in the future, with God’s help, in their entirety.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person should presume to violate this privilege of ours by acting against it, let that person be separated from the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ and, unless he repents and comes to make satisfaction, let him remain perpetually subject to the penalty with which God threatens all the accursed [Col. 1242A]. But let peace and mercy from the Lord Jesus Christ be with all who observe it, in this age and in the age to come.

So that this privilege of ours may remain firm, fixed, stable, and unshaken, it pleased us to secure it with the impression of our leaden seal and to confirm it by the truthful testimony of the witnesses written below. The witnesses to this matter are:

Ralph of Bethlehem; Rainerius of Lydda; Rainerius of Sebaste, bishops; Ralph, prior of Sebaste; Haimeric, prior of Mount Olivet; Ralph, archdeacon; Amalric, chancellor; Master Heraclius; Hugh of Jerusalem; Robert of Pinchinee; Geoffrey of Tours.

[Col. 1242B] Given at Jerusalem, in the year 1168 from the Incarnation of the Lord, sixty-nine years from the capture of the holy city.

## CLXII. PRIVILEGE OF THE CHURCH OF JOPPA

(See under Alexander III, for the year 1181.)

## CLXIII [Note: [Col. 1241] A, folio 139 recto; absent from B.] CONCERNING THE LIBERTY OF THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE WHICH IS SITUATED AT TROYES

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen.

In the year 1171 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the month of February, indiction 4, William, humble bishop of the Church of Troyes.

The more holy and venerable places are recognized to be esteemed and cherished before God and human beings, the more they are shown by the authority of both the Old and the New Testament to be venerated and protected by the faithful who fear God and belong to the mother Church, and, if necessary, relieved of the burden of temporal servitude.

For this reason the Lord commanded holy Moses not to approach the burning bush except with bare feet, and a forty-day fast was imposed on the magnificent prophet Elijah so that, having been sanctified, he might pass to the mountain of God, Horeb.

King and prophet David considered this when he said: “Lord, I have loved the beauty of your house and the place where your glory dwells.”

The Lord Christ too, promulgator of evangelical grace and author of our redemption, bore witness to this matter when, having made a whip of cords [Col. 1242D], he drove the sellers and buyers from his holy temple, saying: “My house shall be called a house of prayer.”

The consideration of this matter therefore often humbles and compels the minds of exalted powers, so that they may greatly fear and honor in these places the holy souls dedicated and given over to the service of God, and diligently attend to their just requests.

Therefore, venerable Peter, prior of the holy congregation of the Lord’s Sepulchre, we have decided to assent to the worthy requests of your honesty and prudence and of your brothers. We show ourselves all the more readily favorable to your wishes because we know that you serve the most holy place from which the holiness of the Christian religion took its beginning throughout the ends of the world, as it is written: “From Zion the law and the word shall go forth . . .”

After consulting the whole counsel of our chapter, in the presence of our brothers, who assented and praised the act, we have remitted forever the annual census—namely, one ounce of gold—which your church, situated at Troyes and called the Holy Sepulchre, was obliged to pay annually to our cathedra. We have reserved only this condition: that each year you pay our see one pound of wax and another of incense.

If anyone should presume to oppose this remission of ours, let him be struck by the sword of our anathema.

So that this remission of ours may remain stable forever, we ordered you, William of Bayeux, our notary, to write this brief; we fortified it with this sign of the cross made by our own [hand] [Col. 1243B], and strengthened it with our seal, with our canons written below as witnesses, at the city of Troyes, successfully.

I, William, third bishop of Troyes.

I, William, dean of Troyes.

I, Mysandus, archdeacon of Troyes.

I, John son of Landulf, precentor of the Church of Troyes.

I, Thomas, archpriest of the Mount and canon of Troyes.

I, John Mannus, canon and priest.

I, Castorius, canon of Troyes.

I, Theobald, canon.

I, John Rao . . . .

I, Gar . . . ., canon and deacon.

[Col. 1243C] I, Alfericus, canon and treasurer.

I, Nicholas, canon and priest.

### CLXIV. [Note: [Col. 1243] A, folio 140 verso; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE OF THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE, WHICH IS SITUATED NEAR TROIA

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1171, in the month of March, in the fourth indiction, on the sixth day after the beginning of the month, I, Raginald, chaplain of William, the third bishop of Troia, renounced into the hands of the aforementioned bishop the annual rent of one ounce of gold which I held from the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, situated at Troia. Therefore, through grace alone, Peter, prior of the Holy Resurrection, together with his brothers, gave me five and a half ounces of gold, in the presence of:

[Col. 1243D] William, dean of Troia; Musand, archdeacon; John Landulfi, cantor; Master Thomas, archpriest of Mons; John Manni; and other good men.

[Note: [Col. 1243] The manuscript repeats the words “and John.”]

### CLXV. [Note: [Col. 1243] A, folio 140 verso; absent from B.] GIFT OF A CERTAIN HOUSE TO THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

In the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1171, in the month of April, in the fourth indiction, while our most glorious lord William II, king of Sicily, duke of Apulia and prince of Capua, was happily reigning in his fifth year, amen.

I, Ansaldus, castellan of the sacred palace, by the grace granted by the most holy royal majesty, moved by divine love [Col. 1244A] and for the remission of my sins, before the presence of the sacred royal court, of my own free will gave, transferred, and granted in perpetuity to the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre my house, which I possessed at Messina, with all its appurtenances, as I held it, and which I caused to be built at my own expense.

It is contiguous with the city wall outside the main gate that leads to Saint John of the Hospital. This house lies between the dyer’s house, the house formerly belonging to Bonus Prolupus, the city wall, and the public road.

I therefore caused the house itself, with its entrance and exit and all its appurtenances, as I held it, to be assigned to Lord Peter, venerable prior of that Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and to two of his fellow canons, Brother Achilleus and Brother Baldwin, [Col. 1244B] who received it for the use of that Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre.

So that this gift of mine might be held perpetually inviolable and secure, I ordered this document to be written by the hand of Robert, my notary; I confirmed it with the sign of the holy cross made by my own hands; and I asked the witnesses subscribed below to testify to it in the same charter.

I, Nicholas, by the grace of God first archbishop of Messina, was present, and grant and affirm.

I, Thomas, bishop of Cassano, was present and subscribed.

Sign of the hand of Bartholomew de Placza, chief justiciar of the great royal court, witness.

[Col. 1244C] I, Gualterus de Moac, master constable of the royal privy chamber, am witness.

Sign of the hand of John Burdon, chief justiciar of the great court.

I, Persicus, son of Saductus, chief justiciar of the greater royal court.

I, Robert, son of the aforesaid Lord Ansaldus, castellan of the sacred palace, grant and affirm this.

### CLXVI. PRIVILEGE OF POPE ALEXANDER III

(See under Alexander III, for the year 1181.)

### CLXVII. [Note: [Col. 1243] A, folio 144 verso; B, folios 29 recto and 123 verso.] PRIVILEGE MADE BY AMALRIC, PATRIARCH OF JERUSALEM, FOR THE CANONS OF THE HOLY [SEPULCHRE], CONCERNING OFFERINGS

[Note: [Col. 1243] The heading is absent from B.]

[Col. 1244D]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Amalric, by the grace of God patriarch of the Church of the Holy Resurrection, to his beloved sons Peter, prior, and all the canons of that same church, present and future, forever.

Because the most sacred Church of the Lord’s Resurrection, by a certain special prerogative of holiness, is rightly venerated with the utmost devotion by all Christian people, and because, with pious regard for the restoration of humanity, it is truly proclaimed by all who worship God to be the fountain and origin of the whole Church, we who, by God’s assent, preside over the aforementioned church wish to honor it with still greater care and, with fatherly affection, to love you who regularly serve the Lord in it through divine offices as special sons, to cherish you in the bosom of our care [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *intuicionis*.], and, with God’s help, to labor diligently for the increase of your possessions. [Col. 1245A]

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, pleasing to God, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Lords Arnulf and William, patriarchs, and pursuing with pious eagerness their statutes, which are known to have been both just and sanctioned for you by privileges of apostolic authority, we decree, grant, and confirm, by the authority granted to us by God, that all the possessions and goods which you presently possess, whether here or overseas, through the gift and grant of those same patriarchs, through the generosity of kings or princes, through the largesse of other faithful people, by purchase or exchange, or by any other means, or which in the future, with the Lord’s help, you may justly and canonically acquire, shall remain perpetually firm and unimpaired for you and your successors canonically appointed in the aforementioned Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre. We also fortify them with the privilege of this present document.

Of these possessions and rights we have thought it appropriate to state the names expressly:

First, one half of all the offerings that belong or are brought [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *defferentur*.] to the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *Sepulchrum*]; but of the wax the church shall always have two parts—one for preparing the lights, the other for the canons’ service—while the third shall accrue only to our use and that of our successors. [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *ecclesia partes*; B, *tercia*.]

Likewise, all the offerings of the Life-Giving Cross, which is entrusted to your keeping, except on Good Friday alone, or when necessity [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *necessitas*.] compels us or our successors to carry it on campaign; and likewise the great altar in your choir, with all the offerings accruing to it, we confirm to you.

We also confirm to you the prison and its altar, with everything offered there; the altar of Saint Peter and Saint Stephen and the Finding, with all its altars and offerings; the altar at the head [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *caput*.] of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *Sepulchri*], the parish altar with its offerings [Note: [Col. 1245] Supplied from B]; the seat behind the great altar, and everything offered there or at any of the aforesaid altars when the patriarch celebrates Mass, whether offered into his hand or at his foot; and all the offerings of the *compassus* (the meaning of this term is uncertain) situated in the middle of your choir.

We also confirm the square between the church door and the columns, and the other square between those same columns and the Hospital of Saint John, as it extends in length and breadth; furthermore, the houses, shops, lands, and whatever [Latin *qui[c]quid*] you possess in the church quarter and in our quarter, and may justly acquire thereafter; and all the other houses, shops, and lands that you possess within or outside Jerusalem.

Likewise, all the ovens of Jerusalem except two—one belonging to the Hospital and one belonging to the Latins—and especially that oven which we returned to you [Note: [Col. 1245] Latin *reddidimus*, restored from B], in the presence of Lord Peter, archbishop of Tyre, which we had held on loan from you. [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *specialiter*.]

Furthermore, the church and cemetery [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *cymiterium*.] outside the Gate of David beside the road leading to Bethlehem; also half of that possession which Baldwin [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *Baldewinus*.], the first king, gave to the aforementioned Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre in exchange for the bishopric of Bethlehem; all the tithes of the city of Jerusalem and of its entire [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *tocius*.] bishopric, except the tithes of the *funda*; twenty-one villages which Duke Godfrey gave to your church with their appurtenances; and the villages which you have built, such as Great Mahomeria [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “Mahomaria”], Little Mahomeria, and Bethsuri, and all the others which you will build, where Latins will dwell, with the full exercise of justice [Note: [Col. 1245] B, *iusticie*, for A *iustitie*.] and parish law.

Likewise, Tekoa with all its appurtenances, and the Church of Quarantena with its appurtenances; Geladia; the land which you bought from John Gomannus; and all the villages with their appurtenances which you bought from Hugh of Ibelin [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “Ybelino”].

The Church of Saint Peter in Jaffa, with the full extent of its honor and dignity; and the tithe which you receive throughout that county from the king, from religious men, [and from all] Christians [Note: [Col. 1245] Supplied from B].

Whatever you possess at Ascalon and in its territory; at Nablus and throughout its borders; whatever you possess under the power and lordship of the lord of Assur [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “Arsur”]; at Caesarea and throughout its archbishopric; the castle of Feniculus; the house beside Haifa [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “Cayphas”]; Gebul; and Lecara.

Everything also that you possess throughout the entire archbishopric of Nazareth, in the bishopric of Acre [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “the bishopric of Acon”], and throughout the entire archbishopric of Tyre; and likewise everything that you possess [Note: [Col. 1245] Omitted in B] or will possess throughout the whole patriarchate and kingdom of Jerusalem.

Likewise, whatever you possess at Mount Pilgrim and throughout the entire bishopric of Tripoli, in Antioch and throughout its entire patriarchate and principality, or whatever, with God’s gift, you may acquire in the future.

Furthermore, all the possessions that you hold overseas, such as in the kingdom of the king of Sicily, namely in Sicily itself, in Calabria, and throughout Apulia: first, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre at Brindisi with all its appurtenances; at Barletta, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “Sepulchri”] with all its appurtenances; and the Church of Troia with all its appurtenances.

Whatever you possess at Rome and throughout its territory; likewise in Tuscany [and] throughout all Italy [Note: [Col. 1245] Supplied from B; B spells Italy “Ytalia”], or whatever you will possess.

Moreover, everything that you possess throughout the whole kingdom of France and in all the provinces subject to it by right [Note: [Col. 1245] B reads “provinces”], as well as in all the kingdoms and counties of Spain, or wherever in the regions beyond the mountains the aforementioned Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre is known to possess [Col. 1247A] or may acquire in the future, by the Lord’s generosity.

All these things, and all other possessions which the devotion [Note: [Col. 1247] B, *devocio*.] of the faithful has bestowed or will bestow upon the most holy Church of the Sepulchre, already often mentioned, and upon you, in the regions of the aforesaid patriarchates, bishoprics, kingdoms, lands, or provinces, whether on this side of the sea or beyond it, with God in mind; and whatever you have acquired by purchase or otherwise, as we have said, or may thereafter acquire by just means with the Lord’s assistance; and likewise all the good and ancient customs of your church—we confirm and strengthen all these perpetually and irrevocably for you and your successors, without any reservation, while preserving, of course, the obedience and reverence owed to the patriarch of Jerusalem.

You shall indeed have free authority to dispose of these and your other possessions and goods, provided that you act with common counsel and for the honor of God and the benefit of your church. [Col. 1247B]

When the patriarch of Jerusalem dies or crosses overseas, the prior and canons who are then in that church shall faithfully guard and administer, both within and outside, the patriarch’s house and household and everything belonging to his right, until another patriarch has been appointed in accordance with God’s will, or until he himself returns, if he has crossed overseas.

Moreover, of the possessions which are held jointly by us, such as those in England, Denmark, Germany, Poland, Ruthenia, Avaria, Hungary, Constantinople [Note: [Col. 1247] B reads “Constantinopoli”] and throughout its territory, in which we are obliged to contribute half the expenses, we confirm one half to you.

If anyone should presume to violate this privilege of ours, let him be subject to the punishment which God has promised to all the accursed, unless he turns back from his presumption. But may grace and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ be with whoever preserves this privilege and upholds the rights of the holy Church of Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 1247] “Church” supplied from B].

So that this privilege of ours may remain firm, fixed, stable, and unshaken, we have decided to secure it with the impression of our lead seal and to confirm it by the truthful testimony of the witnesses subscribed below. The witnesses to this are:

Letard, archbishop of Nazareth; Hernesius [Note: [Col. 1247] B reads “Hernerius”], archbishop of Caesarea; William, bishop of Acre [Note: [Col. 1247] B reads “Aconensis”]; Bernard, bishop of Lydda; Absalon, formerly bishop of Ascalon; Reynald, abbot of Mount Zion; Raymond, abbot of the Temple of the Lord; Guido, abbot of Saint Mary of the Latins; Bernard, prior of Mount Olivet; Eraclius, archdeacon of Jerusalem; Arnulf [Note: [Col. 1247] B reads “Arnulphus”], chaplain; Geoffrey, steward; Robert of Picquigny.

Issued at Jerusalem [Note: [Col. 1247] B reads “Ierusalem”], in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1169.

### CLXVIII. [Note: [Col. 1247] A, folio 147 verso; absent from B.] GIFT OF A VINEYARD TO THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

[Col. 1248A] Let it be known to all people, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God patriarch of the Church of the Holy Resurrection, moved by piety and almsgiving, for the salvation of my soul, give and firmly grant to you, Peter, prior of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and to your chapter and church and your successors in perpetuity, the jurisdiction which I held over the vineyard that belonged to Peter of Saint James. It is evident that you bought from him the portion which that Peter held in the vineyard.

This vineyard has, on the east and north, the vineyard of the Latins; on the west, the royal road leading from the house of the lepers of Saint Lazarus toward Lake Leger; and on the south, the road leading from the Church of Saint Stephen to the same road.

You shall hold and possess it freely and peacefully, doing as you please with the aforesaid vineyard, its land, and its other appurtenances. It is stipulated, however, that both you and your successors, out of piety, must on the day of my death, in memory of me, provide food for thirteen poor people and thirteen other clerics, who shall sing psalms for my repose. Thereafter, every year forever, on the anniversary of my death, you shall feed thirteen poor people; and on Saint Michael’s Day you shall cause two candles, worth one bezant, to be brought every year to our chapel and to that of whoever succeeds to the patriarchate, there to be lit.

So that this agreement, gift, and grant may on both sides remain valid and inviolate at all times, I ordered this present document to be preserved as an everlasting memorial and strengthened by the affixing of my seal. [Col. 1248C]

This was done in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1177, in the eighth indiction, while Baldwin, by the grace of God sixth king of the Latins in holy Jerusalem, was reigning. The witnesses to this are:

Among the priest-canons of the Holy Sepulchre:

Hugh of Nigella; Constantine, deacon; Odo; Roger, subdeacon; Robert of Rome; Peter of Barcelona.

From my household:

Galfred, steward; Girard, chaplain; Peter, cleric; William, cross-bearer, who wrote this; Aldebert, cupbearer, at that time master of my household; Peter the Lombard.

[Col. 1248D] Issued by the hand of Master Monachus, chancellor, in the month of June.

### CLXIX. [Note: [Col. 1247] A, folio 148 verso; absent from B.] CONCERNING TWO *QUINTARIA* OF GRAPE-HARVEST, WHICH BALDWIN, SIXTH KING OF THE HOLY CITY OF JERUSALEM, GAVE TO THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, future and present, that I, Baldwin, by God’s grace sixth Latin king in the holy city of Jerusalem, give and grant, and by the authority of the royal majesty confirm, to God and the Church of the Holy Resurrection, and also to Peter, its venerable prior, and to all the canons serving God there now and destined to serve him forever, two *quintaria* of grapes from my vineyards near the Church of the Holy Cross, to be received, held, and possessed every year forever, in exchange for the tithe which they held in the vineyard beside the second [Note: [Col. 1249] This should probably be corrected to “Saint”] Procopius, which my lord and father, King Amalric of pious memory, gave to the Church of Mount Zion in exchange for Lake German, which is held in common for the use of the whole city.

Therefore, so that this gift of mine might remain forever valid and undissolved, I ordered this present charter to be secured and strengthened with my seal by the witnesses subscribed below.

[Col. 1249B] This was done in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1177, in the tenth indiction. The witnesses to this are:

William Marchisius, count of Ascalon and Jaffa; John of Assur; Anselm of Bria; Roard, castellan of Jerusalem; Peter de Creseca; Anselm d’Abim; William Patrum.

Issued at Jerusalem by the hand of Lambert, the lord king’s chaplain.

### CLXX. [Note: [Col. 1249] A, folio 149 recto; absent from B.] GIFT OF A CERTAIN VINEYARD SITUATED AT THE FOOT OF MOUNT ZION

In the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen; in the unity of the Trinity, amen.

[Col. 1249C] Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Rainald, by the grace of God humble minister of the most holy and primitive Church of Mount Zion, with the common agreement and consent of our chapter, give and grant the vineyard which we possessed at the foot of Mount Zion beneath the house called German’s, in order to make a lake for the common use of Christians, in exchange for that vineyard which Lord King Amalric gave us beside the Church of Saint Procopius.

We have also granted to it another small vineyard, adjoining the aforesaid vineyard on the south, at the crossroads beside the house of the aforementioned German.

Therefore, so that the aforesaid agreement may be held valid and secure, and the exchange and grant of this aforesaid small vineyard [Col. 1249D] may likewise remain so, and so that the aforesaid lake may freely serve the common use of Christians, we have taken care to strengthen this present charter with the seal of the community and church.

Done in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1176. The witnesses to this are:

Peter, abbot of Jehoshaphat; Lord Ribald, abbot of the Latins; Lord Roger, abbot of the Temple; Rohard, castellan; Anselm of Brie; Anselm Babic.

### CLXXI. [Note: [Col. 1249] A, folio 149 verso; B, folio 33 verso.] PRIVILEGE OF LORD WILLIAM, KING OF SICILY

[Note: [Col. 1249] This heading is absent from B.]

[Col. 1250A]

In the name of the eternal God and our Savior Jesus Christ, amen.

William, by the favor of divine clemency king of Sicily [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *Sycilie*.], duke of Apulia and prince of Capua.

Due honor must be shown to all churches and places devoted to religion; yet those which, by the privilege of divine power, possess greater glory deserve still greater reverence. Among these, the Lord’s Sepulchre [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *Sepulchrum*], just as it stands out by its more illustrious title, must likewise, out of Christian devotion, be honored with more distinguished worship.

Therefore, the ears of our clemency incline all the more readily to the prayers of the venerable community of that church, the more devotedly we cherish and venerate the mystery [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *mysterium*.] of our redemption celebrated there. [Col. 1250B]

At the petition, therefore, of Peter, venerable prior, and of the community of that church, we grant to the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and confirm with the protection of royal authority all the possessions and holdings which this church [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *ipsa*.] is presently known to possess in our kingdom by a legitimate title.

For the memory of this grant and confirmation of ours, and as an inviolable guarantee, we ordered this present privilege to be written by the hand of Alexander, our notary, and strengthened with a leaden bull [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *bulla plumbea*.] impressed with our seal-die, in the year, month, and indiction written below.

Issued in the fortunate city of Palermo, by the hand of Gualterus, venerable archbishop of Palermo; Matthew, [Col. 1250C] royal vice-chancellor; and Richard, venerable bishop of Syracuse [Note: [Col. 1249] B reads “Syracusani”], members of the lord king’s household; in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1178, in the month of April, in the eleventh indiction, and in the twelfth year of the reign of our lord William, by the grace of God magnificent and most glorious king of Sicily [Note: [Col. 1249] B reads “Sicily”], duke of Apulia and prince of Capua, happily, amen.

### CLXXII. [Note: [Col. 1249] A, folio 150 recto; B, folio 34 recto.] LETTER OF THE KING OF SICILY

[Note: [Col. 1249] This heading is absent from B.]

William, by the grace of God king of Sicily [Note: [Col. 1249] B, *Sycilie*.], duke of Apulia and prince of Capua, to the prelates of the churches, counts, justiciars, barons, chamberlains, bailiffs, and all his faithful subjects to whom this letter is shown: greeting and affection.

Out of regard for the divine majesty, in whose name we direct our vows and under whose name we happily establish every royal disposition, we deem it fitting reverently to honor throughout our kingdom the most sacred churches, monasteries, and venerable places established everywhere; to defend their claims; to uphold their rights; and mercifully to provide for their peace and tranquility. [Col. 1250D]

Therefore, by this present document we command and order all of you that you inflict no wrong or injustice [Note: [Col. 1251] B, *iniusticiam*, for A *iniustitiam*] upon the houses which the Church of the Holy Sepulchre possesses in Apulia, nor upon their people, obediences, or legitimate possessions and holdings, and that you do not permit any such wrong to be inflicted in any way. Nor shall you burden them in their rights or claims with unjust vexations.

You are to know that if anyone rashly opposes this command of ours, he will incur the indignation of our majesty.

Issued at Palermo, on the twenty-fifth day of April, in the eleventh indiction.

### CLXXIII. [Note: [Col. 1251] A, folio 150 verso; B, folio 34 verso.] GIFT OF BALDWIN RUFUS AND HIS WIFE ARTEMILIA

[Note: [Col. 1251] This heading is absent from B.]

Because through the passage of time, which is the mother of forgetfulness, the deeds or words of people can be erased or believed never to have existed unless they are committed to writing, I, Baldwin Rufus, and I, Artemilia, his wife, commit the following to written memory:

In the presence of Lord Peter, venerable prior of the Most Holy Sepulchre, and Master Robert, his fellow canon, and other brothers of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, we perpetually give one half of our entire house, as it stands, above and below, on the side of Saint John, so that he may make us fellow members and participants in their prayers and benefits [Note: [Col. 1251] B, *beneficiorum*, for A *benefitiorum*].

We stipulate that, for as long as we live, we may retain that house without mortgaging or selling it. If one of us should die, the other shall, if willing, be received wholly into the brotherhood of the aforementioned church. If not, he or she shall retain the house, with its profits, for as long as he or she lives; after that person’s death, it shall freely and absolutely revert to the same church.

This gift was made and granted in the year from the [Lord’s] Incarnation [Note: [Col. 1251] Supplied from B] 1178, in the eleventh indiction. The witnesses to this are:

Henry, priest; Brother Raymond; Bernard the Merchant; Stephen Corvesarius; Lord Saxo; Raymond Provincial [Note: [Col. 1251] B reads “Provincialis”]; Roland [Note: [Col. 1251] B reads “Rodlandus”]; Gerbinus the Pisan; and Lady Calva.

### CLXXIV. [Note: [Col. 1251] A, folio 151 recto; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE OF EXEMPTION FROM THE MILL TAX IN SICILY

Frederick, by the favor of divine clemency king of Sicily, duke of Apulia and prince of Capua.

What is granted to the most sacred churches and venerable places is pleasing to people and contributes to the salvation of souls. Therefore, considering the venerable religious character of the brothers of the Lord’s Sepulchre, in which the King of kings and Savior was pleased to be humanly buried, out of reverence for him and in recognition of the brothers’ honorable conduct, and also for the remedy of the souls of our august parents of blessed memory and for our own salvation, as well as out of regard for the worthiness of Brother Alexander, prior of the Church of Saint Andrew of Platia, which is an obedience of the aforementioned Lord’s Sepulchre, by our customary liberality we remit and perpetually release to that Church of Saint Andrew of Platia thirty-eight *salmae* of provisions, consisting of wheat and barley, which that church was accustomed to pay annually to our court from the tax on its mills in the territory of Platia. [Col. 1252A]

For the memory of this remission and release of ours, and for its perpetual force, we ordered this present privilege to be written by the hand of Nicholas of Petrali, our notary and faithful servant, and secured with the seal of our majesty, in the year, month, and indiction written below.

Issued at Platia in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1210, in the month of September, in the fourteenth indiction; and in the thirteenth year of the reign of our lord Frederick, by the grace of God glorious king of Sicily, duke of Apulia and prince of Capua, happily, amen.

### CLXXV. [Note: [Col. 1251] A, folio 151 verso; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE OF THE CHURCH OF TROIA AND OF THE CANONS OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE, BY WILLIAM, FORMER BISHOP OF TROIA

[Col. 1252B]

In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

In the year from his Incarnation 1182, and in the seventeenth year of the reign of our lord William, by the grace of God most invincible king of Sicily and Italy, son of the most holy King William, of illustrious and glorious memory, on the twentieth day of July, in the fifteenth indiction, William, by the grace of God fourth bishop of Troia, to Brother William, venerable canon of the Lord’s Sepulchre and prior of the Holy Sepulchre in the city of Troia, and to the Church of the Holy Resurrection, forever.

Although by the general obligation of the Christian profession we are bound, wherever we can, to assist all venerable places, we ought especially to love and [Col. 1252C] support the Church of the Lord’s Holy Sepulchre, where our life is hidden with Christ and from which, when he rose, it also rose with him in glory.

In other venerable places we venerate the members of Christ through the service of pious devotion; but in the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre we honor Christ, the head of the universal Church, with singular veneration. We celebrate the memory of his Passion, by which we were redeemed, and proclaim the glory of his Resurrection, through which we shall reign together with him.

Moved by due consideration of this special excellence, through which the aforesaid Church of the Lord’s Resurrection surpasses all others, we wish to provide something for its temporal benefit, whose spiritual benefit we continually experience.

Therefore, of our good and spontaneous will, and also at the prayers and with the consent of our beloved brothers, the canons of the Church of Troia, we grant and give to you, the aforesaid Brother William, prior of the Holy Sepulchre of Troia, and through you to the most sacred Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre, in perpetuity, one piece of land which until now belonged to our Church of Troia and is situated beside the circuit of our city.

Together with the same Troian canon-brothers, with our master of law present as our advocate in this affair, and with Nicholas, royal judge of Troia, present as the advocate of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre, we grant, give, and transfer it to you to possess in perpetuity, without opposition or claim from us or our successors, free and entire, and in every way useful to the church to which it is granted, as its boundaries are described below:

On the first side above, it lies beside the land of Bartholomew of Ruding; on the second side, descending and beside the valley which lies between this land and the land of the aforementioned Church of the Holy Sepulchre; and on the fourth side, ascending, it borders the public road by which one travels from the city to the River Aceloy.

So that this grant and gift of ours may possess perpetual and inviolable firmness, we ordered this present document to be prepared by the hand of Maraldus, [Col. 1253B] our notary, and strengthened by the affixing of our seal and by the subscriptions of our canon-brothers.

If any ecclesiastical or secular person should thereafter rashly presume to disturb this transfer and gift, and a second or third time [lacuna; the remainder is missing from the manuscript].

### CLXXVI. [Note: [Col. 1253] A, folio 152 verso; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING LACRIDON IN CYPRUS

In the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Hugh, by the grace of God king of Cyprus, give, grant, and confirm to God and to the Church of the Lord’s Sepulchre—namely, to its canons, present and future—as a perpetual alms for the souls of my father and mother and of all my predecessors, in the territory of Paphos, the *prastia* called Lacridon, with all its appurtenances in lands, waters, and villagers, and with all the rights and customs belonging to that *prastia*, together with five villagers, with their wives and children, present and future, and with all their belongings, including their *stagia* and *chevagia*.

The names of the aforesaid five villagers are these: Basil of Liquetima; Basil, son of the wife of Basil of Liquetima.

So that this gift of mine may remain valid and unshaken in perpetuity, I caused this present document to be secured with my lead seal and strengthened by the testimony of the men subscribed below, whose names are these:

Walter of Caesarea, constable of Cyprus; Aimeric of Rivet, seneschal of Cyprus; Rainald of Soissons, marshal of Cyprus; Walter of Bethsan; Gormund of Bethsan; Walter of Saint-Bertin; Simon of Paphos; Peter Chape; Walter the Younger.

Done in the year from the Lord’s Incarnation 1210, in the month of November.

### CLXXVII. [Note: [Col. 1253] A, folio 153 recto; absent from B.] CONCERNING THE VILLAGE OF PENDEKIO

[Col. 1254A]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Aimeric, by the grace of God ninth Latin king of Jerusalem and king of Cyprus, give, grant, and confirm to God and to you, Monachus, venerable patriarch of the Lord’s Sepulchre, and to your successors and the same chapter, in Cyprus, the village called Pendache, with all the right which I had or ought to have had in that village, to be held, retained, and possessed freely and peacefully in perpetual possession, without any service, together with all its appurtenances in lands, waters, and villagers, with all its rights and with all the customs belonging to that village.

This excludes the spring of Saint George with the ten surrounding ploughlands, which I had previously given to the Hospital of the Germans, and excludes the gifts which I and my brother, King Guy, gave to our men.

So that this gift of mine may remain valid and unshaken in perpetuity, I ordered this present document to be written, secured with my lead seal, and strengthened by the testimony of the men subscribed below, whose names are these:

Aimeric of Rivet, seneschal of Cyprus; Rainerius, librarian; Rainald of Soissons; Rustan Aymar; Rainald of Balma; William of Balma, his brother; [Col. 1254C] Simon of Paphos; Baldwin Usserius.

Done in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1201, in the month of March.

Issued at Nicosia by the hand of the venerable Alan, archbishop of Nicosia and chancellor of Cyprus, in the same year and month.

### CLXXVIII. [Note: [Col. 1253] A, folio 153 verso; absent from B.] LETTER OF LORD G. . . ., PATRIARCH OF JERUSALEM

G. . . . [Note: [Col. 1253] This initial may designate Gibelinus, Soffredus, also called Goffredus, or finally Giraldus, all three of whom combined the office of patriarch of Jerusalem with that of legate of the Holy See. In the absence of any chronological indication, I am inclined to believe that Giraldus is meant here, and that the document should be assigned to the period when this prelate, displeased with the truce concluded between Frederick II and the Saracens, had refused to restore the patriarchal see within the walls of Jerusalem.] by divine mercy patriarch of Jerusalem, humble and unworthy legate of the Apostolic See, to the clergy and people residing in Jerusalem: greeting in the Lord.

We wish your entire community to know that we have sent our beloved sons, the abbot of Mount Olivet and the dean of Jaffa, to Jerusalem to conduct our affairs and to seek and preserve our rights. Whatever may be done by them or by either of them, we shall hold to be ratified. We command and ask that you receive them in our place.

Issued at Jaffa, on the Kalends of January.

### CLXXIX. [Note: [Col. 1255] A, folio 153 verso; absent from B.] PRIVILEGE CONCERNING PALAFRUGELL AND TURICELLA OF MONTE RASO

[Col. 1255A]

This has been faithfully translated and transcribed. Let it be known to all that we, P[eter], by the grace of God king of Aragon and count of Barcelona, desiring with good intention and spontaneous will to carry out what the lord [Alfonso], king of illustrious memory and our father, bequeathed in his testament to the most glorious Sepulchre of the Lord for the remedy of his soul, approve, concede, give, and permanently deliver, by this instrument valid in perpetuity, to the Lord God, to that same Sepulchre of the Lord, and to all of you, the canons and brothers of that place, present and future, Palafrugell and Turicella of Monte Raso and Laufrigus [Col. 1255B] and Esclañá—our places or castles—with all their boundaries and appurtenances, both uncultivated and inhabited; with all their waters and streams, pastures, and fisheries of sea and land; with their fortifications, pleas, fines, and all dues; and with all their tributes, revenues, incomes, and produce; with hunting rights and discoveries, accessions and escheats of every kind; with the men and women who are there, or will be there, or may be there; and with all improvements and additions that you may in any way make there; and also with everything that we, or our predecessors, or anyone else, ever possessed, held, or received in the aforesaid places and their dependencies, for any reason or cause.

All these things, each and every one, we give and concede to the Sepulchre of the Lord, [Col. 1255C] and through you, our beloved B[eren]g[ar], prior of the house of the Holy Sepulchre of Barcelona, we deliver and relinquish them forever to that same Sepulchre of the Lord and to its canons and brothers, their present and future successors, to have peacefully, fully possess, and firmly and freely hold, according to all your wishes, in whatever manner it can best, most fully, soundly, and beneficially be expressed and understood, for the common good of the house of the Holy Sepulchre and of its brothers and canons, without any bond or reservation on our part or that of our heirs.

Therefore we firmly and strictly will and command all men and women inhabiting or hereafter inhabiting the aforesaid places and their boundaries to obey the aforesaid prior of the house [Col. 1255D] of the Holy Sepulchre of Barcelona, his successors, and those whom they may command or appoint, in all things and through all things, as your special and perpetual lords; and to render fully and faithfully to them everything, each and every thing, that you used in any way to render and give to us, without thereafter requiring any further order from us or from any bailiff or man of ours, or anyone’s consent.

Given at Zaragoza, on Monday, the first day after Pentecost, in the year 1250 of the Spanish era, by the hand of Ferrarius, our notary, with the following witnesses and persons present:

Lord R[aymond], venerable bishop of Zaragoza; Lord G. . . ., venerable [Col. 1256A] bishop of Huesca; Lord Eximenio Cornelii; Lord García Romero; Lord Michael of Lusia; Raymond, the treasurer.

And I, Avzar, together with many other clerics and laymen of our court and household.

The sign of Peter, by the grace of God king of Aragon and count of Barcelona.

I, Ferrarius de Guardia, the lord king’s notary, caused this to be written by his command, at the place, on the day, and in the year specified above.

### CLXXX. ON THE TITHES AND POSSESSIONS OF JERICHO

(See Alexander III, under the year 1181.)

### CLXXXI  
[Note: B, folio 102 verso; missing in A.]

### PRIVILEGE OF BERNARD, BISHOP OF THE CHURCH OF LYDDA

[Col. 1256B]

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that, for the good of peace and the preservation of complete concord, an agreement and concord was made between Lord Bernard, bishop of the church of Lydda, and Lord Peter, prior of the Sepulchre of the Lord, by their common will and with the consent of both chapters, in the presence and with the approval of Lord Patriarch Amalric, through the mediation of Heraclius, then archdeacon of Jerusalem, and Master Monachus, the lord patriarch’s chancellor.

Lord Bernard, bishop of Lydda, gave in full to the church of the Sepulchre of the Lord, to Peter the prior, and to all the canons and their successors forever one-half of the tithe of a certain village called Bermenayn, both in grain and in wine, oil, animals, birds, and everything else from which tithes are customarily given, all of which had previously belonged to him.

Lord Peter, the prior, with the counsel and consent of all the canons of the church of the Holy Sepulchre, granted to the church of Lydda, to Bishop Bernard, and to his successors one-half of all the tithes of the four villages recorded in the privilege of Roger, formerly bishop of Led—namely Capharuth and Git, Kephrecylta and Porfilia—so that, whereas previously the church of Lydda, through Bishop Roger, received from them only one-half of the grain tithes, as is contained in the text of that bishop’s privilege (he had given two of them, Capharuth and Git, and exchanged two, Kephrecylta and Porfilia), which gift and exchange we likewise hold ratified and firm, from the time this agreement was made it would receive in full one-half of all tithes, in grain, wine, oil, animals, and birds, except only the canons’ own provisions of animals and birds of every kind, which they now have and will have in the future in the aforesaid five villages—Bermenaym, Capharuth, Git, Kephrecylta, and Porfilia—and their dependencies. For these provisions they shall pay no tithes forever, by agreement. From everything else, however, both from the labor of the canons and from that of all others cultivating the aforesaid five villages, the church of Lydda shall receive one-half in full.

The aforementioned Bishop Bernard also gave, with the common consent of his chapter, out of piety and almsgiving, the churches built and to be built in those five villages, in their entirety and with all parochial rights, to the church of the Sepulchre of the Lord. He retained for himself and his successors the obedience of the parish priests who would be appointed there at the pleasure of the prior and canons of the Sepulchre of the Lord, and also retained their summons to the synod. They shall receive chrism and oil from the bishop of Lydda; they shall request, and must obtain, the consecration of altars or basilicas and the ordination of clerics who are to be advanced to sacred orders from that bishop and his successors; [Col. 1257B] and the priests of those five villages shall regard as under interdict and excommunication those whom the bishop of Lydda has placed under interdict or excommunicated. [Note: The manuscript has this as one word: “Allidensi.”] All other rights he left to them as a gift.

I, Bernard, bishop of Led, with the common consent of my chapter, and I, Peter, prior of the Sepulchre of the Lord, with the consent of the chapter of that same church, made this agreement in the year 1171 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth indiction, while Lord Amalric was venerable patriarch and the illustrious Amalric was reigning, the fifth king of Jerusalem. The witnesses to this agreement are:

From the chapter of the Sepulchre of the Lord:

Hugh of Nigella; Reginald of Loches; Peter [Col. 1257C] Calvus; Peter, cantor; Arnulf, subprior; Baldwin, treasurer—priests.

From the deacons:

Dalmatius; Savinus; Rogerius.

From the subdeacons:

Odo; Ingerradus and Peter.

From the chapter of Saint George:

Gislebertus, cantor; Franco; Peter, preceptor—priests.

From the deacons:

William; Peter Testa.

From the subdeacons:

Gerurfus; John and Papion.

The following were also present at this agreement:

[Col. 1257D] Lord Rainaldus, bishop of Hebron; Lord Heraclius, archdeacon of Jerusalem; and Master Monachus, the lord patriarch’s chancellor.

### CLXXXII  
[Note: B, folio 127 recto; missing in A.]  
[Without rubric.]

R[aymond], by the grace of God humble servant of Christ’s poor and faithful custodian of the Holy Hospital of Jerusalem, together with the entire community of brothers, to all their brothers who may read or hear this letter—clerics and laymen, both near and far, presently dwelling throughout the world under the title of the Hospital of Jerusalem—health in Christ for both the inner and outer person, and, after their daily labors, the happiness of eternal salvation.

By instruction in divine law, dearest brothers, we are salutarily taught, and by the holiest teachings of the holy fathers we are likewise sufficiently and reasonably enlightened, to take every possible care not to do to others what we do not wish others to do to us. For we brothers, who are professors of poverty in the house of the poor, where the poor and needy shall praise the name of the Lord, and who are appointed providers for poor brothers—not by the merit of our life but by the gift of divine dispensation—must not unjustly desire what belongs to others, but must faithfully distribute our own possessions, if we have any, to all in need.

For, according to Solomon’s saying, who, among the other secrets of his proverbs, records this very point according to the wisdom granted him by God: “To give alms from what has been seized from others is not an act of mercy but the profit of wickedness; for what is wrongly acquired by anyone is never bestowed well upon anyone.”

Therefore, dearest brothers, we command all of you, and in commanding admonish you in the Lord, and furthermore, by the highest and holiest obedience, enjoin upon you by the authority given to us by God for this very purpose, that whatever alms, possessions, churches, hospitals, towns, or anything else that can be enumerated, which, before it came into our hands, belonged or ought to have belonged by right to the Sepulchre of the Lord, you have until now perhaps negligently or unknowingly held, you should, upon receiving or hearing this command of ours, freely and peacefully leave to the bearers of the present letter and relinquish without any claim. Nor should you thereafter presume to take away or diminish anything from the alms of the aforesaid Most Holy Sepulchre or from the possessions assigned to it, or to retain anything already held.

We therefore wish all these things to be observed with the greatest care by all of you, by decree of our entire chapter, and command you all, in the truth of the Holy Spirit, to observe them, lest, if you act otherwise, you be found to resist God and us.

### CLXXXIII  
[Note: B, folio 123 recto; missing in A.]  
[Without rubric.]

F[ulcher], by the divine will of piety patriarch of the most holy church of the Resurrection of Christ our God, and A[malric], prior of that same church, together with the entire community of brothers, to all their brothers who may read or hear this letter—clerics and laymen, both near and far, presently serving throughout the world under the title and for the honor of the Sepulchre of the Lord—health in Christ for both the inner and outer person, and, after the course of this life, eternal happiness in perpetual salvation.

By instruction in divine law, dearest brothers, we are salutarily taught, and by the holiest teachings of the holy fathers we are likewise sufficiently and reasonably enlightened, to take every possible care not to do to others what we do not wish others to do to us. For we brothers, who serve God in the place of mercy, where, according to the testimony of the psalmist, mercy and truth have met, and justice and peace have kissed one another with charity and love, must maintain peace—with which no one shall see God—with all people, and especially with our household and our neighbors. We must also maintain justice, which gives each person what is his, above all other mortals.

For those who pursue justice must not unjustly desire anything belonging to others, but must faithfully distribute their own possessions, if they have any, to all in need. Therefore, dearest brothers, we command all of you, and in commanding admonish you in the Lord, and furthermore, by the highest and holiest obedience, enjoin upon you by the authority given to us by God for this very purpose, that whatever alms, possessions—namely gold, silver, cloth, and horses, houses and villages, fields and vineyards—possessions and churches, hospitals and towns, or anything else that can be enumerated, which, before it came into our hands, belonged or ought to have belonged by right to the Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem, you have until now perhaps negligently or unknowingly held, you should, upon receiving or hearing this command of ours, freely and peacefully leave to the bearers of the present letter and relinquish without any claim. Nor should you thereafter presume to take away or diminish anything from the alms of the aforesaid Hospital of Saint John of Jerusalem or from the possessions assigned to it, or to retain anything already held.

We therefore wish all these things to be observed with the greatest care by all of you, by decree of our entire chapter, and command you all, in the truth of the Holy Spirit, to observe them, lest, if you act otherwise, you be found to resist God and us.

### CLXXXIV  
[Note: B, folio 128 recto; missing in A.]

### PRIVILEGE OF THE SURIANS OF TURCHO CONCERNING THE REMISSION OF THE REVENUE OF THE DAVID GATE

In the name of the holy Trinity, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

Let it be known to all, present and future, that I, Amalric, by the grace of God fifth Latin king in the holy city of Jerusalem, give and concede to the Syrians of Turcho—Turcho being a village of the Holy Sepulchre—and to their heirs dwelling in that village, that they shall forever be free from the revenues which they used to pay each year to me and my predecessors at the David Gate of Jerusalem from their grape-clusters. Therefore, so that this concession of mine may remain ratified and firm for the aforesaid Surians and their heirs, I caused the present charter to be authenticated with the witnesses written below and with my seal.

This was done in the year 1171 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the fourth indiction. The witnesses to this matter are:

Hanfrid, constable; Milo de Placy; Rohard, castellan; Anselm de Passu; Guy de Maneriis; John de Valenciennes; [Col. 1260A] Adam Niger; Fulk Niger; Amalric de Franliu; Thomas Patricius; Girard Passerel; Arnulf, viscount; Amalric, his son; Robert de Pinkeny; Gilbert de Pinkeny; William the Norman; Herbert the Crooked; William Patronus.

Given at Tripoli, by the hand of Ralph, bishop of Bethlehem and the king’s chancellor, on the second day before the Ides of March.

The wife of Peter of Spain was our sister, and she died in our garden at Acre; she left us her house situated in Jerusalem, in Marescalky Street or in Saint Anastasia Street.

Likewise Bernard Bedevvin, our vicar and confrater, left us his house in Saint Anastasia Street, next to the house of Albert the Lombard.

These are the names of the old ovens:

First, in David Street, one oven. Before Saint James’ Gate, one oven. [Col. 1261A] Before the house of Rohard the castellan, one oven. An oven before the church of Saint Martin. An oven in the house called Gilbert de Pingeny’s. An oven in the street of Mount Zion. An oven before the church of Saint Thomas of the Germans. The oven of Saint Giles in the street of the Temple. An oven before the Butchery. The oven of the Tannerie. Rainald’s oven in the street of Kocatrice. Anastasia’s oven. The oven of Repoes. [Col. 1262A] The oven of the Jewry before Saint Elias’ Gate. Another in the Jewry behind Saint Agnes, toward the east. A new oven in the Jewry. Martin Karaoan’s oven. The oven at the head of Girard of Lisbon’s street. An oven in Tresmailes Street. The oven in Saint Stephen’s Street. The oven of Columba. The oven of Ruffeide beside Saint Chariton. The oven before the Gate of the Holy Sepulchre. Cecilia’s oven. The oven of Saint Pastor.

[Col. 1261]

### END OF THE PRIVILEGES OF THE CHURCH OF THE HOLY SEPULCHRE

[Col. 1261]

## PRIVILEGE OF BALDWIN I, KING OF JERUSALEM, FOR THE CHURCH OF BETHLEHEM  
### (Year 1110)

[WILLIAM OF TYRE, *History*, Book XI, chapter 12.]

[Col. 1261B]

By the inspiration of divine grace, the people of the Franks, admonished, freed the holy city of Jerusalem, long wearied by pagan oppression, from the aforementioned defilement. In that city, death—which had invaded the human race through the first transgressing parent—was destroyed by the death of the Savior. This city, worthy of divine worship, was besieged by the aforesaid people on the seventh day before the Ides of June and, with God fighting on its behalf, was captured on the Ides of July.

After the city had been captured in the year of the Lord 1100, by divine providence it pleased the clergy and the counts Raymond of Saint-Gilles, Robert of Normandy, and Robert of Flanders, Tancred, and the other leading men, together with the whole multitude of the Franks, that the most pious and merciful duke Godfrey, my beloved brother, should preside over it. He, [Col. 1261C] a man worthy of God and governor of the holy city, after completing the first year of his rule, by God’s favor, rested in peace on the third day thereafter.

I, Baldwin, therefore, amid the rejoicing clergy, princes, and people, the first king of the Franks by divine will, reflecting with radiant mind upon the excellence of the church of Bethlehem and upon the birth of our Lord Jesus Christ, in which place my venerable head had first shone, adorned with a diadem, was entirely pleased that it should be endowed with episcopal dignity. Accordingly, constantly reflecting upon what I had conceived in a pure heart, I eventually brought it to the ears of Arnulf, the most distinguished archdeacon, and of the chapter of Jerusalem, and I earnestly asked him and that chapter to advise me concerning this matter.

They, complying with my most just request, decided that a petition should be made to Rome both for the see of Jerusalem, which thereafter appeared almost deprived of its parent, [Col. 1262B] and for this matter. Arnulf the archdeacon and Aicard, then dean, undertaking this embassy, went to Rome. With the cooperation of the Holy Spirit, they found an honorable decision concerning both matters from Lord Paschal II, pontiff of the universal Church, and returned to Jerusalem.

Lord Pope Paschal then sent to Jerusalem, after them, Gibelin, archbishop of Arles, a man radiant with the beams of wisdom and shining with every moral virtue; he had entrusted this embassy to him in the presence of Arnulf and Aicard. Therefore, received joyfully by me, by the clergy, and by the people, and acting according to the command of Lord Pope Paschal, my good will, the consent of the chapter of Jerusalem, the favor of the entire council, and his own deliberation, he decreed that Aschetinus, an illustrious man governing the church of Bethlehem—the same man who, while cantor of that church, had been elected and appointed bishop of Ascalon by the chapter of Jerusalem, with my will and that of my nobles and people—should hold the episcopal primacy in the church of Bethlehem. According to our command and consideration, he subjected the church of Ascalon to the see of Bethlehem under parochial right.

Finally, I, Baldwin, by the grace of God king of Jerusalem, the first of the Latins, gladly and earnestly confirmed the foregoing. I also commanded, gave, and conceded that the town of Bethlehem, which I had granted to the church for the salvation of my soul, of my most merciful brother Duke Godfrey, and of all my relatives, together with one village in the territory of Acre called Bedar; another in the territory of Nablus called Seylon; another adjoining Bethlehem called Bethbezan; and two villages in the territory of Ascalon, one called Zeophir and the other Caicapha, with their appurtenances, should be firmly and freely held and possessed by the bishop and his successors.

I also freed the aforesaid church completely from the claim by which the church of Jerusalem had harassed it, by an exchange of lands and vineyards that lay within the circuit of Jerusalem and were in my domain.

We established that if any cleric or layman, driven by most detestable greed, should after my death presume to violate what, at my request, concerning the church of Bethlehem and the glorious birth of our Lord and Savior, with the assistance of the Holy Spirit, was confirmed by Lord Paschal, the supreme and venerable pontiff of the Roman see, through Gibelin, his legate and archbishop of Arles, he shall, unless he repent when admonished, be bound by the crime of invasion and shall be severely judged, deprived of the whole of our kingdom.

Furthermore, I concede that if any of my nobles, or any knight or burgess, inspired by the Spirit of God, wishes to give to that church from his revenues for the sake of his own soul and the souls of his family, he shall be free to carry out his pious will, and the lawful donation of his possessions shall remain valid forever.

This inscription of our concession or confirmation, and statement of the deeds accomplished, was made in the year 1110 from the incarnation of the Lord, in the third indiction, while Lord Paschal II presided as pope of the Roman Church; and in Jerusalem, with Gibelin, archbishop of Arles and vicar of the Apostolic See, elected patriarch. The witnesses to this declaration are:

Arnulf, archdeacon; Aicard, dean; Eustace Garner; [Col. 1264B] Anselm, keeper of David’s Tower; Ralph of Fornitet, Pisellus, viscount; Simon, the duke’s son; Anfred, a religious man; Gerard, chamberlain; and many others.

[Col. 1263]

## TWENTY-SIX LETTERS OF THE KINGS OF JERUSALEM, PRINCES, AND PRELATES TO LOUIS, KING OF THE FRANKS, THE SEVENTH OF THAT NAME, CALLED THE YOUNGER

(Bongars, *Deeds of God through the Franks*, I, p. 1172.)

### I. OF RAYMOND, PRINCE OF ANTIOCH

[Col. 1263C]

To the illustrious Louis, by the grace of God king of the Franks, his most devoted and diligent lord, R., by the same permission prince of Antioch, though unworthy, sends health and affection.

You have often heard, most excellent lord, of the oppressions and poverty of this land, and, unless God avert it, you will hear of them still more often. We can express neither by tongue nor by hand how this poverty and anxiety are endured, although the benign clemency of God has increased in our time.

The ears of all Christians are daily open and attentive, awaiting liberation through us, and asking, like John imprisoned, for the redemption of Jesus Christ through messengers sent by him (Matthew 11:2). Knowing that your heart is frequently intent upon the liberation of this land, they pray daily to God on bended knees for your exaltation, that he may grant you not only the will but also the ability, since the hearts of kings are in his hands, so that this land may be visited by you and freed from the hands of the wicked.

I, born and raised among your native men, am ready to fulfill your command. There are also here two daughters of Prince Raymond, who have reached marriageable age and are exceedingly beautiful in face and body. On their behalf we humbly implore your excellence to deign to give them in marriage in your land, for the honor of their lineage, since in this land, because of the harshness [reading uncertain] of the land itself and their kinship, we could not marry them.

Moreover, I humbly beseech your discernment to deign to pursue, as justice and right demand, the recovery of my patrimony, which they unjustly and forcibly took from me and mine, as is also plainly evident to everyone. May your affection often deign to write back to us concerning your well-being, which we desire to hear about. We, by the mercy of God, are healthy and safe. Milo de Nealphis, your knight and man, will tell you plainly by word of mouth about the state of this land.

### II. OF GILBERT, MASTER OF THE HOSPITAL

To Louis, most powerful lord, by the grace of God most glorious king of the Franks, Gilbert, servant of Christ’s poor and, by God’s mercy, master of the Hospital of Jerusalem, sends greetings, together with the entire community of brothers, and himself in Christ.

[Col. 1265A]

The Lord has made known our weakness, pious king: that the goods and possessions which pilgrims, undertaking the journey to Jerusalem with holy devotion in order to see the holy Resurrection of Christ, [may] remain safe and unharmed under the shelter of your hand. [The transmitted text is syntactically defective.] For this reason we beseech your highness to administer such justice concerning certain wrongdoers who, through their wickedness, burned the land of a worthy man, namely William of Donperre, while he himself remained in Jerusalem, that no one who hears of it may thereafter dare to do anything similar. Farewell.

### III. OF AMALRIC, KING OF JERUSALEM

[Col. 1265B]

To Louis, by the grace of God most glorious king of the Franks, Amalric, by that same grace king of Jerusalem, sends greetings.

We believe that your serenity has learned from the truthful reports of many, dearest one, that after, by reason of our sins, the prince of Antioch was captured by the Turks, and all his men were lost and overwhelmed either by captivity or by death, sudden destruction unexpectedly followed.

For an earthquake unheard of since the beginning of the world leveled castles, towers, towns, and almost everything both in the mountains and on the plains, both in Antioch and in all the regions adjoining it—at one moment on the plains, at another in the mountains—and, alas, consigned an innumerable multitude of Christians of both sexes to sudden death, extinguished them, and, to speak more truly, swallowed them into the earth.

To increase misery and complete utter desolation, that illustrious and excellent king, the shield and strength, after God, of the Eastern Church, and especially the one unshakable and saving hope and confidence of the kingdom of Jerusalem, the heartfelt friend of you and your kingdom, our lord and brother, the most Christian King Baldwin, has entered the way of all flesh—alas, alas!

His passing, grief, and desolation are therefore all the more inconsolable and violent because, by God’s agency, in him and through him the whole Christian community had ready assistance and sufficient strength against every hostile force. It is for this reason, dearest one, that, bowing before your majesty like features hanging from the head, we recognize your serenity in Christ as our support, the bronze foundation and unconquerable citadel of the divine faith, and we profess in the Lord that our humility is your special concern.

Let the abundance and perfection of true charity that existed in the king of Jerusalem, your friend of blessed memory, now be manifest to all through God’s cause, through his unconquerable love, and through the desolation of the Eastern Church. For, as your innate holiness has most truly learned from the most pious intention of your predecessors and of your entire lineage, your house has always, by honorable custom and purpose, protected, cherished, supported, and strengthened in the Lord the kingdom over which you preside, the holy city and the entire region adjoining it, and all who bear the mark of the Catholic faith.

Therefore, if the Spirit of counsel has inspired your magnificent serenity with the desire, for the greater increase of your crown, to visit again the place where the Lord’s feet stood bodily, do not refuse or delay to come now, at least urgently, in this great necessity and manifold anxiety of Christendom. In your holiness all our prayers converge, and, at your will and under your friendly command, we and our entire kingdom will labor with due devotion to God.

For the rest, we commend to your fatherly care the bearer of this letter, a man of great integrity and the venerable archbishop of Mamistria, zealous in carrying out every good work. Receive him kindly and believe him as you would believe our own mouth. We have entrusted him with our secrets so that he may explain them to you face to face, lest we exceed the brevity appropriate to a letter. Farewell.

### IV. OF A[malric], PATRIARCH OF THE HOLY RESURRECTION

A., by the grace of God patriarch of the Church of the Holy Resurrection, to his dearest son Louis, by the same grace illustrious king of the Franks, sends greetings and triumph over all enemies.

Since divine dispensation has caused you to ascend the throne of your father’s kingdom, we invoke divine mercy for the grace bestowed upon you, before the passion and resurrection of God and our Lord Jesus Christ, that the same God and our Lord may graciously prolong and protect your life, and after the end of this life grant you eternal life.

Because we know that under your protection Christ’s poor live and flourish in peace, we earnestly beseech your sublimity on behalf of our poor leprous sons, who are perpetually confined outside the walls of Jerusalem by their illness and condemned to imprisonment. Of their torment and burning anguish we cannot say as much as you have seen with your own eyes.

We commend to you the bearer of this letter, a brother of those same poor, whom they send to your excellence in their need. Having heard him, deign, as seems right to you and as God inspires you, to come to the aid of those who are wholly deprived of human sight and human joy, so that for this and for other benefits you may deserve to receive from God, the rewarder of all good things, both victory in the present and, after completing the administration of your temporal kingdom, a share in eternal blessedness.

For in that place there flows together from different parts of the world a multitude of the sick and poor of God. Since many things are necessary to sustain their miserable and needy life, and since they plainly lack the assistance of many, the Eastern Church, oppressed by many tribulations and incursions of pagans, cannot provide for their needs in full. Therefore we make all their benefactors participants and sharers in all your prayers and benefits, especially those which are performed in the holy city of Jerusalem and which will henceforth be performed there.

### V. OF THE SAME

A., by the grace of God patriarch of the Church of the Holy Resurrection, to his dearest son in Christ Louis, by the same grace victorious and illustrious king of Gaul, sends greetings from him who grants salvation to kings.

The sincere love of true charity with which we embrace you, and the dutiful concern of the patriarchal office incumbent upon us, compel and admonish us to provide for our churches and, insofar as we are able according to God, to watch over the advancement and welfare of all Christendom. For, placed in the midst of a wicked and perverse nation, we are attacked almost every day by the tyranny of unbelievers and endure the constant ambushes and dangers of the enemies of the Christian name. Therefore, the greater and nearer the dangers that threaten us, the more it is fitting that we be prudent and solicitous, and seek counsel and aid from those who possess abundance, know how to bestow it, and are accustomed to give.

We have, moreover, within the boundaries of our patriarchate, in the city of Paneas, which is called Belinas, a church renowned both for its venerable antiquity and for the many and great miracles by which it has been adorned and exalted. This church was formerly founded in that place of Caesarea Philippi where Christ, the Son of the living God, was first and uniquely preached and most manifestly proclaimed by Peter, the chief of the apostles, through the confession of right faith, when above all and on behalf of all he declared: “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16). In that same place he was also deemed worthy to hear from the Lord’s mouth the reward of this blessed confession, when he said to him: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church” (ibid., 18), and to receive the keys of the kingdom of heaven and the power of binding and loosing.

This church, therefore, once so illustrious and worthy of every reverence and service, has now been almost completely overthrown by the Turks, enemies of the Christian name. And, because our sins have demanded it, that once-famous and glorious city, recognized as the bulwark and outwork of our Jerusalem for all the faithful, now retains only an empty name. It lies on the border of the foulest paganism, has been attacked by its barbarous savagery, and, through the constant captivity and death of its children, has been deprived of its best inhabitants; diminished almost every day, it is in peril.

Most recently, in our own times, God stirred up the spirit of his servant, the venerable brother I., newly ordained and appointed bishop in that same city. Wishing to restore this church to its former condition, and having expended much bodily labor and much of his own property, he made his way through various dangers by sea and land and at last came to your charitable knees, so that he might make known to you the calamity and poverty of so great and most venerable a church, and show you the concessions and relaxations which, with the counsel of our venerable brothers the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and priors, we have made for the relief of so great a church.

Therefore we humbly and earnestly beseech your royal majesty, by our continual prayers, to receive and honor graciously our venerable brother, the bishop of the aforesaid city, whose honesty and integrity sufficiently commend him, for the sake of God’s grace and out of reverence for us; and mercifully to hear him in his just petitions. Farewell.

## VI. Of R[AYMOND], duke of Narbonne, count of Toulouse, marquis of Provence

To his lord Louis, by the grace of God king of the Franks, R., duke of Narbonne, count of Toulouse, and marquis of Provence, the service of due fidelity.

Regarding the matter over which the envoys of the emperor of Constantinople, together with ours, as we believe, came to an agreement with us for the honor of your kingdom, we have sent our envoys, together with the envoys of Lord A., the supreme pontiff, to the emperor of the Greeks. Then it seemed fitting to our judgment to summon our envoys from their journey to your presence. Since in all things we have set the prudence of your counsel before us as our guide, and, following your authority, have bound ourselves to the envoys of the Greeks, we once again beg your royal excellence—for it would now be too late to repent—to send such envoys to the emperor of Constantinople that, by God’s favor, the hoped-for matter may be brought to completion for the glory and security of your kingdom, and the desired advantages may come to us.

For through the intervention and insistence of discreet and faithful envoys, great and difficult affairs are accustomed to attain a desired and prosperous end. Farewell.

## VII. R. de Balneo, faithful servant of the emperor of Constantinople

To Louis, by the grace of God most excellent king of the Franks, R. de Balneo, one of the faithful servants of Lord E[MMANUEL], ever-august emperor of Constantinople, the service of sincere fidelity.
